 "new_content": "import express from 'express';\nimport dotenv from 'dotenv';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\n\ndotenv.config();\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst app = express();\nconst PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;\n\napp.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }));\n\n// AI access via the Gemini REST API.\n// The @google/genai SDK misclassifies Google's newer \"AQ.\" authentication keys\n// as OAuth access tokens and returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, while\n// the same key authenticates correctly over REST. const resp = await fetch(url, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: {\n        'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n        'x-goog-api-key': apiKey,\n      },\n      body:  "new_content": "import express from 'express';\nimport dotenv from 'dotenv';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\n\ndotenv.config();\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst app = express();\nconst PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;\n\napp.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }));\n\n// AI access via the Gemini REST API.\n// The @google/genai SDK misclassifies Google's newer \"AQ.\" authentication keys\n// as OAuth access tokens and returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, while\n// the same key authenticates correctly over REST. (.env is gitignored.)\\n'\n  );\n}\n\nclass GeminiRequestError extends Error {\n  status: number;\n  constructor(status: number, message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n// Preferred text models, tried in order. (systemInstruction) payload.systemInstruction = { parts: [{ text: systemInstruction }] };\n    }\n\n    const candidates = modelCandidates(model);\n    let lastError: GeminiRequestError | null = null;\n    for (let i = 0; i < candidates.length; i++) {\n      const resp = await fetch(`${GEMINI_BASE_URL}/models/${candidates[i]}:generateContent`, {\n        method: 'POST',\n        headers: {\n          'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n          'x-goog-api-key': apiKey,\n        },\n        body: JSON.stringify(payload),\n      });\n      const json: any = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));\n      if (resp.ok) return json;\n\n      const status = resp.status;\n      lastError = new GeminiRequestError(\n        status,\n        json?.error?.message || `Gemini request failed (HTTP ${status})`\n      );\n      // Only transient availability/quota problems justify trying another model.\n      const retryable = status === 503 || status === 429 || status === 500;\n      if (!retryable || i === candidates.length - 1) throw lastError;\n      console.warn(\n        `[gemini] ${candidates[i]} unavailable (HTTP ${status}); falling back to ${candidates[i + 1]}`\n      );\n    }\n    throw lastError ?? new GeminiRequestError(500, 'Gemini request failed');\n  },\n};\n\n/** Extract plain text from a generateContent response. */\nfunction geminiText(response: any): string {\n  const parts = response?.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts;\n  if (!Array.isArray(parts)) return '';\n  return parts\n    .map((p: any) => (typeof p?.text === 'string' ? p.text : ''))\n    .join('')\n    .trim();\n}\n\n// Quota & Rate Limit Protection (Circuit breaker for 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)\nlet globalQuotaCooldownUntil = 0;\n\nfunction isQuotaExhaustedError(err: any): boolean {\n  if (!err) return false;\n  const status = err.status || err.code;\n  const msg = String(err.message || err).toLowerCase();\n  return (\n    status === 429 ||\n    msg.includes('429') ||\n const lowerUserMsg = lastUserMsg.toLowerCase();\n\n    // Specific intent detection for Phase 3\n    const isDontUnderstand =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('مش فاهم') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('مش فاهمة') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes(\"don't understand\") ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('dont understand') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes(\"don't get it\");\n\n    const isExplainDifferently =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اشرح بطريقة تانية') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('طريقة تانية') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اشرح تاني') ||\n (isDontUnderstand) {\n        fallbackReply = isArabic\n          ? `ولا يهمك خالص يا ${studentName}! عادي جداً متفهمش من أول مرة، دي خطوة طبيعية في التعلم. قولي إيه أكثر نقطة حسيتها ملخبطة وهنبسطها ### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `9a48cfee-e453-4125-b0ba-79d060c4d290` — 2026-10-21T16:27:48.338053

```
Done — **Nour is live.** Here's the full report.

## The API key: registered and working

Your key is now in a gitignored `.env` (mode 600, confirmed ignored). `/api/health` returns `hasApiKey:true, apiKeySource:"GEMINI_API_KEY"`.

**But detection wasn't enough — your key exposed a real bug I had to fix.** Your `AQ.`-prefixed key is Google's newer auth-key format. The `@google/genai` SDK **misreads `AQ.` keys as OAuth tokens** and returns `403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`, while the same key authenticates fine over REST. I proved it:

| Key | SDK result |
|---|---|
| `AIza...` (fake) | `400 API key not valid` (correct behavior) |
| Your `AQ.` key | `403 insufficient authentication scopes` (**wrong**) |

Same key over REST: **HTTP 200, 50 models listed.**

**Fix:** I replaced the SDK with a direct REST client (`server.ts`) that sends the key in the `x-goog-api-key` header — works for both `AIza` and `AQ.` formats. This was unavoidable: with the SDK, your key would never have worked.

Then I hit two more issues and fixed them:
- REST needs options nested under `generationConfig` (was flattened) → payload now shaped correctly.
- `gemini-3.8-flash` (the default) was returning **503 overloaded** → added automatic model fallback (`gemini-2.5-flash` → `gemini-3.5-flash`) and changed the default to a working model.

## Verified live (real calls, not mocks)

| Feature | Result |
|---|---|
| `/api/chat` | ✅ `source: gemini`, Arabic reply |
| `/api/tutor-explain` | ✅ warm Egyptian Arabic explanation of «تواصل» |
| `/api/tutor-reply` | ✅ Torta-fraction analogy for «الكسور» |
| `/api/tts` (voice) | ✅ 105 KB real audio |
| `/api/check-homework` | ✅ `source: gemini_vision`, graded correctly |
| `/api/health` | ✅ `hasApiKey:true` |

Nour now sounds right — age-appropriate, no scolding, grounded in the lesson.

## Other bugs found and fixed

1. **Work host blocked** by Vite → added `allowedHosts`.
2. **Nour couldn't reference resources** (display-only) → now injected into the tutor prompt with a no-invention rule.
3. **"Open book" led nowhere** → now links to the real Egyptian Knowledge Bank (`ekb.eg`, verified official).
4. **Silent missing-key failure** → loud startup diagnostic.
5. **Fabricated links impossible** → whitelist + tests E.9–E.11.

## Two findings worth your attention (not bugs, but decisions)

- **`CompanionChatScreen.tsx` is dead code** — never rendered. Its prompt says "I am NOT Nour," but no child ever sees it. Harmless now; should be deleted or wired up deliberately.
- **The Feed is genuinely good.** I verified it in the browser: full-screen swipeable reels with *real* lessons («أنا أستطيع», «الجملة الاسمية وركناها»), Nour character, and "اتعلمي مع نور" launch. This satisfies the doc's Feed acceptance test — it is not a placeholder.
- **Timetable is honest**: demo schedules are labeled with a demo badge, never passed off as real.

## Verification
No TS errors · 39 + 145 tests pass · build ✓ · `.env` gitignored · nothing committed.

## Still blocking "sellable" (unchanged)

The curriculum is still a **partial skeleton — 36 lessons across 9 subjects**, not the full books. That's the one thing I cannot fix with code; it needs real textbook content from you. Linking gets the student to the book, but Nour can't *teach* content that isn't ingested.

I also wrote `AGENTS.md` documenting the REST-vs-SDK key issue so this never bites again.

**Your move:** (a) should I delete the dead `CompanionChatScreen`/`/api/chat`? (b) do you want the content-ingestion loader built now so real books drop straight in? (c) anything else you want me to hunt for while I'm in here?
```

entries.append({'kind': kind, 'raw': ln, 'title': title,\n                            'tocPage': i + 1,\n                            'bookPage': int(pg.group(1)) if pg else None})\n    return im.save(b, 'JPEG', quality=85)\n        scanned += 1\n        try:\n            out = vision(base64.b64encode(b.getvalue()).decode(), TOC_PROMPT)\n            j = json.loads(out)\n            if j.get('units'): found = j['units']\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n    d.close()\n    return found, scanned\n\ndef convert(pdf, bid, subject, lang, term, do_structure=True):\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf)\n    bdir = os.path.join(OUT, bid); pdir = os.path.join(bdir, 'pages')\n    os.makedirs(pdir, exist_ok=True)\n    m = {'id': bid, 'subject': subject, 'language': lang, 'term': term,\n         'source': os.path.basename(pdf), 'pages': doc.page_count,\n         'width': WIDTH, 'quality': QUALITY, 'index': []}\n    total = 0\n    for i in range(doc.page_count):\n        im = render(doc[i])\n        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, 'WEBP', quality=QUALITY, method=6)\n        data = b.getvalue(); total += len(data)\n        fn = f'{i+1:04d}.webp'\n        open(os.path.join(pdir, fn), 'wb').write(data)\n        m['index'].append({'p': i+1, 'f': fn, 'w': im.width, 'h': im.height,\n                           'kb': round(len(data)/1024)})\n    m['bytes'] = total\n    if do_structure:\n        units, scanned = extract_structure(pdf, lang)\n        m['units'] = units; m['tocScanned'] = scanned\n    doc.close()\n    json.dump(m, open(os.path.join(bdir,'manifest.json'),'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)\n    return m\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    import sys\n    only = sys.argv[1:] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None\n    for pdf, bid, subj, lang, term in STUDENT_BOOKS:\n        if only and bid not in only: continue\n        if not os.path.exists(f'pdfs/{pdf}'):\n            print(f'MISSING {pdf}', flush=True); continue\n        try:\n            m = convert(f'pdfs/{pdf}', bid, subj, lang, term)\n            print(f\"{bid:22s} {m['pages']:4d}p {m['bytes']/1024/1024:6.1f}MB \"\n                  f\"units={len(m.get('units',[]))}\", flush=True)\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f'{bid} FAILED {e}', flush=True)\n    print('PIPELINE DONE', flush=True)\nPY\necho \"pipeline ready\"; ### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `f3c34c92-129a-4600-921a-9423cccffc26` — 2026-10-21T16:57:35.463971

```
Noted in memory so this survives future sessions.

While those run, here's my read on what we've actually established — and the open question I think you should weigh in on:

## What's proven

Your instinct was right: I could get everything myself, and it's better than I expected. The vision-based structure extraction is the real unlock — that `المحور الأول → الوحدة الأولى → الدرس الأول: موقع بلدي → p.8` chain is exactly what turns Nour from "a chatbot that talks about school" into "a teacher who knows this specific book."

## The honest gap I keep coming back to

**French Math and Science.** I can't find them, and I don't think they're findable publicly — Girard's French-track editions are almost certainly licensed from a French publisher. So there's a fork in the road:

- **Option A:** Ship with Arabic/English books as the spine, and mark French-track lessons as "awaiting school materials." Nour teaches the *concepts* (decimals, the water cycle) in French while the reference book is the EN/Arabic edition. Honest, works today, but the page links don't match her actual book.
- **Option B:** Hold the French subjects until you get the school's books, and launch with the Arabic/English subjects fully wired.

I'd lean **A** — a student can learn decimals in French regardless of which book illustrates them, and the concept mapping is genuinely useful. But you know her school; maybe they'd hand over the PDFs.

## Also worth deciding

**Where should these ~300 MB of books actually live?** Right now they're local files. For a real app you'd want them on object storage / a CDN with the manifests served as JSON. That's a straightforward change to how the reader loads pages, but it's a hosting decision (Vercel Blob, S3, Cloudflare R2), so it's yours to make.

What's on your mind — one of those, or something else?
```

## The constraint

A full Grade 5 library is **~270 MB** (all 24 student books, ~3,000 pages). That's too big to shove onto a child's device at install — and most of it is for the *other* term, or subjects she won't touch today.

## What I recommend: staged downloads

| Stage | What | Size | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0 — Install** | App shell + Nour + Feed | **~3 MB** | Instant, at "Add to Home Screen" |
| **1 — First run** | Her **current-term core** (Arabic, Math, Science, Social, English) | **~85 MB** | One progress bar, with WiFi warning |
| **2 — On demand** | Per-book: tap → downloads that subject | ~10–20 MB each | Only when she opens it |
| **3 — Never on device** | Teacher guides & frameworks | ~15 MB | Stays **server-side** — Nour's knowledge |

**Stage 3 is the important one.** The teacher material isn't for the child to read — it's what makes Nour teach well. Keeping it on the server means it costs the child **zero** storage, and Nour can still quote the teacher guide and the CCIMD framework when explaining.

## Why this fits what you already have

The service worker in `public/sw.js` is already built on exactly the right principle — I read it:

> *"It never caches /api/*. AI answers must be live or honestly degraded; a cached answer presented as fresh would be the exact lying this project is removing."*

Books offline are the same idea: **static pages can be cached honestly; AI answers must stay live or be labeled offline.** So I'd extend `sw.js` with a `amina-books-v1` cache, populated by explicit downloads — not by silent caching.

Now I have the full engineering picture. Let me summarize the engineering audit for an installable app:

**What's RIGHT:**
1. No API key on client — server proxies all AI. ✅
2. SW never caches /api/ — live-or-degrade principle. ✅
3. Hashed assets cache-first (immutable). ✅
4. SW registered prod-only, non-fatal, BASE_URL-aware (works on subpath). ✅
5. Manifest with maskable icons, standalone, RTL/ar. ✅
6. Navigations network-first with shell fallback. ✅

**What's MISSING/WRONG for an installable app:**
1. **No `navigator.storage.persist()`** — books can be evicted. CRITICAL for 300MB.
2. **No book caching in SW** — books aren't handled by the SW at all; no offline books.
3. **No update flow** — SW calls skipWaiting() immediately, which can swap the app under a running session. For a kid mid-lesson, that's disruptive. Standard practice: prompt "update available, reload?" There's `self.skipWaiting()` on install — that force-updates. Actually for this app that's arguably fine (fresh content), but combined with no user prompt it can cause a mid-session reload. Need to handle.

Key answer content:
- Why not raw PDFs from Drive:
  1. **5 GB**, not 300 MB. And a single book is 150–207 MB vs 12–33 MB light. On a child's phone, tapping "Math" to wait for a 207 MB download isn't acceptable; 15-25 MB is.
  2. **They're not ours.** Ministry books are copyrighted/CCIMD. edu2-egypt is an unofficial rehost. Shipping direct links into an installed app launders the hosting through a third party who can delete/revoke, and makes us redistribute unlicensed copies. Light rendering is derivative but intended for the student's own use — still needs a licensing decision, but it isn't us hosting 5 GB of ministry PDFs.
  3. **Fragile & slow.** Drive links break/expire/rate-limit; a >100 MB file hits the virus-scan interstitial (we proved that), which a device fetch may not handle. Latency from Drive to a phone in Egypt is unpredictable.
  4. **Offline.** The promise is "install and it's there offline." Depending on Drive at read time breaks that.
  5. **Control.** We need per-page URLs for deep links ("open lesson 3, page 12"), prefetch, offline caching. Can't do that with one opaque 207 MB file.
- What we could do without re-rendering: serve our OWN copies of the page images derived from the PDFs. The rendering IS skipping the "reproduce" work — it's just rasterize+compress, ~1 min/book.
- The parts that CAN be skipped: the heavy vision PDF pipeline. The 51 lessons in the app have page numbers already.
- Recommendation: ship light pages (~300 MB, on-demand per book), page-accurate, offline-capable, and link to the official source for provenance. Don't raw-link From Drive.

2. Drive rate-limits — I got 429s today. That's *my* requests; 50 kids all opening the app at 8am would be worse. That's when I'd own the Salesforce-style tarball-on-a-bucket.
3. Links die quietly — a Drive folder gets moved or permission flipped and the app 404s with no fallback.
4. Kids' phones can't render a raw 207MB PDF well — iOS Safari in an iframe is bad at large PDFs, no offline cache of the file, and it looks like a scanned government PDF, not a product.
5. "Pretty, on our own terms" is literally impossible with a raw PDF — it's a fixed black-box. With baked pages, we control size, quality, RTL layout, zoom, and can add captions/targets.

Then the design that honors the intent:
- Keep the links (I saved source-links.json) — provenance + re-fetch forever.
- Bake once server-side.
- Client downloads only what's needed, on demand: one book = 33 MB, fetched "instantly" as you said.
- Hybrid option if you want: serve both — the pretty reader by default, "تحميل PDF الأصلي" link for parents.

Then the current status + ETA.

Let me write it.

Also let me check pipeline progress to report.

 "new_content": "import express from 'express';\nimport dotenv from 'dotenv';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\n\ndotenv.config();\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst app = express();\nconst PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;\n\napp.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }));\n\n// AI access via the Gemini REST API.\n// The @google/genai SDK misclassifies Google's newer \"AQ.\" authentication keys\n// as OAuth access tokens and returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, while\n// the same key authenticates correctly over REST. (systemInstruction) payload.systemInstruction = { parts: [{ text: systemInstruction }] };\n    }\n\n    const candidates = modelCandidates(model);\n    let lastError: GeminiRequestError | null =         'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n          'x-goog-api-key': apiKey,\n        },\n        body: JSON.stringify(payload),\n      });\n      const json: any = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));\n      if (resp.ok) return json;\n\n      const status = resp.status;\n      lastError = new GeminiRequestError(\n        status,\n        json?.error?.message || `Gemini request failed (HTTP ${status})`\n      );\n      // Only transient availability/quota problems justify trying another model.\n      const retryable = status === 503 || status === 429 || status === 500;\n      if (!retryable || i === candidates.length - 1) throw lastError;\n      console.warn(\n        `[gemini] ${candidates[i]} unavailable (HTTP ${status}); falling back to ${candidates[i + 1]}`\n      );\n    }\n    throw lastError ?? new GeminiRequestError(500, 'Gemini request failed');\n  },\n};\n\n/** Extract plain text from a generateContent response. */\nfunction geminiText(response: any): string {\n  const parts = response?.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts;\n  if (!Array.isArray(parts)) return '';\n  return parts\n    .map((p: any) => (typeof p?.text === 'string' ? p.text : ''))\n    .join('')\n    .trim();\n}\n\n// Quota & Rate Limit Protection (Circuit breaker for 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)\nlet globalQuotaCooldownUntil = 0;\n\nfunction isQuotaExhaustedError(err: any): boolean {\n  if (!err) const lowerUserMsg = lastUserMsg.toLowerCase();\n\n    // Specific intent detection for Phase 3\n    const isDontUnderstand =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('مش فاهم') ||\n const isExplainDifferently =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اشرح بطريقة تانية') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('طريقة تانية') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اشرح تاني') ||\n (isDontUnderstand) {\n        fallbackReply = isArabic\n          ? `ولا يهمك خالص يا ${studentName}! عادي جداً متفهمش من أول مرة، دي خطوة طبيعية في التعلم. قولي إيه أكثر نقطة حسيتها ملخبطة وهنبسطها Ready for a quick, friendly question on what we discussed? I am your AI School Companion.  "file_text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * On-demand curriculum downloads.\n *\n * Books are not bundled with the app. The shell installs small, and the device\n * fetches a book the first time it is opened, then keeps it offline. Page files\n * are content-stable and served immutable, so the browser's HTTP cache makes\n * every later open free.\n *\n * Nothing here fabricates content. If a book cannot be fetched, the reader is\n * told it is unavailable rather than shown a substitute.\n */\n\nexport interface BookSummary {\n  id: string;\n  subject: string;\n  language: string;\n  term: number;\n  pages: number;\n  bytes: number;\n  width: number;\n  units: number;\n}\n\nexport interface BookPage {\n  p: number;\n  f: string;\n  w: number;\n  h: number;\n  kb: number;\n}\n\nexport interface BookManifest extends BookSummary {\n  source: string;\n  index: BookPage[];\n  units?: Array<{ unit: string; lessons: Array<{ title: string; page: number | null }> }>;\n}\n\nconst API = '/api/curriculum';\n\nasync function json<T>(url: string): Promise<T> {\n  const res = await fetch(url);\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n  return res.json() as Promise<T>;\n}\n\n/** List every book the server can serve. */\nexport function listBooks(): Promise<BookSummary[]> {\n  return json<{ books: BookSummary[] }>(`${API}/index`).then((r) => r.books);\n}\n\n/** Fetch one book's manifest (page list + unit/lesson structure). */\nexport function getBookManifest(bookId: string): Promise<BookManifest> {\n  return json<BookManifest>(`${API}/${bookId}/manifest`);\n}\n\n/** URL for a single page image. Immutable, so safe to cache forever. */\nexport function pageUrl(bookId: string, file: string): string {\n  return `${API}/${bookId}/pages/${file}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Ask the browser to keep the app's storage. Without this an installed app's\n * downloaded books are \"best effort\": the OS may evict them under pressure.\n * Returns whether storage is now persistent.\n */\nexport async function requestPersistentStorage(): Promise<boolean> {\n  if (!navigator.storage?.persist) return false;\n  try {\n    if (await navigator.storage.persisted?.()) return true;\n    return await navigator.storage.persist();\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface StorageStatus {\n  usageBytes: number;\n  quotaBytes: number;\n  persisted: boolean;\n}\n\nexport async function storageStatus(): Promise<StorageStatus | null> {\n  if (!navigator.storage?.estimate) return null;\n  try {\n    const est = await navigator.storage.estimate();\n    return {\n      usageBytes: est.usage ?? 0,\n      quotaBytes: est.quota ?? 0,\n      persisted: (await navigator.storage.persisted?.()) ?? false,\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface DownloadProgress {\n  loaded: number;\n  total: number;\n  page: number;\n  pages: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Download every page of a book into the HTTP cache, reporting progress.\n * Sequential rather than parallel: a child's phone on school WiFi should not\n * open thirty sockets at once, and progress is more honest one page at a time.\n */\nexport async function downloadBook(\n  manifest: BookManifest,\n  onProgress?: (p: DownloadProgress) => void,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; failedPage?: number }> {\n  await requestPersistentStorage();\n  const total = manifest.index.length;\n  let loaded = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {\n    const page = manifest.index[i];\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(pageUrl(manifest.id, page.f), { cache: 'force-cache' });\n      if (!res.ok) return { ok: false, failedPage: page.p };\n      // Read the body so it lands in the cache.\n      await res.blob();\n    } catch {\n      return { ok: false, failedPage: page.p };\n    }\n    loaded += page.kb * 1024;\n    onProgress?.({ loaded, total: manifest.bytes, page: i + 1, pages: total });\n  }\n  return { ok: true };\n}\n\nconst KEY = 'amina.downloadedBooks.v1';\n\n/** Book ids the device has finished downloading. */\nexport function downloadedBookIds(): string[] {\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]') as string[];\n  } catch {\n    return [];\n  }\n}\n\nexport function markDownloaded(bookId: string): void {\n  const ids = new Set(downloadedBookIds());\n  ids.add(bookId);\n  localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify([...ids]));\n}\n",

 "new_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * On-demand curriculum downloads.\n *\n * Books are not bundled with the app. The shell installs small, and the device\n * fetches a book the first time it is opened, then keeps it offline. Page files\n * are content-stable and served immutable, so the browser's HTTP cache makes\n * every later open free.\n *\n * Nothing here fabricates content. If a book cannot be fetched, the reader is\n * told it is unavailable rather than shown a substitute.\n */\n\nexport interface BookSummary {\n  id: string;\n  subject: string;\n  language: string;\n  term: number;\n  pages: number;\n  bytes: number;\n  width: number;\n  units: number;\n}\n\nexport interface BookPage {\n  p: number;\n  f: string;\n  w: number;\n  h: number;\n  kb: number;\n}\n\nexport interface BookManifest extends BookSummary {\n  source: string;\n  index: BookPage[];\n  units?: Array<{ unit: string; lessons: Array<{ title: string; page: number | null }> }>;\n}\n\nconst API = '/api/curriculum';\n\nasync function json<T>(url: string): Promise<T> {\n  const res = await fetch(url);\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n  return res.json() as Promise<T>;\n}\n\n/** List every book the server can serve. */\nexport function listBooks(): Promise<BookSummary[]> {\n  return json<{ books: BookSummary[] }>(`${API}/index`).then((r) => r.books);\n}\n\n/** Fetch one book's manifest (page list + unit/lesson structure). */\nexport function getBookManifest(bookId: string): Promise<BookManifest> {\n  return json<BookManifest>(`${API}/${bookId}/manifest`);\n}\n\n/** URL for a single page image. Immutable, so safe to cache forever. */\nexport function pageUrl(bookId: string, file: string): string {\n  return `${API}/${bookId}/pages/${file}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Ask the browser to keep the app's storage. Without this an installed app's\n * downloaded books are \"best effort\": the OS may evict them under pressure.\n * Returns whether storage is now persistent.\n */\nexport async function requestPersistentStorage(): Promise<boolean> {\n  if (!navigator.storage?.persist) return false;\n  try {\n    if (await navigator.storage.persisted?.()) return true;\n    return await navigator.storage.persist();\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface StorageStatus {\n  usageBytes: number;\n  quotaBytes: number;\n  persisted: boolean;\n}\n\nexport async function storageStatus(): Promise<StorageStatus | null> {\n  if (!navigator.storage?.estimate) return null;\n  try {\n    const est = await navigator.storage.estimate();\n    return {\n      usageBytes: est.usage ?? 0,\n      quotaBytes: est.quota ?? 0,\n      persisted: (await navigator.storage.persisted?.()) ?? false,\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface DownloadProgress {\n  loaded: number;\n  total: number;\n  page: number;\n  pages: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Download every page of a book into the HTTP cache, reporting progress.\n * Sequential rather than parallel: a child's phone on school WiFi should not\n * open thirty sockets at once, and progress is more honest one page at a time.\n */\nexport async function downloadBook(\n  manifest: BookManifest,\n  onProgress?: (p: DownloadProgress) => void,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; failedPage?: number }> {\n  await requestPersistentStorage();\n  const total = manifest.index.length;\n  let loaded = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {\n    const page = manifest.index[i];\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(pageUrl(manifest.id, page.f), { cache: 'force-cache' });\n      if (!res.ok) return { ok: false, failedPage: page.p };\n      // Read the body so it lands in the cache.\n      await res.blob();\n    } catch {\n      return { ok: false, failedPage: page.p };\n    }\n    loaded += page.kb * 1024;\n    onProgress?.({ loaded, total: manifest.bytes, page: i + 1, pages: total });\n  }\n  return { ok: true };\n}\n\nconst KEY = 'amina.downloadedBooks.v1';\n\n/** Book ids the device has finished downloading. */\nexport function downloadedBookIds(): string[] {\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]') as string[];\n  } catch {\n    return [];\n  }\n}\n\nexport function markDownloaded(bookId: string): void {\n  const ids = new Set(downloadedBookIds());\n  ids.add(bookId);\n  localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify([...ids]));\n}\n",

In \"${lessonTitle}\", your insight brings us closer to mastering the exercise!`;\n      }\n      return res.json({ reply: contextualReply });\n    }\n\n    const systemInstruction = `\nYou are \"نور\" (Nour), an inspiring, loving, warm, enthusiastic, highly skilled private tutor talking to a ${studentName}, an 11-year-old 5th-grade student in Egypt.\nCURRENT SUBJECT: \"${subjectName}\".\nCURRENT LESSON: \"${lessonTitle}\".\nCURRICULUM CONTEXT / TEXTBOOK TEXT:\n\"\"\"${currentBeatText ? currentBeatText.slice(0, 1000) : 'Grade 5 Egyptian Ministry Curriculum.'}\"\"\"\n\nRULES:\n1. In \"${req.body?.lessonTitle || 'our lesson'}\", the main point is to stay curious and focused.`,\n    });\n  }\n});\n\n// Photo & Digital Homework Check API endpoint (Phase 6)\napp.post('/api/check-homework', async (req, res) => {\n  try {\n    const {\n      imageBase64,\n      mimeType = 'image/jpeg',\n      questionPrompt = '',\n      expectedAnswer = '',\n      rubric = '',\n      language = 'ar',\n      grade = 'Grade 5',\n      subject = '',\n    } = req.body;\n\n    const isArabic = language === 'ar';\n\n    if (!imageBase64 && !req.body.studentAnswerText) {\n      return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Missing image or text payload' });\n    }\n\n    if (!apiKey || Date.now() < globalQuotaCooldownUntil) {\n      // Never grade without the model. Tell the client we are degraded.\n      return res.json({\n        extractedAnswerText: null,\n        extractionConfidence: 0,\n        evaluation: 'unclear',\n        mistakeDescription: isArabic\n          ? 'مش قادرة أصحّح الواجب دلوقتي. وريه لحد من أهلك أو لمعلمتك.'\n          : \"I can't check this right now. 'Arabic (Egypt/Standard)' : 'English'}.\nSubject: \"${subject}\".\nQuestion Prompt: \"${questionPrompt}\".\nExpected Answer / Rubric: \"${expectedAnswer || rubric}\".\n\nYOUR TASK:\n1. If legible (extractionConfidence >= 0.5):\n   - Evaluate correctness against the expected answer/rubric: 'correct' | 'partial' | 'wrong' | 'unclear'.\n   - If wrong or partial, identify the specific mistake in a gentle, warm tone in \"mistakeDescription\".\n   - Provide a partial hint / worked step (\"workedStep\") to guide them without revealing the full answer.\n   - Set \"finalAnswer\" to the correct target answer.\n5. SEPARATION OF ACADEMIC CORRECTNESS VS HANDWRITING QUALITY:\n   - If the student's concept, calculation, or fact is right, assign evaluation = \"correct\", EVEN IF the handwriting is messy or uneven!\n   - Separately evaluate \"handwritingQuality\": \"neat\" | \"readable\" | \"messy\" | \"unclear\".\n   - In \"handwritingFeedback\", provide gentle, friendly handwriting advice (e.g. \"حلك الرياضي صحيح ١٠٠٪! نصيحة لتحسين الخط: باعدي قليلاً بين الأرقام\").\n6. Return JSON ONLY matching this exact schema:\n{\n  \"extractedAnswerText\": string | null,\n  \"extractionConfidence\": number (between 0.0 and 1.0),\n  \"evaluation\": \"correct\" | \"partial\" | \"wrong\" | \"unclear\",\n  \"mistakeDescription\": string | null,\n  \"workedStep\": string | null,\n  \"finalAnswer\": string | null,\n  \"handwritingQuality\": \"neat\" | \"readable\" | \"messy\" | \"unclear\",\n  \"handwritingFeedback\": string | null\n}\n`.trim();\n\n    const studentAnswerText =\n      typeof req.body.studentAnswerText === 'string'\n        ? req.body.studentAnswerText.replace(/[\\u0000-\\u001F\\u007F]/g, ' ').slice(0, 2000)\n        : '';\n    const parts: any[] = [];\n    if (cleanBase64) {\n      parts.push({\n        inlineData: {\n          mimeType,\n          data: cleanBase64,\n        },\n      });\n    }\n    parts.push({\n      text:\n        `Please evaluate the student's answer for prompt: \"${questionPrompt}\". 'الطالب لم يتذكر أحداث اليوم أو اختصر بالنسيان.' : 'Student did not recall details or stated amnesia.',\n        isSilence: true,\n        isVague: false,\n        detectedConfidence: 'vague',\n        source: 'rule_detection',\n      });\n    }\n\n    if (isVague) {\n      return res.json({\n        lessonsCovered: [],\n        homeworkAssigned: [],\n        notes: trimmedInput,\n        isSilence: false,\n        isVague: true,\n        detectedConfidence: 'vague',\n        source: 'rule_detection',\n      });\n    }\n\n    if (!apiKey || Date.now() < globalQuotaCooldownUntil) {\n      // Local rule-based parser fallback\n      const lessons: { subject: string; topic?: string; notes?: string }[] = [];\n      const homework: { subject: string; description: string; dueDate?: string }[] = [];\n\n      if (lower.includes('فرنساوي') || lower.includes('french') || lower.includes('français')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'اللغة الفرنسية' });\n        if (lower.includes('واجب') || lower.includes('homework') || lower.includes('devoir')) {\n          homework.push({ subject: 'اللغة الفرنسية', description: isArabic ? 'واجب (التفاصيل غير محددة)' : 'Homework (details not specified)' });\n        }\n      }\n      if (lower.includes('ساينس') || (lower.includes('sci') && lower.includes('fr')) || lower.includes('sciences')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'العلوم بالفرنسية (Sciences)' });\n      } else if (lower.includes('علوم') || lower.includes('science')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'العلوم' });\n      }\n      if (lower.includes('عرب') || lower.includes('arabic')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'اللغة العربية' });\n        if (lower.includes('واجب') || lower.includes('homework')) {\n          homework.push({ subject: 'اللغة العربية', description: isArabic ? Do not hallucinate or invent subjects that the student did not attend or mention.\n2. If the student explicitly names a subject not in the timetable, capture it accurately.\n3. Page filenames are content-stable, so they can be cached\n// immutably; the client downloads one book on demand and keeps it offline.\nconst CURRICULUM_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, 'content', 'curriculum');\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/index', (_req, res) => {\n  const dir = path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books');\n  fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }, (err, entries) => {\n    if (err) return res.status(503).json({ error: 'curriculum_unavailable' });\n    const books = [];\n    for (const e of entries) {\n      if (!e.isDirectory()) continue;\n      try {\n        const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, e.name, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8'));\n        books.push({\n          id: m.id, subject: m.subject, language: m.language, term: m.term,\n          pages: m.pages, bytes: m.bytes, width: m.width,\n          units: (m.units || []).length,\n        });\n      } catch { /* skip an unreadable book rather than fail the list */ }\n    }\n    res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-cache');\n    res.json({ books });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/manifest', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'manifest.json'), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'book_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/pages/:file', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId, file } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  if (!/^\\d{4}\\.webp$/.test(file)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_page' });\n  // Content is immutable per filename, so the device may cache it indefinitely.\n  res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable');\n  res.type('image/webp');\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'pages', file), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'page_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\n// Dev vs Prod server setup\nif (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {\n  const { createServer: createViteServer } = await import('vite');\n  const vite = await createViteServer({\n    server: { middlewareMode: true },\n    appType: 'spa',\n  });\n  app.use(vite.middlewares);\n} else {\n  app.use(express.static(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist')));\n  app.get('*', (_req, res) => {\n    res.sendFile(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist', 'index.html'));\n  });\n}\n\napp.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {\n  console.log(`AI School Companion Server running on http://0.0.0.0:${PORT}`);\n});\n",
 "new_content": "import express from 'express';\nimport dotenv from 'dotenv';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport fs from 'fs';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\n\ndotenv.config();\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst app = express();\nconst PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;\n\napp.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }));\n\n// AI access via the Gemini REST API.\n// The @google/genai SDK misclassifies Google's newer \"AQ.\" authentication keys\n// as OAuth access tokens and returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, while\n// the same key authenticates correctly over REST. We therefore call the REST API\n// directly with the key in the x-goog-api-key header, which works for both the\n// legacy \"AIza\" and the newer \"AQ.\" key formats.\nconst API_KEY_SOURCES = ['GEMINI_API_KEY', 'GOOGLE_API_KEY', 'GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY', 'API_KEY'] as const;\nconst apiKeySource = API_KEY_SOURCES.find((name) => Boolean(process.env[name])) ?? null;\nconst apiKey = apiKeySource ? process.env[apiKeySource] : undefined;\nconst GEMINI_BASE_URL = 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta';\n\nif (!apiKey) {\n  console.warn(\n    '\\n⚠️  NO AI API KEY DETECTED — Nour will run in local companion mode (no live model calls).\\n' +\n      '   To enable the live tutor, provide a Gemini API key as one of:\\n' +\n      `   ${API_KEY_SOURCES.join(', ')}\\n` +\n      '   Easiest local option: create a file named \".env\" in the project root containing\\n' +\n      '     GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key_here\\n' +\n      '   then restart the server. (.env is gitignored.)\\n'\n  );\n}\n\nclass GeminiRequestError extends Error {\n  status: number;\n  constructor(status: number, message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n// Preferred text models, tried in order. A model that is temporarily overloaded\n// (503) or rate-limited (429) falls through to the next, so a busy model never\n// takes the whole app down. Text-only: TTS/image models are never substituted.\nconst TEXT_MODEL_FALLBACKS = ['gemini-2.5-flash', 'gemini-3.5-flash'];\nconst DEFAULT_TEXT_MODEL = TEXT_MODEL_FALLBACKS[0];\n\n/** Resolve the model list to attempt for a request. */\nfunction modelCandidates(requested: string): string[] {\n  const isTextModel = !requested.includes('tts') && !requested.includes('image');\n  if (!isTextModel) return [requested];\n  const chain = [requested, ...TEXT_MODEL_FALLBACKS];\n  return [...new Set(chain)];\n}\n\n/**\n * Minimal REST client for the subset of Gemini the app uses (generateContent).\n * Kept intentionally small so the key travels in the header the API expects.\n */\nconst gemini = {\n  async generateContent(body: {\n    model: string;\n    contents: unknown;\n    config?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  }): Promise<any> {\n    if (!apiKey) throw new GeminiRequestError(401, 'No API key configured');\n    const { model, contents, config } = body;\n    const payload: Record<string, unknown> = { contents };\n    if (config) {\n      const { systemInstruction, ...generationConfig } = config as Record<string, unknown>;\n      // REST expects sampling/response options nested under generationConfig;\n      // only systemInstruction sits at the top level.\n      if (Object.keys(generationConfig).length > 0) payload.generationConfig = generationConfig;\n      if (systemInstruction) payload.systemInstruction = { parts: [{ text: systemInstruction }] };\n    }\n\n    const candidates = modelCandidates(model);\n    let lastError: GeminiRequestError | null = null;\n    for (let i = 0; i < candidates.length; i++) {\n      const resp = await fetch(`${GEMINI_BASE_URL}/models/${candidates[i]}:generateContent`, {\n        method: 'POST',\n        headers: {\n          'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n          'x-goog-api-key': apiKey,\n        },\n        body: JSON.stringify(payload),\n      });\n      const json: any = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));\n      if (resp.ok) return json;\n\n      const status = resp.status;\n      lastError = new GeminiRequestError(\n        status,\n        json?.error?.message || `Gemini request failed (HTTP ${status})`\n      );\n      // Only transient availability/quota problems justify trying another model.\n      const retryable = status === 503 || status === 429 || status === 500;\n      if (!retryable || i === candidates.length - 1) throw lastError;\n      console.warn(\n        `[gemini] ${candidates[i]} unavailable (HTTP ${status}); falling back to ${candidates[i + 1]}`\n      );\n    }\n    throw lastError ?? new GeminiRequestError(500, 'Gemini request failed');\n  },\n};\n\n/** Extract plain text from a generateContent response. */\nfunction geminiText(response: any): string {\n  const parts = response?.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts;\n  if (!Array.isArray(parts)) return '';\n  return parts\n    .map((p: any) => (typeof p?.text === 'string' ? p.text : ''))\n    .join('')\n    .trim();\n}\n\n// Quota & Rate Limit Protection (Circuit breaker for 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)\nlet globalQuotaCooldownUntil = 0;\n\nfunction isQuotaExhaustedError(err: any): boolean {\n  if (!err) return false;\n  const status = err.status || err.code;\n  const msg = String(err.message || err).toLowerCase();\n  return (\n    status === 429 ||\n    msg.includes('429') ||\n    msg.includes('resource_exhausted') ||\n    msg.includes('quota') ||\n    msg.includes('rate limit')\n  );\n}\n\nfunction handleAiError(scope: string, err: any) {\n  if (isQuotaExhaustedError(err)) {\n    // 10-minute cooldown where no external calls are made; graceful fallbacks are served\n    globalQuotaCooldownUntil = Date.now() + 10 * 60 * 1000;\n  } else {\n    console.warn(`[${scope}] handled  "file_text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * Book reader. Opens a real ministry textbook on the device: downloads it once\n * on demand, then reads it offline. Nothing here invents pages or content — if\n * a book is missing, it says so.\n */\n\nimport React, { useEffect, useRef, useState, useCallback } from 'react';\nimport { X, Download, ChevronLeft, ChevronRight, Loader2, WifiOff, BookOpen } from 'lucide-react';\nimport {\n  BookManifest,\n  pageUrl,\n  getBookManifest,\n  downloadBook,\n  markDownloaded,\n  downloadedBookIds,\n  requestPersistentStorage,\n  type DownloadProgress,\n} from '../../services/content/bookLibrary';\n\ninterface Props {\n  bookId: string;\n  language: 'ar' | 'en';\n  startPage?: number;\n  onClose: () => void;\n}\n\ntype State =\n  | { kind: 'loading' }\n  | { kind: 'error'; message: string }\n  | { kind: 'downloading'; progress: DownloadProgress }\n  | { kind: 'ready'; manifest: BookManifest; offline: boolean };\n\nconst T = {\n  ar: {\n    loading: 'جارٍ فتح الكتاب…',\n    download: 'تحميل الكتاب',\n    downloading: 'جارٍ التحميل',\n    ready: 'الكتاب متاح على جهازك',\n    offline: 'متاح بدون إنترنت',\n    missing: 'هذا الكتاب غير متاح بعد',\n    retry: 'إعادة المحاولة',\n    page: 'صفحة',\n    of: 'من',\n    close: 'إغلاق',\n  },\n  en: {\n    loading: 'Opening book…',\n    download: 'Download book',\n    downloading: 'Downloading',\n    ready: 'Saved on this device',\n    offline: 'Available offline',\n    missing: 'This book is not available yet',\n    retry: 'Try again',\n    page: 'Page',\n    of: 'of',\n    close: 'Close',\n  },\n};\n\nexport const BookReader: React.FC<Props> = ({ bookId, language, startPage = 1, onClose }) => {\n  const t = T[language] ?? T.en;\n  const [state, setState] = useState<State>({ kind: 'loading' });\n  const [page, setPage] = useState(startPage);\n  const [imgLoaded, setImgLoaded] = useState(false);\n  const scrollRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n\n  // Load the manifest. If the book was downloaded before, go straight to ready.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    (async () => {\n      try {\n        const manifest = await getBookManifest(bookId);\n        if (cancelled) return;\n        const already = downloadedBookIds().includes(bookId);\n        setState({ kind: 'ready', manifest, offline: already });\n      } catch {\n        if (!cancelled) setState({ kind: 'error', message: t.missing });\n      }\n    })();\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n  }, [bookId, t.missing]);\n\n  const startDownload = useCallback(async () => {\n    if (state.kind !== 'ready' && state.kind !== 'error') return;\n    let manifest: BookManifest;\n    try {\n      manifest = state.kind === 'ready' ? state.manifest : await getBookManifest(bookId);\n    } catch {\n      setState({ kind: 'error', message: t.missing });\n      return;\n    }\n    await requestPersistentStorage();\n    setState({ kind: 'downloading', progress: { loaded: 0, total: manifest.bytes, page: 0, pages: manifest.pages } });\n    const res = await downloadBook(manifest, (p) => setState({ kind: 'downloading', progress: p }));\n    if (res.ok) {\n      markDownloaded(bookId);\n      setState({ kind: 'ready', manifest, offline: true });\n    } else {\n      setState({ kind: 'error', message: t.missing });\n    }\n  }, [state, bookId, t.missing]);\n\n  // Reset the image fade whenever the page changes.\n  useEffect(() => setImgLoaded(false), [page]);\n\n  // Preload the next two pages so turning a page never stalls.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (state.kind !== 'ready') return;\n    for (const p of [page + 1, page + 2]) {\n      const entry = state.manifest.index.find((x) => x.p === p);\n      if (entry) new Image().src = pageUrl(bookId, entry.f);\n    }\n  }, [page, state, bookId]);\n\n  const totalPages = state.kind === 'ready' ? state.manifest.pages : 0;\n  const current = state.kind === 'ready' ? state.manifest.index.find((x) => x.p === page) : undefined;\n\n  const go = (delta: number) => setPage((p) => Math.min(totalPages || 1, Math.max(1, p + delta)));\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"fixed inset-0 z-50 flex flex-col bg-[#0b1020]\" dir={language === 'ar' ? 'rtl' : 'ltr'}>\n      {/* Header */}\n      <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between gap-3 border-b border-white/10 px-4 py-3\">\n        <button\n          onClick={onClose}\n          className=\"flex items-center gap-1 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm text-white/80 hover:bg-white/10\"\n        >\n          <X size={18} /> {t.close}\n        </button>\n\n        {state.kind === 'ready' && (\n          <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2 text-xs text-white/60\">\n            <BookOpen size={14} />\n            <span>\n              {t.page} {page} {t.of} {totalPages}\n            </span>\n            {state.offline && (\n              <span className=\"flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full bg-emerald-500/15 px-2 py-0.5 text-emerald-300\">\n                <WifiOff size={12} /> {t.offline}\n              </span>\n            )}\n          </div>\n        )}\n      </div>\n\n      {/* Body */}\n      <div ref={scrollRef} className=\"relative flex-1 overflow-auto\">\n        {state.kind === 'loading' && (\n          <div className=\"flex h-full items-center justify-center gap-3 text-white/70\">\n            <Loader2 className=\"animate-spin\" size={22} /> {t.loading}\n          </div>\n        )}\n\n        {state.kind === 'downloading' && (\n          <div className=\"flex h-full flex-col items-center justify-center gap-4 px-8 text-center\">\n            <Download className=\"text-indigo-300\" size={30} />\n            <div className=\"text-white/90\">\n              {t.downloading} — {state.progress.page}/{state.progress.pages}\n            </div>\n            <div className=\"h-2 w-full max-w-sm overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-white/10\">\n              <div\n                className=\"h-full rounded-full bg-indigo-400 transition-all\"\n                style={{\n                  width: `${state.progress.total ? ### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `d6c60416-53e6-4bda-bfd1-01de5978c570` — 2026-10-21T17:13:58.556003

```
The render will finish in ~20 min. Let me give you a status report while it runs.

## You asked: "can't we just use the links?" — No, and here's why it matters

| | Raw PDF from Drive | Light pages (what I built) |
|---|---|---|
| Arabic T1 | **207 MB** | **33 MB** |
| Full library | **~3 GB** | **~350 MB** |
| Files >100 MB | Drive returns an HTML warning, not the PDF | ✅ |
| Drive rate limits | 429s on normal use | ✅ (our own server) |
| Link moves/expires | App breaks mid-lesson | ✅ immutable |
| Offline after download | Browser can't cache PDFs reliably | ✅ cache-first |
| Pretty, on our terms | ✗ fixed black box | ✓ |

The links are **the source, not the delivery**. I saved all 66 of them in `source-links.json` so provenance is never lost.

## Engineering verdict — I checked the four things that matter for an installed app

1. **No API key ships to the device.** ✅ Verified clean — model calls go through your server.
2. **No file disclosure.** ✅ Tested path traversal against the new routes; blocked.
3. **Eviction protection — this was missing.** ⚠️→✅ Books could be silently evicted by the OS. I added `navigator.storage.persist()` in the download path.
4. **Offline works honestly.** ✅ Book pages are cache-first (fixed material, safe to keep). AI stays live, so Nour never presents a stale answer as fresh — matching the principle already in your `sw.js`.

## What I built while the render runs

- `server.ts` — new `/api/curriculum/*` routes with immutable caching (verified live: `200`, correct `image/webp`, `max-age=31536000`)
- `src/services/content/bookLibrary.ts` — on-demand download, progress, persistence request
- `src/components/curriculum/BookReader.tsx` — RTL-aware reader with page preload and offline badge
- `public/sw.js` — `BOOKS` cache, cache-first for pages only

## One honest gap

**The vision API is rate-limited through this proxy** — I get `429`s. That's why `unitCount=0` right now. I decoupled it so it can't block rendering, and I'll re-run structure extraction once the books finish (it's a few minutes, retryable, and doesn't require re-rendering).

**Real chapter titles are proven working** — that `المحور الأول → الوحدة الأولى → الدرس الأول: موقع بلدي → p.8` extraction succeeded in my direct test. It's a throughput issue, not a capability issue.

Want me to **wire the reader into the Library next**, or **prioritize getting the lesson structure in** first? I'd wire the reader — it makes the ~350 MB of books visible and testable right away.
```

 "new_str": "def parse_toc(pdf_path: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Return {\"offset\": int, \"units\": [{\"unit\": str, \"lessons\": [...]}]}.\n    Entries carry both the printed page and the resolved PDF page.\n    Two layouts occur in these books and both are handled:\n      A) \"12. . . . . .  title\"          (dot leader, Science/Math)\n      B) \"title\" then \"12\" on next line  (Social Studies)\n    \"\"\"\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)\n    try:\n        offset = _detect_offset(doc)\n        units: list[dict] = []\n        current: Optional[dict] = None\n\n        for i in _toc_pages(doc):\n            lines = [norm(l) for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\")]\n            lines = [l for l in lines if l.strip()]\n\n            for idx, line in enumerate(lines):\n                # Layout A\n                m = ENTRY_RE.match(line)\n                if m:\n                    title = clean_title(m.group(2))\n                    if title and re.search(r\"[\\w\\u0600-\\u06FF]\", title):\n                        entry = _entry(int(m.group(1)), title, offset, doc.page_count)\n                        current = _attach(units, current, entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # Layout B: this line is a title and the next is its page number.\n                nxt = lines[idx + 1] if idx + 1 < len(lines) else \"\"\n                nxt_digits = digits(nxt).strip(\" .-|\")\n                if (\n                    nxt_digits.isdigit()\n                    and not digits(line).strip(\" .-|\").isdigit()\n                    and ARABIC_RE.search(line)\n                    and 2 <= len(line.strip()) <= 90\n                ):\n                    title = clean_title(line)\n                    if title and not UNIT_RE.search(title):\n                        entry = _entry(int(nxt_digits), title, offset, doc.page_count)\n                        current = _attach(units, current, entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # A unit / mahwar heading.\n                if UNIT_RE.search(line) and not ENTRY_RE.match(line):\n                    heading = clean_title(DOT_LEADER_RE.sub(\" \", line))\n                    if 2 <= len(heading) <= 90:\n                        current = {\"unit\": heading, \"lessons\": []}\n                        units.append(current)\n\n        units = [u for u in units if u[\"lessons\"]]\n        return {\"offset\": offset, \"units\": units}\n    finally:\n        doc.close()\n\n\ndef _entry(printed: int, title: str, offset: int, page_count: int) -> dict:\n    resolved = printed + offset\n    return {\n        \"title\": title,\n        \"printedPage\": printed,\n        \"page\": resolved if 0 < resolved <= page_count else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef _attach(units: list, current: Optional[dict], entry: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Append an entry to the open unit, opening a default one if needed.\"\"\"\n    if current is None:\n        current = {\"unit\": \"المحتوى\", \"lessons\": []}\n        units.append(current)\n    current[\"lessons\"].append(entry)\n    return current",

 "old_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDeterministic table-of-contents extraction.\n\nThe ministry PDFs carry a real text layer, so contents can be read directly —\nno OCR, no vision API, no quota. Two quirks have to be undone first:\n\n1. Arabic lines are stored in visual order, i.e. with the word order reversed.\n   Reversing the words restores logical Arabic.\n2. The lam-alef ligature is decomposed into \"ا\" + \"ل\" + \"ا\" style sequences\n   (\"األ\" for \"الأ\"). These are repaired by table.\n\nPage numbers in the contents are the *printed* numbers. The offset to the PDF\npage index is detected per book by finding the most common difference between\na page's printed number and its position.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport fitz\n\n# Ligature repairs: NFKC leaves these broken, so fix them explicitly.\nLIGATURES = [\n    (\"األ\", \"الأ\"), (\"اإل\", \"الإ\"), (\"اآل\", \"الآ\"),\n    (\"ألا\", \"ألا\"), (\"إل\", \"إل\"),\n]\n\nARABIC_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\u0600-\\u06FF]\")\n# Arabic-Indic (0-9) and Extended Arabic-Indic digits -> ASCII.\nDIGITS = str.maketrans(\"٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹\",\n                       \"01234567890123456789\")\n\n\ndef digits(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Convert Arabic-Indic numerals to ASCII.\"\"\"\n    return unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s).translate(DIGITS)\n# \"12. . . . . . . title\" — number, dot leader, then the title.\nENTRY_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\d{1,4})\\s*\\.\\s*(?:\\.\\s*){2,}\\s*\\x03?\\s*(.+?)\\s*$\", re.M)\nUNIT_RE = re.compile(r\"(الوحدة|المحور|الوحده)\")\nDOT_LEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\\.{2,}[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\")\n\n\ndef norm(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalise and repair Arabic extracted from these PDFs.\"\"\"\n    s = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s)\n    for bad, good in LIGATURES:\n        s = s.replace(bad, good)\n    return s\n\n\ndef fix_visual_order(line: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"These PDFs store Arabic words in visual order. Reverse the words.\"\"\"\n    if not ARABIC_RE.search(line):\n        return line\n    words = line.split()\n    return \" \".join(reversed(words))\n\n\n# Letters that can precede the definite article (و ف ب ك ل + أ لل). A mid-word\n# \"ال\" after one of these is a real article and must be left alone.\nPREFIX_LETTERS = set(\"وفبكلأ\")\n\n\ndef fix_lam_alef(word: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    The lam-alef ligature is stored reversed as \"ال\" instead of \"لا\".\n    Repair only mid-word occurrences, and never a prefixed article\n    (بالمدرسة, والكتاب stay intact).\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(word) < 3 or ARABIC_RE.search(word) is None:\n        return word\n    # Protect a leading definite article, including after a prefix letter.\n    protected = 0\n    if word.startswith(\"ال\"):\n        protected = 2\n    elif len(word) > 2 and word[0] in PREFIX_LETTERS and word[1:3] == \"ال\":\n        protected = 3\n    head, tail = word[:protected], word[protected:]\n    return head + tail.replace(\"ال\", \"لا\")\n\n\ndef clean_title(raw: str) -> str:\n    raw = raw.replace(\"\\x03\", \" \").strip()\n    raw = fix_visual_order(raw)\n    # A colon that ended up attached to the wrong side after reversal.\n    raw = re.sub(r\"\\s+:\", \":\", raw)\n    raw = re.sub(r\":(\\S)\", r\": \\1\", raw)\n    # Unit headings read \"الوحدة: الأولى …\" once reversed; the colon belongs\n    # after the ordinal: \"الوحدة الأولى: …\".\n    m = re.match(r\"^(الوحدة|المحور)\\s*:\\s*(\\S+)\\s*(.*)$\", raw)\n    if m:\n        rest = f\" {m.group(3)}\" if m.group(3) else \"\"\n        raw = f\"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}:{rest}\"\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s{2,}\", \" \", raw).strip(\" .\")\n\n\ndef _toc_pages(doc) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Pages near the front that look like a table of contents.\"\"\"\n    hits = []\n    for i in range(min(20, doc.page_count)):\n        t = doc[i].get_text()\n        if len(ENTRY_RE.findall(t)) >= 3 or \"قائمة المحتوى\" in t or \"المحتويات\" in t:\n            hits.append(i)\n    return hits\n\n\ndef _detect_offset(doc) -> int:\n    \"\"\"\n    Printed page number -> PDF page index offset.\n    Scan pages for a bare number and take the most common difference.\n    \"\"\"\n    diffs = Counter()\n    for i in range(min(60, doc.page_count)):\n        lines = [l.strip() for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\") if l.strip()]\n        # Page numbers usually sit in the first or last couple of lines.\n        for cand in (lines[:2] + lines[-2:]):\n            digits = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", cand).strip(\" .-|\")\n            if digits.isdigit():\n                n = int(digits)\n                if 1 <= n <= doc.page_count:\n                    diffs[i - n] += 1\n    return diffs.most_common(1)[0][0] if diffs else 0\n\n\ndef parse_toc(pdf_path: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Return {\"offset\": int, \"units\": [{\"unit\": str, \"lessons\": [...]}]}.\n    Entries carry both the printed page and the resolved PDF page.\n    \"\"\"\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)\n    try:\n        offset = _detect_offset(doc)\n        units: list[dict] = []\n        current: Optional[dict] = None\n\n        for i in _toc_pages(doc):\n            for raw_line in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\"):\n                line = norm(raw_line)\n                if not line.strip():\n                    continue\n\n                m = ENTRY_RE.match(line)\n                if m:\n                    printed = int(m.group(1))\n                    title = clean_title(m.group(2))\n                    if not title:\n                        continue\n                    # A dot-leader line with no letters is a spacing artefact.\n                    if not re.search(r\"[\\w\\u0600-\\u06FF]\", title):\n                        continue\n                    entry = {\n                        \"title\": title,\n                        \"printedPage\": printed,\n                        \"page\": printed + offset if 0 < printed + offset <= doc.page_count else None,\n                    }\n                    if current is None:\n                        current = {\"unit\": \"المحتوى\", \"lessons\": []}\n                        units.append(current)\n                    current[\"lessons\"].append(entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # A unit/mahwar heading line (no dot leader).\n                if UNIT_RE.search(line) and not ENTRY_RE.match(line):\n                    heading = clean_title(DOT_LEADER_RE.sub(\" \", line))\n                    if 2 <= len(heading) <= 90:\n                        current = {\"unit\": heading, \"lessons\": []}\n                        units.append(current)\n\n        # Drop empty unit shells.\n        units = [u for u in units if u[\"lessons\"]]\n        return {\"offset\": offset, \"units\": units}\n    finally:\n        doc.close()\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import json\n    import sys\n\n    for p in sys.argv[1:]:\n        r = parse_toc(p)\n        print(f\"\\n=== {p}  offset={r['offset']}  units={len(r['units'])} ===\")\n        for u in r[\"units\"]:\n            print(f\"  {u['unit']}\")\n            for l in u[\"lessons\"][:6]:\n                print(f\"     p{l['printedPage']:>4} (pdf {l['page']})  {l['title']}\")\n",
 "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDeterministic table-of-contents extraction.\n\nThe ministry PDFs carry a real text layer, so contents can be read directly —\nno OCR, no vision API, no quota. Two quirks have to be undone first:\n\n1. Arabic lines are stored in visual order, i.e. with the word order reversed.\n   Reversing the words restores logical Arabic.\n2. The lam-alef ligature is decomposed into \"ا\" + \"ل\" + \"ا\" style sequences\n   (\"األ\" for \"الأ\"). These are repaired by table.\n\nPage numbers in the contents are the *printed* numbers. The offset to the PDF\npage index is detected per book by finding the most common difference between\na page's printed number and its position.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport fitz\n\n# Ligature repairs: NFKC leaves these broken, so fix them explicitly.\nLIGATURES = [\n    (\"األ\", \"الأ\"), (\"اإل\", \"الإ\"), (\"اآل\", \"الآ\"),\n    (\"ألا\", \"ألا\"), (\"إل\", \"إل\"),\n]\n\nARABIC_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\u0600-\\u06FF]\")\n# Arabic-Indic (0-9) and Extended Arabic-Indic digits -> ASCII.\nDIGITS = str.maketrans(\"٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹\",\n                       \"01234567890123456789\")\n\n\ndef digits(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Convert Arabic-Indic numerals to ASCII.\"\"\"\n    return unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s).translate(DIGITS)\n# \"12. . . . . . . title\" — number, dot leader, then the title.\nENTRY_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\d{1,4})\\s*\\.\\s*(?:\\.\\s*){2,}\\s*\\x03?\\s*(.+?)\\s*$\", re.M)\nUNIT_RE = re.compile(r\"(الوحدة|المحور|الوحده)\")\nDOT_LEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\\.{2,}[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\")\n\n\ndef norm(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalise and repair Arabic extracted from these PDFs.\"\"\"\n    s = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s)\n    for bad, good in LIGATURES:\n        s = s.replace(bad, good)\n    return s\n\n\ndef fix_visual_order(line: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"These PDFs store Arabic words in visual order. Reverse the words.\"\"\"\n    if not ARABIC_RE.search(line):\n        return line\n    words = line.split()\n    return \" \".join(reversed(words))\n\n\n# Letters that can precede the definite article (و ف ب ك ل + أ لل). A mid-word\n# \"ال\" after one of these is a real article and must be left alone.\nPREFIX_LETTERS = set(\"وفبكلأ\")\n\n\ndef fix_lam_alef(word: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    The lam-alef ligature is stored reversed as \"ال\" instead of \"لا\".\n    Repair only mid-word occurrences, and never a prefixed article\n    (بالمدرسة, والكتاب stay intact).\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(word) < 3 or ARABIC_RE.search(word) is None:\n        return word\n    # Protect a leading definite article, including after a prefix letter.\n    protected = 0\n    if word.startswith(\"ال\"):\n        protected = 2\n    elif len(word) > 2 and word[0] in PREFIX_LETTERS and word[1:3] == \"ال\":\n        protected = 3\n    head, tail = word[:protected], word[protected:]\n    return head + tail.replace(\"ال\", \"لا\")\n\n\ndef clean_title(raw: str) -> str:\n    raw = raw.replace(\"\\x03\", \" \").strip()\n    raw = fix_visual_order(raw)\n    # A colon that ended up attached to the wrong side after reversal.\n    raw = re.sub(r\"\\s+:\", \":\", raw)\n    raw = re.sub(r\":(\\S)\", r\": \\1\", raw)\n    # Unit headings read \"الوحدة: الأولى …\" once reversed; the colon belongs\n    # after the ordinal: \"الوحدة الأولى: …\".\n    m = re.match(r\"^(الوحدة|المحور)\\s*:\\s*(\\S+)\\s*(.*)$\", raw)\n    if m:\n        rest = f\" {m.group(3)}\" if m.group(3) else \"\"\n        raw = f\"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}:{rest}\"\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s{2,}\", \" \", raw).strip(\" .\")\n\n\ndef _toc_pages(doc) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Pages near the front that look like a table of contents.\"\"\"\n    hits = []\n    for i in range(min(20, doc.page_count)):\n        t = doc[i].get_text()\n        if len(ENTRY_RE.findall(t)) >= 3 or \"قائمة المحتوى\" in t or \"المحتويات\" in t:\n            hits.append(i)\n    return hits\n\n\ndef _detect_offset(doc) -> int:\n    \"\"\"\n    Printed page number -> PDF page index offset.\n    Scan pages for a bare number and take the most common difference.\n    \"\"\"\n    diffs = Counter()\n    for i in range(min(60, doc.page_count)):\n        lines = [l.strip() for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\") if l.strip()]\n        # Page numbers usually sit in the first or last couple of lines.\n        for cand in (lines[:2] + lines[-2:]):\n            digits = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", cand).strip(\" .-|\")\n            if digits.isdigit():\n                n = int(digits)\n                if 1 <= n <= doc.page_count:\n                    diffs[i - n] += 1\n    return diffs.most_common(1)[0][0] if diffs else 0\n\n\ndef parse_toc(pdf_path: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Return {\"offset\": int, \"units\": [{\"unit\": str, \"lessons\": [...]}]}.\n    Entries carry both the printed page and the resolved PDF page.\n    Two layouts occur in these books and both are handled:\n      A) \"12. . . . . .  title\"          (dot leader, Science/Math)\n      B) \"title\" then \"12\" on next line  (Social Studies)\n    \"\"\"\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)\n    try:\n        offset = _detect_offset(doc)\n        units: list[dict] = []\n        current: Optional[dict] = None\n\n        for i in _toc_pages(doc):\n            lines = [norm(l) for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\")]\n            lines = [l for l in lines if l.strip()]\n\n            for idx, line in enumerate(lines):\n                # Layout A\n                m = ENTRY_RE.match(line)\n                if m:\n                    title = clean_title(m.group(2))\n                    if title and re.search(r\"[\\w\\u0600-\\u06FF]\", title):\n                        entry = _entry(int(m.group(1)), title, offset, doc.page_count)\n                        current = _attach(units, current, entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # Layout B: this line is a title and the next is its page number.\n                nxt = lines[idx + 1] if idx + 1 < len(lines) else \"\"\n                nxt_digits = digits(nxt).strip(\" .-|\")\n                if (\n                    nxt_digits.isdigit()\n                    and not digits(line).strip(\" .-|\").isdigit()\n                    and ARABIC_RE.search(line)\n                    and 2 <= len(line.strip()) <= 90\n                ):\n                    title = clean_title(line)\n                    if title and not UNIT_RE.search(title):\n                        entry = _entry(int(nxt_digits), title, offset, doc.page_count)\n                        current = _attach(units, current, entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # A unit / mahwar heading.\n                if UNIT_RE.search(line) and not ENTRY_RE.match(line):\n                    heading = clean_title(DOT_LEADER_RE.sub(\" \", line))\n                    if 2 <= len(heading) <= 90:\n                        current = {\"unit\": heading, \"lessons\": []}\n                        units.append(current)\n\n        units = [u for u in units if u[\"lessons\"]]\n        return {\"offset\": offset, \"units\": units}\n    finally:\n        doc.close()\n\n\ndef _entry(printed: int, title: str, offset: int, page_count: int) -> dict:\n    resolved = printed + offset\n    return {\n        \"title\": title,\n        \"printedPage\": printed,\n        \"page\": resolved if 0 < resolved <= page_count else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef _attach(units: list, current: Optional[dict], entry: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Append an entry to the open unit, opening a default one if needed.\"\"\"\n    if current is None:\n        current = {\"unit\": \"المحتوى\", \"lessons\": []}\n        units.append(current)\n    current[\"lessons\"].append(entry)\n    return current\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import json\n    import sys\n\n    for p in sys.argv[1:]:\n        r = parse_toc(p)\n        print(f\"\\n=== {p}  offset={r['offset']}  units={len(r['units'])} ===\")\n        for u in r[\"units\"]:\n            print(f\"  {u['unit']}\")\n            for l in u[\"lessons\"][:6]:\n                print(f\"     p{l['printedPage']:>4} (pdf {l['page']})  {l['title']}\")\n",

The offset to the PDF\npage index is detected per book by finding the most common difference between\na page's printed number and its position.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport fitz\n\n# Ligature repairs: NFKC leaves these broken, so fix them explicitly.\nLIGATURES = [\n    (\"األ\", \"الأ\"), (\"اإل\", \"الإ\"), (\"اآل\", \"الآ\"),\n    (\"ألا\", \"ألا\"), (\"إل\", \"إل\"),\n]\n\nARABIC_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\u0600-\\u06FF]\")\n# Arabic-Indic (0-9) and Extended Arabic-Indic digits -> ASCII.\nDIGITS = str.maketrans(\"٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹\",\n                       \"01234567890123456789\")\n\n\ndef digits(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Convert Arabic-Indic numerals to ASCII.\"\"\"\n    return unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s).translate(DIGITS)\n# \"12. . . . . . . title\" — number, dot leader, then the title.\nENTRY_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\d{1,4})\\s*\\.\\s*(?:\\.\\s*){2,}\\s*\\x03?\\s*(.+?)\\s*$\", re.M)\nUNIT_RE = re.compile(r\"(الوحدة|المحور|الوحده)\")\nDOT_LEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\\.{2,}[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\")\n\n\ndef norm(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalise and repair Arabic extracted from these PDFs.\"\"\"\n    s = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s)\n    for bad, good in LIGATURES:\n        s = s.replace(bad, good)\n    return s\n\n\ndef fix_visual_order(line: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"These PDFs store Arabic words in visual order. Reverse the words.\"\"\"\n    if not ARABIC_RE.search(line):\n        return line\n    words = line.split()\n    return \" \".join(reversed(words))\n\n\n# Letters that can precede the definite article (و ف ب ك ل + أ لل). A mid-word\n# \"ال\" after one of these is a real article and must be left alone.\nPREFIX_LETTERS = set(\"وفبكلأ\")\n\n\ndef fix_lam_alef(word: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    The lam-alef ligature is stored reversed as \"ال\" instead of \"لا\".\n    Repair only mid-word occurrences, and never a prefixed article\n    (بالمدرسة, والكتاب stay intact).\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(word) < 3 or ARABIC_RE.search(word) is None:\n        return word\n    # Protect a leading definite article, including after a prefix letter.\n    protected = 0\n    if word.startswith(\"ال\"):\n        protected = 2\n    elif len(word) > 2 and word[0] in PREFIX_LETTERS and word[1:3] == \"ال\":\n        protected = 3\n    head, tail = word[:protected], word[protected:]\n    return head + tail.replace(\"ال\", \"لا\")\n\n\ndef clean_title(raw: str) -> str:\n    raw = raw.replace(\"\\x03\", \" \").strip()\n    raw = fix_visual_order(raw)\n    # A colon that ended up attached to the wrong side after reversal.\n    raw = re.sub(r\"\\s+:\", \":\", raw)\n    raw = re.sub(r\":(\\S)\", r\": \\1\", raw)\n    # Unit headings read \"الوحدة: الأولى …\" once reversed; the colon belongs\n    # after the ordinal: \"الوحدة الأولى: …\".\n    m = re.match(r\"^(الوحدة|المحور)\\s*:\\s*(\\S+)\\s*(.*)$\", raw)\n    if m:\n        rest = f\" {m.group(3)}\" if m.group(3) else \"\"\n        raw = f\"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}:{rest}\"\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s{2,}\", \" \", raw).strip(\" .\")\n\n\ndef _toc_pages(doc) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Pages near the front that look like a table of contents. Two shapes:\n    a dot-leader list, or a contents heading with many bare numerals.\n    \"\"\"\n    hits = []\n    for i in range(min(20, doc.page_count)):\n        t = norm(doc[i].get_text())\n        if \"قائمة المحتوى\" in t or \"المحتويات\" in t or \"قائمة املحتوى\" in t:\n            hits.append(i)\n            continue\n        if len(ENTRY_RE.findall(t)) >= 3:\n            hits.append(i)\n            continue\n        # Layout B: several lines that are only a page number.\n        bare = sum(\n            1\n            for l in t.split(\"\\n\")\n            if digits(l).strip(\" .-|\").isdigit() and l.strip()\n        )\n        if bare >= 5 and (\"الدرس\" in t or \"الوحدة\" in t):\n            hits.append(i)\n    return hits\n\n\ndef _detect_offset(doc) -> int:\n    \"\"\"\n    Printed page number -> PDF page index offset.\n    Scan pages for a bare number and take the most common difference.\n    \"\"\"\n    diffs = Counter()\n    for i in range(min(60, doc.page_count)):\n        lines = [l.strip() for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\") if l.strip()]\n        # Page numbers usually sit in the first or last couple of lines.\n        for cand in (lines[:2] + lines[-2:]):\n            digits = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", cand).strip(\" .-|\")\n            if digits.isdigit():\n                n = int(digits)\n                if 1 <= n <= doc.page_count:\n                    diffs[i - n] += 1\n    return diffs.most_common(1)[0][0] if diffs else 0\n\n\ndef parse_toc(pdf_path: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Return {\"offset\": int, \"units\": [{\"unit\": str, \"lessons\": [...]}]}.\n    Entries carry both the printed page and the resolved PDF page.\n    Two layouts occur in these books and both are handled:\n      A) \"12. . . . . .  title\"          (dot leader, Science/Math)\n      B) \"title\" then \"12\" on next line  (Social Studies)\n    \"\"\"\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)\n    try:\n        offset = _detect_offset(doc)\n        units: list[dict] = []\n        current: Optional[dict] = None\n\n        for i in _toc_pages(doc):\n            lines = [norm(l) for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\")]\n            lines = [l for l in lines if l.strip()]\n\n            for idx, line in enumerate(lines):\n                # Layout A\n                m = ENTRY_RE.match(line)\n                if m:\n                    title = clean_title(m.group(2))\n                    if title and re.search(r\"[\\w\\u0600-\\u06FF]\", title):\n                        entry = _entry(int(m.group(1)), title, offset, doc.page_count)\n                        current = _attach(units, current, entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # Layout B: this line is a title and the next is its page number.\n                nxt = lines[idx + 1] if idx + 1 < len(lines) else \"\"\n                nxt_digits = digits(nxt).strip(\" .-|\")\n                if (\n                    nxt_digits.isdigit()\n                    and not digits(line).strip(\" .-|\").isdigit()\n                    and ARABIC_RE.search(line)\n                    and 2 <= len(line.strip()) <= 90\n                ):\n                    title = clean_title(line)\n                    if title and not UNIT_RE.search(title):\n                        entry = _entry(int(nxt_digits), title, offset, doc.page_count)\n                        current = _attach(units, current, entry)\n                    continue\n\n                # A unit / mahwar heading.\n                if UNIT_RE.search(line) and not ENTRY_RE.match(line):\n                    heading = clean_title(DOT_LEADER_RE.sub(\" \", line))\n                    if 2 <= len(heading) <= 90:\n                        current = {\"unit\": heading, \"lessons\": []}\n                        units.append(current)\n\n        units = [u for u in units if u[\"lessons\"]]\n        return {\"offset\": offset, \"units\": units}\n    finally:\n        doc.close()\n\n\ndef _entry(printed: int, title: str, offset: int, page_count: int) -> dict:\n    resolved = printed + offset\n    return {\n        \"title\": title,\n        \"printedPage\": printed,\n        \"page\": resolved if 0 < resolved <= page_count else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef _attach(units: list, current: Optional[dict], entry: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Append an entry to the open unit, opening a default one if needed.\"\"\"\n    if current is None:\n        current = {\"unit\": \"المحتوى\", \"lessons\": []}\n        units.append(current)\n    current[\"lessons\"].append(entry)\n    return current\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import json\n    import sys\n\n    for p in sys.argv[1:]:\n        r = parse_toc(p)\n        print(f\"\\n=== {p}  offset={r['offset']}  units={len(r['units'])} ===\")\n        for u in r[\"units\"]:\n            print(f\"  {u['unit']}\")\n            for l in u[\"lessons\"][:6]:\n                print(f\"     p{l['printedPage']:>4} (pdf {l['page']})  {l['title']}\")\n",
