'واجب (التفاصيل غير محددة)' : 'Homework (details not specified)' });\n        }\n      } else if (lower.includes('رياض') || lower.includes('math') || lower.includes('حساب') || lower.includes('كسور')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'الرياضيات' });\n        if (lower.includes('واجب') || lower.includes('homework') || lower.includes('مسائل')) {\n          homework.push({ subject: 'الرياضيات', description: isArabic ? 'واجب (التفاصيل غير محددة)' : 'Homework (details not specified)' });\n        }\n      }\n      if (lower.includes('ساينس') || (lower.includes('sci') && lower.includes('fr')) || lower.includes('sciences')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'العلوم بالفرنسية (Sciences)' });\n      } else if (lower.includes('علوم') || lower.includes('science')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'العلوم' });\n      }\n      if (lower.includes('عرب') || lower.includes('arabic')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'اللغة العربية' });\n        if (lower.includes('واجب') || lower.includes('homework')) {\n          homework.push({ subject: 'اللغة العربية', description: isArabic ? 'واجب (التفاصيل غير محددة)' : 'Homework (details not specified)' });\n        }\n      }\n      if (lower.includes('إنجليز') || lower.includes('انجليز') || lower.includes('english')) {\n        lessons.push({ subject: 'اللغة الإنجليزية' });\n      }\n\n      return res.json({\n        lessonsCovered: lessons,                      // may be empty; never invent a default lesson\n        homeworkAssigned: homework,\n        notes: trimmedInput,\n        isSilence: false,\n        isVague: lessons.length === 0,\n        detectedConfidence: lessons.length > 0 ? 'partial' : 'vague',\n        degraded: true,\n        source: 'local_parser_fallback',\n      });\n    }\n\n    const systemInstruction = `\nYou are the \"AI School Companion\" Day Record extractor for a ${grade} student named \"${studentName}\".\nThe student has just come home from school and described their day in free-text: \"${trimmedInput}\".\nToday's timetable scheduled subjects are: ${JSON.stringify(todayTimetableSubjects)}.\n\nYOUR TASK:\nExtract the concrete lessons covered and homework assigned into structured JSON.\nCRITICAL RULES:\n1. Do not hallucinate or invent subjects that the student did not attend or mention.\n2. If the student explicitly names a subject not in the timetable, capture it accurately.\n3. Extract homework with clear subject, description, and due date if stated.\n4. If input is vague or brief, mark detectedConfidence as \"partial\" or \"vague\".\n5. Return JSON ONLY matching this exact structure:\n{\n  \"lessonsCovered\": [\n    { \"subject\": \"string\", \"topic\": \"string (optional)\", \"notes\": \"string (optional)\" }\n  ],\n  \"homeworkAssigned\": [\n    { \"subject\": \"string\", \"description\": \"string\", \"dueDate\": \"string (optional)\" }\n  ],\n  \"notes\": \"string (optional)\",\n  \"detectedConfidence\": \"high\" | \"partial\" | \"vague\",\n  \"isSilence\": boolean,\n  \"isVague\": boolean\n}\n`.trim();\n\n    const response = await gemini.generateContent({\n      model: process.env.GEMINI_MODEL || DEFAULT_TEXT_MODEL,\n      contents: [{ role: 'user', parts: [{ text: trimmedInput }] }],\n      config: {\n        systemInstruction,\n        responseMimeType: 'application/json',\n      },\n    });\n    const responseText = geminiText(response);\n\n    const text = responseText || '{}';\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(text);\n\n    res.json({\n      lessonsCovered: parsed.lessonsCovered || [],\n      homeworkAssigned: parsed.homeworkAssigned || [],\n      notes: parsed.notes || trimmedInput,\n      detectedConfidence: parsed.detectedConfidence || 'partial',\n      isSilence: Boolean(parsed.isSilence),\n      isVague: Boolean(parsed.isVague),\n      source: 'gemini',\n    });\n  } catch (error: any) {\n    console.error('Reconstruct Day API Error:', error);\n    res.json({\n      lessonsCovered: [],\n      homeworkAssigned: [],\n      notes: req.body?.studentInput || '',\n      detectedConfidence: 'vague',\n      isSilence: false,\n      isVague: true,\n      degraded: true,\n      source: 'error_fallback',\n    });\n  }\n});\n\n// Curriculum library: light book pages + manifests, served from a\n// CDN-friendly route. Page filenames are content-stable, so they can be cached\n// immutably; the client downloads one book on demand and keeps it offline.\nconst CURRICULUM_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, 'content', 'curriculum');\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/index', (_req, res) => {\n  const dir = path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books');\n  fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }, (err, entries) => {\n    if (err) return res.status(503).json({ error: 'curriculum_unavailable' });\n    const books = [];\n    for (const e of entries) {\n      if (!e.isDirectory()) continue;\n      try {\n        const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, e.name, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8'));\n        books.push({\n          id: m.id, subject: m.subject, language: m.language, term: m.term,\n          pages: m.pages, bytes: m.bytes, width: m.width,\n          unitCount: (m.units || []).length,\n        });\n      } catch { /* skip an unreadable book rather than fail the list */ }\n    }\n    res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-cache');\n    res.json({ books });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/manifest', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'manifest.json'), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'book_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/pages/:file', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId, file } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  if (!/^\\d{4}\\.webp$/.test(file)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_page' });\n  // Content is immutable per filename, so the device may cache it indefinitely.\n  res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable');\n  res.type('image/webp');\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'pages', file), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'page_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\n// Dev vs Prod server setup\nif (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {\n  const { createServer: createViteServer } = await import('vite');\n  const vite = await createViteServer({\n    server: { middlewareMode: true },\n    appType: 'spa',\n  });\n  app.use(vite.middlewares);\n} else {\n  app.use(express.static(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist')));\n  app.get('*', (_req, res) => {\n    res.sendFile(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist', 'index.html'));\n  });\n}\n\napp.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {\n  console.log(`AI School Companion Server running on http://0.0.0.0:${PORT}`);\n});\n",
 "new_content": "import express from 'express';\nimport dotenv from 'dotenv';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport fs from 'fs';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\n\ndotenv.config();\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst app = express();\nconst PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;\n\napp.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }));\n\n// AI access via the Gemini REST API.\n// The @google/genai SDK misclassifies Google's newer \"AQ.\" authentication keys\n// as OAuth access tokens and returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, while\n// the same key authenticates correctly over REST. We therefore call the REST API\n// directly with the key in the x-goog-api-key header, which works for both the\n// legacy \"AIza\" and the newer \"AQ.\" key formats.\nconst API_KEY_SOURCES = ['GEMINI_API_KEY', 'GOOGLE_API_KEY', 'GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY', 'API_KEY'] as const;\nconst apiKeySource = API_KEY_SOURCES.find((name) => Boolean(process.env[name])) ?? null;\nconst apiKey = apiKeySource ? process.env[apiKeySource] : undefined;\nconst GEMINI_BASE_URL = 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta';\n\nif (!apiKey) {\n  console.warn(\n    '\\n⚠️  NO AI API KEY DETECTED — Nour will run in local companion mode (no live model calls).\\n' +\n      '   To enable the live tutor, provide a Gemini API key as one of:\\n' +\n      `   ${API_KEY_SOURCES.join(', ')}\\n` +\n      '   Easiest local option: create a file named \".env\" in the project root containing\\n' +\n      '     GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key_here\\n' +\n      '   then restart the server. (.env is gitignored.)\\n'\n  );\n}\n\nclass GeminiRequestError extends Error {\n  status: number;\n  constructor(status: number, message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n// Preferred text models, tried in order. A model that is temporarily overloaded\n// (503) or rate-limited (429) falls through to the next, so a busy model never\n// takes the whole app down. Text-only: TTS/image models are never substituted.\nconst TEXT_MODEL_FALLBACKS = ['gemini-2.5-flash', 'gemini-3.5-flash'];\nconst DEFAULT_TEXT_MODEL = TEXT_MODEL_FALLBACKS[0];\n\n/** Resolve the model list to attempt for a request. */\nfunction modelCandidates(requested: string): string[] {\n  const isTextModel = !requested.includes('tts') && !requested.includes('image');\n  if (!isTextModel) return [requested];\n  const chain = [requested, ...TEXT_MODEL_FALLBACKS];\n  return [...new Set(chain)];\n}\n\n/**\n * Minimal REST client for the subset of Gemini the app uses (generateContent).\n * Kept intentionally small so the key travels in the header the API expects.\n */\nconst gemini = {\n  async generateContent(body: {\n    model: string;\n    contents: unknown;\n    config?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  }): Promise<any> {\n    if (!apiKey) throw new GeminiRequestError(401, 'No API key configured');\n    const { model, contents, config } = body;\n    const payload: Record<string, unknown> = { contents };\n    if (config) {\n      const { systemInstruction, ...generationConfig } = config as Record<string, unknown>;\n      // REST expects sampling/response options nested under generationConfig;\n      // only systemInstruction sits at the top level.\n      if (Object.keys(generationConfig).length > 0) payload.generationConfig = generationConfig;\n      if (systemInstruction) payload.systemInstruction = { parts: [{ text: systemInstruction }] };\n    }\n\n    const candidates = modelCandidates(model);\n    let lastError: GeminiRequestError | null = null;\n    for (let i = 0; i < candidates.length; i++) {\n      const resp = await fetch(`${GEMINI_BASE_URL}/models/${candidates[i]}:generateContent`, {\n        method: 'POST',\n        headers: {\n          'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n          'x-goog-api-key': apiKey,\n        },\n        body: JSON.stringify(payload),\n      });\n      const json: any = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));\n      if (resp.ok) return json;\n\n      const status = resp.status;\n      lastError = new GeminiRequestError(\n        status,\n        json?.error?.message || `Gemini request failed (HTTP ${status})`\n      );\n      // Only transient availability/quota problems justify trying another model.\n      const retryable = status === 503 || status === 429 || status === 500;\n      if (!retryable || i === candidates.length - 1) throw lastError;\n      console.warn(\n        `[gemini] ${candidates[i]} unavailable (HTTP ${status}); falling back to ${candidates[i + 1]}`\n      );\n    }\n    throw lastError ?? new GeminiRequestError(500, 'Gemini request failed');\n  },\n};\n\n/** Extract plain text from a generateContent response. */\nfunction geminiText(response: any): string {\n  const parts = response?.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts;\n  if (!Array.isArray(parts)) return '';\n  return parts\n    .map((p: any) => (typeof p?.text === 'string' ? p.text : ''))\n    .join('')\n    .trim();\n}\n\n// Quota & Rate Limit Protection (Circuit breaker for 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)\nlet globalQuotaCooldownUntil = 0;\n\nfunction isQuotaExhaustedError(err: any): boolean {\n  if (!err) return false;\n  const status = err.status || err.code;\n  const msg = String(err.message || err).toLowerCase();\n  return (\n    status === 429 ||\n    msg.includes('429') ||\n    msg.includes('resource_exhausted') ||\n    msg.includes('quota') ||\n    msg.includes('rate limit')\n  );\n}\n\nfunction handleAiError(scope: string, err: any) {\n  if (isQuotaExhaustedError(err)) {\n    // 10-minute cooldown where no external calls are made; graceful fallbacks are served\n    globalQuotaCooldownUntil = Date.now() + 10 * 60 * 1000;\n  } else {\n    console.warn(`[${scope}] handled gracefully:`, err?.message || err);\n  }\n}\n\n// Health check endpoint\napp.get('/api/health', (_req, res) => {\n  res.json({\n    status: 'ok',\n    hasApiKey: Boolean(apiKey),\n    apiKeySource,\n    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n  });\n});\n\n// Chat API endpoint for Companion\napp.post('/api/chat', async (req, res) => {\n  try {\n    const { messages = [], studentName = 'طالب', grade = 'Grade 5', language = 'ar', schoolBrainContext = null } = req.body;\n\n    const isArabic = language === 'ar';\n    const lastUserMsg = (messages[messages.length - 1]?.content || '').trim();\n    const lowerUserMsg = lastUserMsg.toLowerCase();\n\n    // Specific intent detection for Phase 3\n    const isDontUnderstand =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('مش فاهم') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('مش فاهمة') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes(\"don't understand\") ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('dont understand') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes(\"don't get it\");\n\n    const isExplainDifferently =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اشرح بطريقة تانية') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('طريقة تانية') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اشرح تاني') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('explain differently') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('another way') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('مش واضحة');\n\n    const isTestMe =\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اختبرني') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اسألني سؤال') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('اختبار') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('test me') ||\n      lowerUserMsg.includes('quiz me');\n\n    if (!apiKey || Date.now() < globalQuotaCooldownUntil) {\n      // Graceful offline/local companion fallback if API key is not yet set or during quota cooldown\n      let fallbackReply = '';\n      if (isDontUnderstand) {\n        fallbackReply = isArabic\n          ? `ولا يهمك خالص يا ${studentName}! عادي جداً متفهمش من أول مرة، دي خطوة طبيعية في التعلم. قولي إيه أكثر نقطة حسيتها ملخبطة وهنبسطها سوا خطوة بخطوة.`\n          : `No worries at all, ${studentName}! It's completely normal not to understand right away. Tell me which part felt tricky, and we'll break it down step by step together.`;\n      } else if (isExplainDifferently) {\n        fallbackReply = isArabic\n          ? `حاضر يا ${studentName}! تعال نجرب مثال من حياتنا اليومية أو نشبه الموضوع بحاجة بنشوفها كل يوم. قولي تحب نبدأ من أول فكرة ولا من النص؟`\n          : `Sure thing, ${studentName}! Let's look at this with a simple real-world analogy. Would you like to restart from the beginning or focus on the tricky part?`;\n      } else if (isTestMe) {\n        fallbackReply = isArabic\n          ? `فكرة ممتازة وتحدي حلو يا ${studentName}! جاهز لسؤال خفيف وسريع على اللي ذكرته؟ خد وقتك خالص وفكر على مهلك.`\n          : `Awesome attitude and great challenge, ${studentName}! Ready for a quick, friendly question on what we discussed? Take your time!`;\n      } else {\n        fallbackReply = isArabic\n          ? `أهلاً يا ${studentName}! أنا رفيقك الذكي للتعلم. أنا هنا علشان أسمعك وأساعدك تنظم يومك وتفهم اللي محتاجه بهدوء ودون أي ضغط.`\n          : `Hello ${studentName}! I am your AI School Companion. I am here to help organize your day and walk through any questions without stress.`;\n      }\n\n      return res.json({\n        reply: fallbackReply,\n        source: 'local_companion_fallback',\n        degraded: true,\n        detectedIntent: isDontUnderstand ? 'dont_understand' : isExplainDifferently ? 'explain_differently' : isTestMe ? 'test_me' : 'general',\n      });\n    }\n\n    const contextJson = schoolBrainContext ? JSON.stringify({\n      school: schoolBrainContext.school || null,\n      location: schoolBrainContext.location || null,\n      curriculumTrack: schoolBrainContext.curriculumTrack || null,\n      dayRecord: schoolBrainContext.dayRecord || null,\n      activeMission: schoolBrainContext.activeMission || null,\n    }) : 'No verified School Brain context was supplied.';\n\n    const systemInstruction = `\nYou are the \"AI School Companion\" (الرفيق الدراسي الذكي), a personal AI learning assistant for a ${grade} student named \"${studentName}\".\nCRITICAL PRINCIPLES:\n1. You are an AI companion, NOT a human teacher or parent. Never pretend to be human.\n2. Tone: Warm, patient, encouraging, age-appropriate for an ~11-year-old child.\n3. Absolutely NO moralizing, scolding, or guilt-tripping (e.g. never say \"you should have studied earlier\" or \"why didn't you finish?\").\n4. Praise must be specific and grounded, never generic or effusive.\n5. Language: Primarily Egyptian/Friendly Arabic when the student writes in Arabic (${isArabic ? 'Active' : 'Optional'}), clear simple English if English is selected.\n6. 'lessons.json');\n  res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=86400');\n  res.sendFile(file, (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'lessons_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\n// Dev vs The app server reads\ncontent/curriculum/books/<id>/, so each rendered book needs two things there:\n\n  manifest.json  a real file (small, committed, so the book list is auditable)\n  lessons.json   a real file (small, committed; the lesson text the app shows)\n  pages/         a symlink to the rendered images (large, gitignored)\n\nRun after tools/curriculum/pipeline.py and tools/curriculum/extract_lessons.py.\n\nUsage:\n    AMINA_BOOKS_DIR=/path/to/books python3 tools/curriculum/link_books.py\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport os\nimport shutil\nimport sys\n\nREPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))\nSOURCE = os.environ.get('AMINA_BOOKS_DIR', 'books')\nTARGET = os.path.join(REPO, 'content', 'curriculum', 'books')\n\n\ndef link_book(book_id: str) -> str:\n    src_dir = os.path.join(SOURCE, book_id)\n    manifest = os.path.join(src_dir, 'manifest.json')\n    pages = os.path.join(src_dir, 'pages')\n\n    if not os.path.exists(manifest):\n        return 'no manifest'\n    if not os.path.isdir(pages) or not os.listdir(pages):\n        return 'no pages'\n\n    dst_dir = os.path.join(TARGET, book_id)\n    os.makedirs(dst_dir, exist_ok=True)\n\n    # Copy the manifest so the committed book list matches what is served.\n    shutil.copyfile(manifest, os.path.join(dst_dir, 'manifest.json'))\n\n    # Lesson text is small and text-only, so it is committed alongside the\n    # manifest. That way the app's lesson content is reviewable in the repo and\n    # survives without the external render directory.\n    lessons = os.path.join(src_dir, 'lessons.json')\n    if os.path.exists(lessons):\n        shutil.copyfile(lessons, os.path.join(dst_dir, 'lessons.json'))\n\n    link = os.path.join(dst_dir, 'pages')\n    if os.path.islink(link):\n        if os.path.realpath(link) == os.path.realpath(pages):\n            return 'already linked'\n        os.unlink(link)\n    elif os.path.isdir(link):\n        return 'skipped: real pages dir present'\n    os.symlink(pages, link)\n\n    with open(manifest) as fh:\n        meta = json.load(fh)\n    return f\"linked {meta.get('pages', '?')}p\"\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    if not os.path.isdir(SOURCE):\n        print(f'source dir not found: {SOURCE}', file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    for book_id in sorted(os.listdir(SOURCE)):\n        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(SOURCE, book_id)):\n            continue\n        print(f'{book_id:24s} {link_book(book_id)}', flush=True)\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}

<button\n                  onClick={() => askNour('simplify', '', '')}\n                  className=\"px-3 py-2 rounded-lg bg-white border border-indigo-300 text-indigo-800 text-sm font-medium\"\n Selecting one opens the book at that page.\n */\n\nimport React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\nimport { BookOpen, ChevronLeft, ChevronRight, Loader2, AlertCircle } from 'lucide-react';\nimport {\n  allBooksForSubject,\n  getBookContents,\n  type BookContents,\n} from '../../services/content/bookCatalog';\nimport { downloadedBookIds, type BookSummary } from '../../services/content/bookLibrary';\n\ninterface Props {\n  subjectId: string;\n  language: 'ar' | 'en';\n  isAr: boolean;\n  isFr: boolean;\n  /** Open the reader for a book, optionally at a given image page. */\n  onOpenBook: (bookId: string, page?: number) => void;\n}\n\nexport const BookContentsView: React.FC<Props> = ({ subjectId, language, isAr, isFr, onOpenBook }) => {\n  const [books, setBooks] = useState<BookSummary[]>([]);\n  const [contents, setContents] = useState<Record<string, BookContents>>({});\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);\n  const [error, setError] = useState(false);\n  const [activeBookId, setActiveBookId] = useState<string | null>(null);\n  const [downloaded] = useState<string[]>(() => downloadedBookIds());\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let alive = true;\n    setLoading(true);\n    setError(false);\n    setContents({});\n\n    allBooksForSubject(subjectId)\n      .then(async (list) => {\n        if (!alive) return;\n        setBooks(list);\n        if (list.length === 0) {\n          setLoading(false);\n          return;\n        }\n        // Default to the student's language edition when one exists.\n        const preferred = list.find((b) => b.language === language) ?? list[0];\n        setActiveBookId(preferred.id);"

These tests read the\n * committed lessons.json files and check the text is present, in reading order,\n * and not the sort of artifact that would embarrass the app in front of a\n * student (mojibake, decorative letter runs, or an entire lesson of dots).\n */\n\nimport * as fs from 'fs';\nimport * as path from 'path';\n\nlet passed = 0;\nlet failed = 0;\n\nfunction assert(condition: boolean, message: string) {\n  if (condition) {\n    console.log(`✅ [PASS] ${message}`);\n    passed++;\n  } else {\n    console.error(`❌ [FAIL] ${message}`);\n    failed++;\n  }\n}\n\nconst BOOKS_ROOT = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'content/curriculum/books');\n\ninterface LessonEntry {\n  title: string;\n  printedPage: number | null;\n  unitName: string;\n  unitNumber: number;\n  pages: number[];\n  text: string;\n}\n\nfunction booksWithLessons(): string[] {\n  if (!fs.existsSync(BOOKS_ROOT)) return [];\n  return fs\n    .readdirSync(BOOKS_ROOT)\n    .filter((e) => fs.existsSync(path.join(BOOKS_ROOT, e, 'lessons.json')));\n}\n\nfunction loadLessons(bookId: string): Record<string, LessonEntry> {\n  const p = path.join(BOOKS_ROOT, bookId, 'lessons.json');\n  return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8'));\n}\n\nfunction manifestPages(bookId: string): number {\n  const p = path.join(BOOKS_ROOT, bookId, 'manifest.json');\n  const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8'));\n  return m.pages;\n}\n\nfunction runLessonTextTests() {\n  console.log('--- LESSON TEXT ---\\n');\n\n  const ids = booksWithLessons();\n  assert(ids.length >= 15, `lesson text is committed for the rendered books (${ids.length})`);\n\n  let totalLessons = 0;\n  let totalChars = 0;\n\n  for (const id of ids) {\n    const lessons = loadLessons(id);\n    const pages = manifestPages(id);\n    const keys = Object.keys(lessons);\n\n    assert(keys.length > 0, `${id} has lessons`);\n    totalLessons += keys.length;\n\n    // Every lesson must carry real text; an empty one means the girl taps a\n    // lesson and reads nothing, which is the failure this whole change fixes.\n    const empty = keys.filter((k) => !lessons[k].text || lessons[k].text.trim().length < 40);\n    assert(\n      empty.length === 0,\n      `${id} every lesson has real text (${empty.length} empty of ${keys.length})`,\n    );\n\n    // Keys are image pages the reader can actually open.\n    const badKeys = keys.filter((k) => {\n      const n = Number(k);\n      return !Number.isInteger(n) || n < 1 || n > pages;\n    });\n    assert(badKeys.length === 0, `${id} lesson keys are valid page numbers`);\n\n    // A lesson's pages must all be inside the book.\n    const badPages = keys.filter((k) =>\n      lessons[k].pages.some((p) => p < 1 || p > pages),\n    );\n    assert(badPages.length === 0, `${id} lesson page ranges stay inside the book`);\n\n    for (const k of keys) {\n      const text = lessons[k].text;\n      totalChars += text.length;\n\n      // Decorative lettering and dot leaders are not lesson content.\n      const lines = text.split('\\n').filter((l) => l.trim());\n      const dotted = lines.filter((l) => (l.match(/\\./g) || []).length > l.length / 2);\n      if (dotted.length > 0) {\n        assert(false, `${id} p${k} has no dot-leader runs (${dotted.length} lines)`);\n      }\n\n      const fragmentRows = lines.filter(\n        (l) => l.split(/\\s+/).length >= 5 && l.split(/\\s+/).every((w) => w.length <= 2),\n      );\n      if (fragmentRows.length > 0) {\n        assert(false, `${id} p${k} has no decorative letter rows (${fragmentRows.length})`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  console.log(`   ${totalLessons} lessons, ${totalChars} characters of real text`);\n\n  // Arabic text must contain Arabic letters, and be in logical order: a line\n  // reversed from visual order reads backwards, which is the defect the\n  // coordinate-based extractor fixes.\n  const arabicBooks = ids.filter((id) => {\n    const m = JSON.parse(\n      fs.readFileSync(path.join(BOOKS_ROOT, id, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8'),\n    );\n    return m.language === 'ar';\n  });\n  assert(arabicBooks.length > 0, `Arabic books are among those with lesson text (${arabicBooks.length})`);\n\n  for (const id of arabicBooks) {\n    const lessons = loadLessons(id);\n    const joined = Object.values(lessons).map((l) => l.text).join('\\n');\n    const arabicChars = (joined.match(/[\\u0600-\\u06FF]/g) || []).length;\n    assert(\n      arabicChars > joined.length * 0.3,\n      `${id} lesson text is predominantly Arabic (${Math.round((arabicChars / joined.length) * 100)}%)`,\n    );\n  }\n\n  // The specific book from the report must be fully readable.\n  const arabic = loadLessons('arabic-g5-t1');\n  const arabicLessons = Object.values(arabic);\n  assert(\n    arabicLessons.length >= 25,\n    `arabic-g5-t1 exposes all its lessons as text (${arabicLessons.length})`,\n  );\n  const realText = arabicLessons.filter((l) => l.text.length > 200);\n  assert(\n    realText.length >= 20,\n    `arabic-g5-t1 lessons carry substantial text (${realText.length} over 200 chars)`,\n  );\n}\n\nfunction main() {\n  runLessonTextTests();\n  console.log(`\\n=== LESSON TEXT: ${passed} passed, ${failed} failed ===`);\n  if (failed > 0) process.exit(1);\n}\n\nmain();\n",

That matters: the vision\nAPI is limited to a handful of requests per day, and the text layer is both free\nand more faithful than OCR.\n\nOutput: content/curriculum/books/<bookId>/lessons.json, keyed by the lesson's\nfirst image page. Each entry holds the lesson title, the pages it spans, and the\ncleaned text. Lessons come from the book's own فهرس (the manifest units), so the\nlist matches what the book prints — nothing is invented.\n\n    python3 tools/curriculum/extract_lessons.py [--books-dir D] [--pdf-dir D] [book-id ...]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport os\nimport re\nimport sys\nimport unicodedata\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nsys.path.insert(0, HERE)\n\nimport fitz  # noqa: E402  (PyMuPDF)\n\n# A lesson in these books runs a handful of pages. The page images stay available, so a\n# capped range loses nothing the girl cannot still read in the book view.\nMAX_LESSON_PAGES = 8\n\n# Dot leaders, running heads, and bare page numbers carry no lesson content.\nPAGE_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*[-–—]?\\s*\\d{1,4}\\s*[-–—]?\\s*$\")\nLEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"[.·\\u2026]{3,}\")\n\n\ndef clean_word(word: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Repair a single extracted word (ligatures are stored reversed).\"\"\"\n    from toc import fix_lam_alef, norm\n\n    w = norm(word).replace(\"\\x03\", \" \").replace(\"\\x07\", \" \").strip()\n    w = LEADER_RE.sub(\"\", w)\n    return fix_lam_alef(w)\n\n\ndef page_text(page, rtl: bool) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Read a page as lines of words, ordered by position.\n\n    These PDFs store Arabic glyph runs out of reading order, so the text layer's\n    own sequence is unreliable.  "new_str": "    words = page.get_text(\"words\")  # (x0, y0, x1, y1, text, block, line, word)\n    if not words:\n        return \"\"\n\n    lines: list[list[tuple]] = []\n    for x0, y0, x1, y1, text, *_ in words:\n        if not text.strip():\n            continue\n        # Same baseline if the tops are within a couple of points.\n        for line in lines:\n            if abs(line[0][0] - y0) <= 2.5:\n                line.append((x0, x1, y1 - y0, text))\n                break\n        else:\n            lines.append([(y0, \"\"), (x0, x1, y1 - y0, text)])\n\n    # Sort lines top-to-bottom, then words in reading direction.\n    lines.sort(key=lambda ln: ln[0][0])\n    out = []\n    for line in lines:\n        pairs = list(line[1:])\n        if not pairs:\n            continue\n        pairs.sort(key=lambda t: -t[0] if rtl else t[0])\n\n        # These PDFs split a single Arabic word into several fragments. Fragments\n        # of one word sit almost flush against each other; a real space is a wide\n        # gap. Joining on that gap turns \"إ ج ا ز ا ت\" back into \"إجازات\".\n        height = max((p[2] for p in pairs), default=10) or 10\n        space_gap = max(4.0, height * 0.35)\n        words: list[str] = []\n        for i, (x0, x1, _h, text) in enumerate(pairs):\n            cleaned = clean_word(text)\n            if not cleaned:\n                continue\n            if words and i > 0:\n                prev = pairs[i - 1]\n                gap = (prev[0] - x1) if rtl else (x0 - prev[1])\n                if gap <= space_gap:\n                    words[-1] = words[-1] + cleaned\n                    continue\n            words.append(cleaned)\n        if not words:\n            continue\n        text = re.sub(r\"[ \\t]{2,}\", \" \", \" \".join(words)).strip()\n        # Placeholder rows (\".\" under each blank) and rule lines carry no words.\n        if not re.search(r\"[\\w\\u0600-\\u06FF]\", text):\n            continue\n        # Decorative lettering (a title stretched with kashida) comes through as\n        # each letter doubled — \"أَ أَ ك ك ت ت\" — so most words repeat. Real prose\n        # does not look like that.\n        if len(words) >= 5 and len(set(words)) <= len(words) / 2:\n            continue\n        if text and not PAGE_NUMBER_RE.match(text):\n            out.append(text)\n    return \"\\n\".join(out)",

 "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Extract the readable text of each lesson from a rendered book's source PDF.\n\nAmina shows the real ministry books as page images. Page images alone are not\nenough to *study* from: the girl needs the lesson's actual text so she can read\nit, highlight a sentence, and ask Miss Nour about it.\n\nThese PDFs carry a real text layer, so the lesson text can be recovered exactly\nas printed, offline, with no model call and no quota. That matters: the vision\nAPI is limited to a handful of requests per day, and the text layer is both free\nand more faithful than OCR.\n\nOutput: content/curriculum/books/<bookId>/lessons.json, keyed by the lesson's\nfirst image page. Each entry holds the lesson title, the pages it spans, and the\ncleaned text. The page images stay available, so a\n# capped range loses nothing the girl cannot still read in the book view.\nMAX_LESSON_PAGES = 8\n\n# Dot leaders, running heads, and bare page numbers carry no lesson content.\nPAGE_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*[-–—]?\\s*\\d{1,4}\\s*[-–—]?\\s*$\")\nLEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"[.·\\u2026]{3,}\")\n\n\ndef clean_word(word: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Repair a single extracted word (ligatures are stored reversed).\"\"\"\n    from toc import fix_lam_alef, norm\n\n    w = norm(word).replace(\"\\x03\", \" \").replace(\"\\x07\", \" \").strip()\n    w = LEADER_RE.sub(\"\", w)\n    return fix_lam_alef(w)\n\n\ndef page_text(page, rtl: bool) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Read a page as lines of words, ordered by position.\n\n    These PDFs store Arabic glyph runs out of reading order, so the text layer's\n    own sequence is unreliable. Sorting each visual line by x-position recovers\n    the order a reader would use: right-to-left for Arabic, left-to-right for\n    English. Grouping is by y, so a line is whatever shares a baseline.\n    \"\"\"\n    words = page.get_text(\"words\")  # (x0, y0, x1, y1, text, block, line, word)\n    if not words:\n        return \"\"\n\n    lines: list[list[tuple]] = []\n    for x0, y0, x1, y1, text, *_ in words:\n        if not text.strip():\n            continue\n        # Same baseline if the tops are within a couple of points.\n        for line in lines:\n            if abs(line[0][0] - y0) <= 2.5:\n                line.append((x0, x1, y1 - y0, text))\n                break\n        else:\n            lines.append([(y0, \"\"), (x0, x1, y1 - y0, text)])\n\n    # Sort lines top-to-bottom, then words in reading direction.\n    lines.sort(key=lambda ln: ln[0][0])\n    out = []\n    for line in lines:\n        pairs = list(line[1:])\n        if not pairs:\n            continue\n        pairs.sort(key=lambda t: -t[0] if rtl else t[0])\n        words = [clean_word(w) for _x, _x1, _h, w in pairs]\n        words = [w for w in words if w]\n        if not words:\n            continue\n        text = re.sub(r\"[ \\t]{2,}\", \" \", \" \".join(words)).strip()\n        # Placeholder rows (\".\" under each blank) and rule lines carry no words.\n        if not re.search(r\"[\\w\\u0600-\\u06FF]\", text):\n            continue\n        # A title stretched with kashida comes through as each letter doubled —\n        # \"ع ع ر ر ف ف ت ت\" — so nearly every word repeats the one before it. 1) * 0.6:\n                continue\n        if text and not PAGE_NUMBER_RE.match(text):\n            out.append(text)\n    return \"\\n\".join(out)\n\n\ndef flatten_lessons(units: list) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Every lesson in binding order, carrying the unit it belongs to.\"\"\"\n    flat = []\n    for ui, unit in enumerate(units):\n        name = (unit.get(\"unit\") or unit.get(\"name\") or \"\").strip()\n        for lesson in unit.get(\"lessons\") or []:\n            page = lesson.get(\"page\")\n            if not isinstance(page, int) or page < 1:\n                continue\n            flat.append({\n                \"title\": (lesson.get(\"title\") or \"\").strip(),\n                \"page\": page,\n                \"printedPage\": lesson.get(\"printedPage\"),\n                \"unitName\": name,\n                \"unitNumber\": ui + 1,\n            })\n    flat.sort(key=lambda x: x[\"page\"])\n    return flat\n\n\ndef extract_book(pdf_path: str, manifest: dict, out_dir: str) -> dict | None:\n    lessons = flatten_lessons(manifest.get(\"units\") or [])\n    if not lessons:\n        return None\n\n    rtl = manifest.get(\"language\") == \"ar\"\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)\n    total = manifest.get(\"pages\") or doc.page_count\n    entries = {}\n\n    for i, lesson in enumerate(lessons):\n        start = lesson[\"page\"]\n        next_start = lessons[i + 1][\"page\"] if i + 1 < len(lessons) else total + 1\n        end = min(next_start - 1, start + MAX_LESSON_PAGES - 1, total)\n\n        chunks, used = [], []\n        for p in range(start, end + 1):\n            if p - 1 >= doc.page_count:\n                break\n            t = page_text(doc[p - 1], rtl)\n            if t:\n                chunks.append(t)\n                used.append(p)\n\n        entries[str(start)] = {\n            \"title\": lesson[\"title\"],\n            \"printedPage\": lesson[\"printedPage\"],\n            \"unitName\": lesson[\"unitName\"],\n            \"unitNumber\": lesson[\"unitNumber\"],\n            \"pages\": used,\n            \"text\": text,\n            # Opener and picture pages carry no prose. res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-cache');\n    res.json({ books });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/manifest', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'manifest.json'), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'book_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/pages/:file', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId, file } = req.params;\n  if res.sendFile(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist', 'index.html'));\n  });\n}\n\napp.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {\n  console.log(`AI School Companion Server running on http://0.0.0.0:${PORT}`);\n});\n",
 "new_content": "import express from 'express';\nimport dotenv from 'dotenv';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport fs from 'fs';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\n\ndotenv.config();\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst app = express();\nconst PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;\n\napp.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }));\n\n// AI access via the Gemini REST API.\n// The @google/genai SDK misclassifies Google's newer \"AQ.\" authentication keys\n// as OAuth access tokens and returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, while\n// the same key authenticates correctly over REST. (.env is gitignored.)\\n'\n  );\n}\n\nclass GeminiRequestError extends Error {\n  status: number;\n  constructor(status: number, message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n// Preferred text models, tried in order.         'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n          'x-goog-api-key': apiKey,\n        },\n        body: JSON.stringify(payload),\n      });\n      const json: any = await resp.json().catch(() => }\n    throw lastError ?? new GeminiRequestError(500, 'Gemini request failed');\n  },\n};\n\n/** Extract plain text from a generateContent response. */\nfunction geminiText(response: any): string {\n  const parts = response?.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts;\n  if (!Array.isArray(parts)) return '';\n  return parts\n    .map((p: any) => (typeof p?.text === 'string' ? p.text : ''))\n    .join('')\n Do not hallucinate or invent subjects that the student did not attend or mention.\n2. If the student explicitly names a subject not in the timetable, capture it accurately.\n3. Extract homework with clear subject, description, and due date if stated.\n4. If input is vague or brief, mark detectedConfidence as \"partial\" or \"vague\".\n5. Return JSON ONLY matching this exact structure:\n{\n  \"lessonsCovered\": [\n    { \"subject\": \"string\", \"topic\": \"string (optional)\", \"notes\": \"string (optional)\" }\n  ],\n  \"homeworkAssigned\": [\n    { \"subject\": \"string\", \"description\": \"string\", \"dueDate\": \"string (optional)\" }\n  ],\n  \"notes\": \"string (optional)\",\n  \"detectedConfidence\": \"high\" | \"partial\" | \"vague\",\n  \"isSilence\": boolean,\n  \"isVague\": boolean\n}\n`.trim();\n\n    const response = await gemini.generateContent({\n      model: process.env.GEMINI_MODEL || DEFAULT_TEXT_MODEL,\n      contents: [{ role: 'user', parts: [{ text: trimmedInput }] }],\n      config: {\n        systemInstruction,\n        responseMimeType: 'application/json',\n      },\n    });\n    const responseText = geminiText(response);\n\n    const text = responseText || '{}';\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(text);\n\n    res.json({\n      lessonsCovered: parsed.lessonsCovered || [],\n      homeworkAssigned: parsed.homeworkAssigned || [],\n      notes: parsed.notes || trimmedInput,\n      detectedConfidence: parsed.detectedConfidence || 'partial',\n      isSilence: Boolean(parsed.isSilence),\n      isVague: Boolean(parsed.isVague),\n      source: 'gemini',\n    });\n  } catch (error: any) {\n    console.error('Reconstruct Day API Error:', error);\n    res.json({\n      lessonsCovered: [],\n      homeworkAssigned: [],\n      notes: req.body?.studentInput || '',\n      detectedConfidence: 'vague',\n      isSilence: false,\n      isVague: true,\n      degraded: true,\n      source: 'error_fallback',\n    });\n  }\n});\n\n// Curriculum library: light book pages + manifests, served from a\n// CDN-friendly route. Page filenames are content-stable, so they can be cached\n// immutably; the client downloads one book on demand and keeps it offline.\nconst CURRICULUM_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, 'content', 'curriculum');\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/index', (_req, res) => {\n  const dir = path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books');\n  fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }, (err, entries) => {\n    if (err) return res.status(503).json({ error: 'curriculum_unavailable' });\n    const books = [];\n    for (const e of entries) {\n      if (!e.isDirectory()) continue;\n      try {\n        const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, e.name, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8'));\n        books.push({\n          id: m.id, subject: m.subject, language: m.language, term: m.term,\n          pages: m.pages, bytes: m.bytes, width: m.width,\n          unitCount: (m.units || []).length,\n        });\n      } catch { /* skip an unreadable book rather than fail the list */ }\n    }\n    res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-cache');\n    res.json({ books });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/manifest', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'manifest.json'), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'book_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/pages/:file', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId, file } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  if (!/^\\d{4}\\.webp$/.test(file)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_page' });\n  // Content is immutable per filename, so the device may cache it indefinitely.\n  res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable');\n  res.type('image/webp');\n  res.sendFile(path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'pages', file), (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'page_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\n// Lesson text pulled from the book's own text layer, keyed by image page.\n// Serving it separately keeps the page images cacheable and lets the reader\n// show a lesson's text without waiting on the whole book.\napp.get('/api/curriculum/:bookId/lessons', (req, res) => {\n  const { bookId } = req.params;\n  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(bookId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'bad_id' });\n  const file = path.join(CURRICULUM_ROOT, 'books', bookId, 'lessons.json');\n  res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=86400');\n  res.sendFile(file, (err) => {\n    if (err) res.status(404).json({ error: 'lessons_not_found' });\n  });\n});\n\n// Dev vs Prod server setup\nif (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {\n  const { createServer: createViteServer } = await import('vite');\n  const vite = await createViteServer({\n    server: { middlewareMode: true },\n    appType: 'spa',\n  });\n  app.use(vite.middlewares);\n} else {\n  app.use(express.static(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist')));\n  app.get('*', (_req, res) => {\n    res.sendFile(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist', 'index.html'));\n  });\n}\n\napp.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {\n  console.log(`AI School Companion Server running on http://0.0.0.0:${PORT}`);\n});\n",

 "new_str": "def _parse_number_band(doc, page_index: int, offset: int) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Layout E (Religious Education, some second-term books): a contents page whose\n    lesson titles sit in a right-hand column and whose page ranges sit in a\n    left-hand column, each range printed right-to-left (\"٣١-٧\" is pages 7 to 31).\n\n    Titles often wrap onto the lines above their page range, so a row with\n    letters and no number is held and prepended to the next numbered row.\n    A row is only accepted when it carries both a number and real title text,\n    which keeps decorative rules and the page-number grid out of the contents.\n    \"\"\"\n    page = doc[page_index]\n    width = page.rect.width\n    number_band = width * 0.35\n\n    rows: dict[int, list] = {}\n    for w in page.get_text(\"words\"):\n        if not w[4].strip():\n            continue\n        rows.setdefault(round((w[1] + w[3]) / 2 / 4), []).append((w[0], w[2], w[4]))\n\n    entries: list[dict] = []\n    pending: list[str] = []\n\n    for key in sorted(rows):\n        row = sorted(rows[key], key=lambda t: -t[0])  # right-to-left\n        nums, titles = [], []\n        for x0, x1, text in row:\n            bare = digits(text).strip(\" .-|–(),«»:\")\n            if bare.isdigit():\n                nums.append(int(bare))\n            elif LETTER_RE.search(text):\n                titles.append(text)\n\n        if not nums:\n            # Letters with no page number: a wrapped title line, or a unit\n            # heading. Headings start a new unit and are not lesson titles.\n            if titles:\n                joined = \" \".join(titles)\n                if UNIT_RE.search(joined):\n                    entries.append({\"__unit__\": clean_title(joined, reverse=False)})\n                else:\n                    pending.extend(titles)\n            continue\n\n        title = clean_title(\" \".join(pending + titles), reverse=False)\n        pending = []\n        if not title or not has_title_text(title):\n            continue\n        if len(LETTER_RE.findall(title)) < len(re.findall(r\"\\d\", title)) + 2:\n            continue\n        # A range reads right-to-left, so the smallest number is the first page.\n        entries.append(_entry(min(nums), title, offset, doc.page_count))\n\n    return entries if len(entries) >= 4 else []\n\n\ndef _page_from_tokens(tokens: list[str]) -> Optional[int]:",

Walk back up to two lines,\n    skipping reversed-duplicate echoes and bare labels like \"الدرس الأوّل:\".\n    \"\"\"\n    for k in (j - 1, j - 2):\n        if k < 0:\n            break\n        cand = lines[k].strip()\n        if not cand or not has_title_text(cand):\n            continue\n        if LABEL_RE.match(cand):\n            continue\n        if k - 1 >= 0 and _is_echo(cand, lines[k - 1]):\n            continue\n        title = clean_title(dedupe_echo_line(cand), reverse=False)\n        if title and has_title_text(title):\n            return title\n    return None\n\n\ndef _entry(printed: int, title: str, offset: int, page_count: int) -> dict:\n    resolved = printed - 1 + offset\n    return {\n        \"title\": title,\n        \"printedPage\": printed,\n        \"page\": resolved if 0 < resolved <= page_count else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef _attach(units: list, current: Optional[dict], entry: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Append an entry to the open unit, opening a default one if needed.\"\"\"\n    if current is None:\n        current = {\"unit\": \"المحتوى\", \"lessons\": []}\n        units.append(current)\n    current[\"lessons\"].append(entry)\n    return current\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import json\n    import sys\n\n    for p in sys.argv[1:]:\n        r = parse_toc(p)\n        print(f\"\\n=== {p}  offset={r['offset']}  units={len(r['units'])} ===\")\n        for u in r[\"units\"]:\n            print(f\"  {u['unit']}\")\n            for l in u[\"lessons\"][:6]:\n                print(f\"     p{l['printedPage']:>4} (pdf {l['page']})  {l['title']}\")\n",
 "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDeterministic table-of-contents extraction.\n\nThe ministry PDFs carry a real text layer, so contents can be read directly —\nno OCR, no vision API, no quota. Two quirks have to be undone first:\n\n1. Arabic lines are stored in visual order, i.e. with the word order reversed.\n   Reversing the words restores logical Arabic.\n2. The lam-alef ligature is decomposed into \"ا\" + \"ل\" + \"ا\" style sequences\n   (\"األ\" for \"الأ\"). These are repaired by table.\n\nPage numbers in the contents are the *printed* numbers. The offset to the PDF\npage index is detected per book by finding the most common difference between\na page's printed number and its position.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport fitz\n\n# Ligature repairs: NFKC leaves these broken, so fix them explicitly.\nLIGATURES = [\n    (\"األ\", \"الأ\"), (\"اإل\", \"الإ\"), (\"اآل\", \"الآ\"),\n    (\"ألا\", \"ألا\"), (\"إل\", \"إل\"),\n]\n\nARABIC_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\u0600-\\u06FF]\")\n# Arabic-Indic (0-9) and Extended Arabic-Indic digits -> ASCII.\nDIGITS = str.maketrans(\"٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹\",\n                       \"01234567890123456789\")\n\n\ndef digits(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Convert Arabic-Indic numerals to ASCII.\"\"\"\n    return unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s).translate(DIGITS)\n# \"12. . . . . . . title\" — number, dot leader, then the title.\nENTRY_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\d{1,4})\\s*\\.\\s*(?:\\.\\s*){2,}\\s*\\x03?\\s*(.+?)\\s*$\", re.M)\nTITLE_LEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"^(.*?)\\x03[\\s.]*(?:\\.\\s*){2,}(\\d{1,4})\\s*$\", re.M)\nENGLISH_UNIT_RE = re.compile(r\"^(Unit\\s+\\d+\\s*[:.].*|Theme\\s+\\d+\\s*\\|.*)$\")\nUNIT_RE = re.compile(r\"(الوحدة|المحور|الوحده)\")\nDOT_LEADER_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\\.{2,}[\\s.\\u00b7\\u2026]*\")\n\n\ndef norm(s: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalise and repair Arabic extracted from these PDFs.\"\"\"\n    s = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", s)\n    for bad, good in LIGATURES:\n        s = s.replace(bad, good)\n    return s\n\n\ndef fix_visual_order(line: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"These PDFs store Arabic words in visual order. Reverse the words.\"\"\"\n    if not ARABIC_RE.search(line):\n        return line\n    words = line.split()\n    return \" \".join(reversed(words))\n\n\n# Letters that can precede the definite article (و ف ب ك ل + أ لل). A mid-word\n# \"ال\" after one of these is a real article and must be left alone.\nPREFIX_LETTERS = set(\"وفبكلأ\")\n\n\ndef fix_lam_alef(word: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    The lam-alef ligature is stored reversed as \"ال\" instead of \"لا\".\n    Repair only mid-word occurrences, and never a prefixed article\n    (بالمدرسة, والكتاب stay intact).\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(word) < 3 or ARABIC_RE.search(word) is None:\n        return word\n    # Protect a leading definite article, including after a prefix letter.\n    protected = 0\n    if word.startswith(\"ال\"):\n        protected = 2\n    elif len(word) > 2 and word[0] in PREFIX_LETTERS and word[1:3] == \"ال\":\n        protected = 3\n    head, tail = word[:protected], word[protected:]\n    return head + tail.replace(\"ال\", \"لا\")\n\n\ndef clean_title(raw: str, reverse: bool = True) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Reverse defaults to True for dot-leader books, whose lines are stored in\n    visual order. Social Studies' primary lines are already logical, so its\n    caller passes reverse=False.\n    \"\"\"\n    raw = raw.replace(\"\\x03\", \" \").strip()\n    if reverse:\n        raw = fix_visual_order(raw)\n    # A colon that ended up attached to the wrong side after reversal.\n    raw = re.sub(r\"\\s+:\", \":\", raw)\n    raw = re.sub(r\":(\\S)\", r\": \\1\", raw)\n    # Unit headings read \"الوحدة: الأولى …\" once reversed; the colon belongs\n    # after the ordinal: \"الوحدة الأولى: …\".\n    m = re.match(r\"^(الوحدة|المحور)\\s*:\\s*(\\S+)\\s*(.*)$\", raw)\n    if m:\n        rest = f\" {m.group(3)}\" if m.group(3) else \"\"\n        raw = f\"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}:{rest}\"\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s{2,}\", \" \", raw).strip(\" .\")\n\n\ndef _toks(s: str) -> list[str]:\n    return [w.strip(\":\") for w in s.split()]\n\n\ndef dedupe_echo_line(line: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Some heading lines carry the title twice: once correct and once reversed,\n    run together. When the halves are reverses of each other, keep the one that\n    starts with a unit label.\n    \"\"\"\n    words = line.split()\n    if len(words) < 4 or len(words) % 2:\n        return line\n    h = len(words) // 2\n    # A doubled label (\"الوحدة … الوحدة\") means the echo is run together.\n    for lab in (\"الوحدة\", \"المحور\"):\n        if line.count(lab) >= 2:\n            # Interleaved primary+echo: keep the label and its ordinal only.\n            m = re.search(lab + r\"\\s+(\\S+)\", line)\n            return f\"{lab} {m.group(1)}\".strip(\" :\") if m else lab\n    if _toks(\" \".join(words[h:])) == list(reversed(_toks(\" \".join(words[:h])))):\n        first, second = \" \".join(words[:h]), \" \".join(words[h:])\n        for cand in (second, first):\n            if re.match(r\"^(الوحدة|المحور|مراجعة)\", cand):\n                return cand\n        return first\n    return line\n\n\n# Letters only — excludes digits. Covers Arabic and Latin, since the English\n# books have their own contents pages.\nLETTER_RE = re.compile(r\"[\\u0621-\\u064A A-Za-z]\")\n\n\ndef has_title_text(s: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A real title has at least two letters, not just numerals.\"\"\"\n    return len(LETTER_RE.findall(s)) >= 2\n\n\ndef _toc_pages(doc) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Pages near the front that look like a table of contents. Two shapes:\n    a dot-leader list, or a contents heading with many bare numerals.\n    \"\"\"\n    hits = []\n    for i in range(min(12, doc.page_count)):\n        t = norm(doc[i].get_text())\n        if \"قائمة المحتوى\" in t or \"المحتويات\" in t or \"قائمة املحتوى\" in t:\n            hits.append(i)\n            continue\n        if len(ENTRY_RE.findall(t)) >= 3:\n            hits.append(i)\n            continue\n        # Layout B: several lines that are only a page number.\n        bare = sum(\n            1\n            for l in t.split(\"\\n\")\n            if digits(l).strip(\" .-|\").isdigit() and l.strip()\n        )\n        if bare >= 5 and \"الدرس\" in t:\n            hits.append(i)\n            continue\n        # English books: dot-leader entries after the title.\n        if len(TITLE_LEADER_RE.findall(t)) >= 3 or \"Table of Contents\" in t:\n            hits.append(i)\n            continue\n        # Layout D: two-column contents — a column of page numbers down the\n        # left edge, with titles beside them.\n        if _looks_two_column(doc[i]):\n            hits.append(i)\n    return hits\n\n\ndef _looks_two_column(page) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the left edge holds a column of bare page numbers.\"\"\"\n    width = page.rect.width\n    band = width * 0.32\n    rows: dict[int, bool] = {}\n    for w in page.get_text(\"words\"):\n        if not w[4].strip():\n            continue\n        if w[2] <= band and digits(w[4]).strip(\" .-|–\").isdigit():\n            rows[round((w[1] + w[3]) / 2 / 4)] = True\n    return len(rows) >= 6\n\n\ndef _detect_offset(doc) -> int:\n    \"\"\"\n    Printed page number -> PDF page index offset.\n    Scan pages for a bare number and take the most common difference.\n    \"\"\"\n    diffs = Counter()\n    for i in range(min(60, doc.page_count)):\n        lines = [l.strip() for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\") if l.strip()]\n        # Page numbers usually sit in the first or last couple of lines.\n        for cand in (lines[:2] + lines[-2:]):\n            digits = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", cand).strip(\" .-|\")\n            if digits.isdigit():\n                n = int(digits)\n                if 1 <= n <= doc.page_count:\n                    diffs[(i + 1) - n] += 1\n    return diffs.most_common(1)[0][0] if diffs else 0\n\n\ndef _parse_two_column(doc, page_index: int, offset: int) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Layout D (Arabic Language books): a two-column contents page. Page numbers\n    sit in a narrow left band, titles in the right column at the same height.\n    Text is already in logical order with full diacritics, so nothing is\n    reversed here. Each row pairs a title with the page range beside it.\n    \"\"\"\n    page = doc[page_index]\n    width = page.rect.width\n    words = [w for w in page.get_text(\"words\") if w[4].strip()]\n    if not words:\n        return []\n\n    # The left band is the number column; everything else is the title column.\n    number_band = width * 0.32\n    rows: dict[int, list] = {}\n    for w in words:\n        x0, y0, x1, y1, text = w[0], w[1], w[2], w[3], w[4]\n        rows.setdefault(round((y0 + y1) / 2 / 4), []).append((x0, x1, text))\n\n    entries = []\n    for key in sorted(rows):\n        # Keep the content-stream order: it already yields logical Arabic\n        # (right-to-left) word order, so no sorting is needed.\n        row = rows[key]\n        nums, title_words = [], []\n        for x0, x1, text in row:\n            if x1 <= number_band:\n                nums.append(text)\n            else:\n                title_words.append(text)\n        page_no = _page_from_tokens(nums)\n        title = clean_title(\" \".join(title_words), reverse=False)\n        if page_no is None or not title or not has_title_text(title):\n            continue\n        # Reject rows that are only stray numbers (e.g. a page-range fragment\n        # that drifted past the number band).\n        if len(LETTER_RE.findall(title)) < len(re.findall(r\"\\d\", title)) + 2:\n            continue\n        entries.append(_entry(page_no, title, offset, doc.page_count))\n\n    # A real contents page yields many rows; a stray page does not.\n    return entries if len(entries) >= 6 else []\n\n\ndef _parse_number_band(doc, page_index: int, offset: int) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Layout E (Religious Education, some second-term books): a contents page whose\n    lesson titles sit in a right-hand column and whose page ranges sit in a\n    left-hand column, each range printed right-to-left (\"٣١-٧\" is pages 7 to 31).\n\n    Titles often wrap onto the lines above their page range, so a row with\n    letters and no number is held and prepended to the next numbered row.\n    A row is only accepted when it carries both a number and real title text,\n    which keeps decorative rules and the page-number grid out of the contents.\n    \"\"\"\n    page = doc[page_index]\n    width = page.rect.width\n    number_band = width * 0.35\n\n    rows: dict[int, list] = {}\n    for w in page.get_text(\"words\"):\n        if not w[4].strip():\n            continue\n        rows.setdefault(round((w[1] + w[3]) / 2 / 4), []).append((w[0], w[2], w[4]))\n\n    entries: list[dict] = []\n    pending: list[str] = []\n\n    for key in sorted(rows):\n        row = sorted(rows[key], key=lambda t: -t[0])  # right-to-left\n        nums, titles = [], []\n        for x0, x1, text in row:\n            bare = digits(text).strip(\" .-|–(),«»:\")\n            if bare.isdigit():\n                nums.append(int(bare))\n            elif LETTER_RE.search(text):\n                titles.append(text)\n\n        if not nums:\n            # Letters with no page number: a wrapped title line, or a unit\n            # heading. Headings start a new unit and are not lesson titles.\n            if titles:\n                joined = \" \".join(titles)\n                if UNIT_RE.search(joined):\n                    entries.append({\"__unit__\": clean_title(joined, reverse=False)})\n                else:\n                    pending.extend(titles)\n            continue\n\n        title = clean_title(\" \".join(pending + titles), reverse=False)\n        pending = []\n        if not title or not has_title_text(title):\n            continue\n        if len(LETTER_RE.findall(title)) < len(re.findall(r\"\\d\", title)) + 2:\n            continue\n        # A range reads right-to-left, so the smallest number is the first page.\n        entries.append(_entry(min(nums), title, offset, doc.page_count))\n\n    return entries if len(entries) >= 4 else []\n\n\ndef _page_from_tokens(tokens: list[str]) -> Optional[int]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Page number from the left band. Ranges read right-to-left (\"9 - 6\" is\n    pages 6 to 9), so the lowest number is the page the lesson starts on.\n    \"\"\"\n    found = [int(digits(t).strip(\" .-|–\")) for t in tokens if digits(t).strip(\" .-|–\").isdigit()]\n    return min(found) if found else None\n\n\ndef parse_toc(pdf_path: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Return {\"offset\": int, \"units\": [...], \"confidence\": str}.\n    Two contents layouts occur and both are handled:\n      A) \"12. . . . . .  title\"          (dot leader — Science, Math)\n      B) \"title\" then \"12\" below it      (Social Studies)\n    These PDFs also emit each heading twice, the second copy word-reversed.\n    Layout B therefore skips echo lines, and a page is only accepted when\n    enough entries survive. A page that yields nothing usable is reported as\n    low confidence rather than guessed at.\n    \"\"\"\n    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)\n    try:\n        offset = _detect_offset(doc)\n        units: list[dict] = []\n        current: Optional[dict] = None\n        accepted = 0\n\n        for i in _toc_pages(doc):\n            lines = [norm(l) for l in doc[i].get_text().split(\"\\n\")]\n            lines = [l.strip() for l in lines if l.strip()]\n            page_entries: list[dict] = []\n            seen: set[tuple] = set()\n\n            for j, line in enumerate(lines):\n                # Layout A\n                m = ENTRY_RE.match(line)\n                if m:\n                    title = clean_title(m.group(2))\n                    if title and has_title_text(title):\n                        key = (int(m.group(1)), title)\n                        if key not in seen:\n                            seen.add(key)\n                            page_entries.append(_entry(int(m.group(1)), title, offset, doc.page_count))\n                    continue\n\n                # Layout B: a bare number, title on a preceding line.\n                # Digits in these lines are visual too, so a multi-digit\n                # number must be reversed (\"٦١\" is really 16).\n                num = digits(line).strip(\" .-|\")\n                if num.isdigit() and len(num) <= 3:\n                    if len(num) > 1:\n                        num = num[::-1]\n                    title = _preceding_title(lines, j)\n                    if title:\n                        key = (int(num), title)\n                        if key not in seen:\n                            seen.add(key)\n                            page_entries.append(_entry(int(num), title, offset, doc.page_count))\n                    continue\n\n                # Layout C: \"Title\\x03. . . . . . 12\" — dot-leader after title.\n                m = TITLE_LEADER_RE.match(line)\n                if m:\n                    title = clean_title(m.group(1), reverse=False)\n                    if title and has_title_text(title):\n                        n = int(digits(m.group(2)))\n                        key = (n, title)\n                        if key not in seen:\n                            seen.add(key)\n                            page_entries.append(_entry(n, title, offset, doc.page_count))\n                    continue\n\n            if len(page_entries) < 4 and _looks_two_column(doc[i]):\n                # The flat text had no usable line structure here, so read\n                # this page by coordinates instead.\n                page_entries = _parse_two_column(doc, i, offset)\n\n            # A two-column page also has a flat-text reading, but it is\n            # usually garbled. Prefer whichever reading yields more entries.\n            if _looks_two_column(doc[i]):\n                coord = _parse_two_column(doc, i, offset)\n                if len(coord) > len(page_entries):\n                    page_entries = coord\n\n            if len(page_entries) >= 4:\n                accepted += len(page_entries)\n                for e in page_entries:\n                    current = _attach(units, current, e)\n\n            # Unit / mahwar headings on any contents page.\n            for line in lines:\n                em = ENGLISH_UNIT_RE.match(line.strip())\n                if em:\n                    current = {\"unit\": line.strip(), \"lessons\": []}\n                    units.append(current)\n                    continue\n                if UNIT_RE.search(line) and not ENTRY_RE.match(line):\n                    heading = clean_title(\n                        DOT_LEADER_RE.sub(\" \", dedupe_echo_line(line)), reverse=False\n                    )\n                    if 2 <= len(heading) <= 90:\n                        current = {\"unit\": heading, \"lessons\": []}\n                        units.append(current)\n\n        units = [u for u in units if u[\"lessons\"]]\n\n        return {\n            \"offset\": offset,\n            \"units\": units,\n            \"confidence\": \"high\" if accepted >= 8 else (\"low\" if accepted else \"none\"),\n        }\n    finally:\n        doc.close()\n\n\nLABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"^(الدرس|الوحدة|المحور|الظاهرة|المفهوم|املفهوم|تعلّم|شارك|تساءل|مشروع)\\b\")\n\n\ndef _wordbag(s: str) -> frozenset:\n    return frozenset(re.findall(r\"[\\u0600-\\u06FF]+\", s))\n\n\ndef _is_echo(cand: str, prev: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when cand is a reversed duplicate of prev (a bidi artefact).\"\"\"\n    a, b = _wordbag(cand), _wordbag(prev)\n    if not a or not b:\n        return False\n    return a == b\n\n\ndef _preceding_title(lines: list[str], j: int) -> Optional[str]:\n    \"\"\"\n    The lesson title for the number at lines[j]. Walk back up to two lines,\n    skipping reversed-duplicate echoes and bare labels like \"الدرس الأوّل:\".\n    \"\"\"\n    for k in (j - 1, j - 2):\n        if k < 0:\n            break\n        cand = lines[k].strip()\n        if not cand or not has_title_text(cand):\n            continue\n        if LABEL_RE.match(cand):\n            continue\n        if k - 1 >= 0 and _is_echo(cand, lines[k - 1]):\n            continue\n        title = clean_title(dedupe_echo_line(cand), reverse=False)\n        if title and has_title_text(title):\n            return title\n    return None\n\n\ndef _entry(printed: int, title: str, offset: int, page_count: int) -> dict:\n    resolved = printed - 1 + offset\n    return {\n        \"title\": title,\n        \"printedPage\": printed,\n        \"page\": resolved if 0 < resolved <= page_count else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef _attach(units: list, current: Optional[dict], entry: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Append an entry to the open unit, opening a default one if needed.\"\"\"\n    if current is None:\n        current = {\"unit\": \"المحتوى\", \"lessons\": []}\n        units.append(current)\n    current[\"lessons\"].append(entry)\n    return current\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import json\n    import sys\n\n    for p in sys.argv[1:]:\n        r = parse_toc(p)\n        print(f\"\\n=== {p}  offset={r['offset']}  units={len(r['units'])} ===\")\n        for u in r[\"units\"]:\n            print(f\"  {u['unit']}\")\n            for l in u[\"lessons\"][:6]:\n                print(f\"     p{l['printedPage']:>4} (pdf {l['page']})  {l['title']}\")\n",

def _parse_number_band(doc, page_index, offset):
    page = doc[page_index]
    width = page.rect.width
    number_band = width * 0.35
    rows = {}
    for w in page.get_text("words"):
        if not w[4].strip(): continue
        rows.setdefault(round((w[1]+w[3])/2/4), []).append((w[0], w[2], w[4]))

    units = []
    current = None

        row = sorted(rows[key], key=lambda t: -t[0])  # RTL
        nums, titles = [], []
        for x0, x1, text in row:
            bare = digits(text).strip(" .-|–(),«»:")
            if bare.isdigit():
                nums.append(_rtl_number(text))
            elif LETTER_RE.search(text):
                titles.append(text)
        if not nums:
            if titles:
                joined = " ".join(titles)
                if _is_unit_heading(joined):
                    current = {"unit": clean_title(joined, reverse=False), "lessons": []}
                    units.append(current)
                else:
                    pending.extend(titles)
            continue
        title = clean_title(" ".join(pending + titles), reverse=False)
        pending = []

        entry = _entry(min(nums), title, offset, doc.page_count)
        current = _attach(units, current, entry)

    entries = sum(len(u["lessons"]) for u in units)
    return units if entries >= 4 else []
