### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `47cbe065-de11-4de7-baaf-44f6d368db63` — 2026-10-21T20:00:35.950844

```
Done. Here's what's actually blocking Amina, based on the work order doc plus what I verified and fixed in the code.

## What was broken (and is now fixed)

**1. The book library — this was the real bug, and it was three bugs stacked**

The work order's own diagnosis was that Amina shipped a "demo-sized curriculum." That was correct, and I found the root causes:

- **The app only knew ~40 hand-written lessons for an entire Grade 5 year.** The page images were complete, but the lesson registry was a sample. Every engine around it — pacing, missions, review, mastery, Miss Nour — was scheduling a demo.
- **The Arabic text extraction was scrambling words.** These PDFs store Arabic in *visual* order, so the obvious `get_text()` returns backwards, broken text. My first fix joined words by gap width and merged whole lines into one token (`الكَلِمَاتُالآتِيَةُ...`).
- **One contents-page layout wasn't handled at all**, so the Religious Education books reported *zero* chapters.

**The key discovery: the PDFs have real text layers.** Lesson text and most contents pages need **no AI calls at all**. That matters enormously, because the free Gemini tier is **20 requests per day** and returns HTTP 429.

So I stopped trying to use vision and read the PDFs directly:

| Result | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Real chapters | ~40 hand-written | **426 read from the PDFs** |
| Lesson text | none | **434 lessons, ~1.7M characters** |
| `christian-g5-t2` | 5 junk chapters | 11 correct chapters |
| Books served | 13 | **24** |

**2. Highlight-to-explain now actually works.** `/api/tutor-explain` accepted a highlight and a question and then *ignored both*, returning a generic script. It now answers the specific passage or question, grounded in that lesson's real text. I verified all three modes live against the running server — real model replies, in Egyptian Arabic.

**3. Tests.** `npm test` is green: **435 assertions, 0 failures** across seven suites, including a new 111-assertion lesson-text suite. Type check and build clean.

## What still stops it from being sellable

I want to be straight with you rather than declare victory, because the work order explicitly says not to call it sellable just because the build passes.

1. **Five books are pure image scans — no text layer on any single page.** `calligraphy-g5`, `islamic-g5-t2`, `morals-g5-t1`, `morals-g5-t2`, `profskills-g5-t1`. I verified this by scanning every page. Reading them needs a vision model at roughly one call per page, which is hundreds of calls against a 20/day quota. **This is your decision:** buy quota, or accept these five as page images. I made the app say so honestly instead of inventing contents.

2. **No real school calendar.** The year plan runs on clearly-labelled *assumed* dates. I deliberately kept pacing opt-in — the integrity tests forbid planning against fabricated dates.

3. **The `AMINA5` access code doesn't exist as a gate.** The API key itself works (verified live, real model replies). But if you meant a *licence code* for selling, nothing is built.

4. **FEED and the Nour loop exist and pass their tests, but I never drove them in a browser.** The work order asks for runtime evidence, and I'm not going to claim it without doing it. Same for session resume.

## What I'd do next, in order

Fix #4 first — it's free and it's the gap between "tested" and "proven." Then #2 (send me the school calendar) and #1 (your call on quota).

**Committed on branch `wip/handoff-2026-10-21`** (3 commits, not pushed, nothing merged). The full audit with file-and-line evidence is in `docs/AMINA_REQUIREMENTS_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md`, and I recorded the extraction rules in `AGENTS.md` so nobody re-derives them.

One caveat on my own work: I briefly killed your port 12001 preview server while cleaning up a test process. Both servers are back up and healthy (`12000=200`, `12001=200`) — but that was my error, and worth knowing if you saw a blip.

**reasoning_content:**
```
Both servers restored. Now let me give the user the answer to their actual question: "what is preventing Amina to be a functionable sellable app".

Let me summarize concisely and honestly, based on the work order doc + my audit.

Let me write the final answer. Keep it clear, structured, evidence-based. The user asked me to read the MD file and get back to them.

Key answer: The main blockers are now:
1. 5 image-only scan books (needs paid vision quota or owner decision) — the one genuine content gap left.
2. Real school calendar missing (year plan uses assumed dates).
3. Licence/access code (AMINA5) not implemented as a gate.
4. Browser-level verification of FEED / Nour loop / year plan / session resume not done.

And I fixed: book library, lesson text, highlight-to-explain, chapters (426), tests.

Let me present this well and mention the doc updated + commits.

Reuse the existing scene structure\n(`ReelScene`: `hook` / `explanation` / `example` / `quick_check`) and the\nexisting viewer. Do not build a second reel system.\n\n### 4b. Memorising session — new, and it must be real\n\nOwner's words: \"memorizing session where [Miss Nour] will help Amina to\nmemorize by repeating and writing etc.\"\n\nA genuine memorising flow, not a label:\n\n1. **Listen / repeat** — Miss Nour reads a short unit of the lesson (a line, a\n   verse, a definition, a vocab set), Amina repeats it. Use the existing\n   `voiceService` and `VoiceInputControl`.\n2. **Write** — she writes it. Reuse the existing `TraceCanvas` (already a\n   touch/pointer tracing canvas built for calligraphy) rather than inventing a\n   new drawing surface.\n3. **Recall check** — the line is hidden and she reproduces it; compare.\n4. **Spaced repetition** — what she struggled with is scheduled for review,\n   through the existing review scheduler. Not a separate scheduler.\n\nMust work for Arabic, French and English text, and must be honest about the\nfive image-only books (no text → nothing to memorise → say so).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Miss Nour as the interface (proactive, not a screen)\n\nOwner's words: \"Miss Nour will be the AI interface that handles the app, this\nis the real teacher, so this is where how she measures and how she guides Amina\nthrough the daily interfaces and daily interactions, and she can pop up and\ngive advice and tell her 'see you missed this because of that'.\"\n\nWhat this requires:\n\n- **She is present across the app**, not only inside the NOUR tab. Other\n  screens hand her context instead of opening a disconnected experience\n  (`setCompanionContext`, `setSelectedCurriculumLessonId` already do this).\n- **She measures.** Mastery and evidence come from real activity and feed her\n  view of Amina. `masteryEngine`, `recordEvidence`, `teacherContextEngine`\n  already exist.\n- **She guides.** On HOME she says what to do next and why.\n- **She explains herself.** When Amina missed something, Miss Nour can say\n  *why* — \"you missed this because of that\" — grounded in real evidence\n  (a wrong answer, a skipped lesson, a due review), never a generic nudge.\n- **She pops up, gently.** Proactive help must be dismissible and must never\n  nag. The existing tone rules (no guilt, wellbeing first — see the companion\n  intent handlers for fatigue/frustration) apply to every popup.\n\n**Do not** build a second advisory system. Egyptian curriculum with French-language learning/assessment for Mathematics and Science. Treat this as the current project target unless the owner updates it.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Product vision — locked\n\nAmina is a **personal AI School Companion**, not a conventional LMS, school administration system, or generic chatbot.\n\nThe experience should feel like a polished, modern, visual, mobile-first learning product: smooth, engaging, game-like, and age-appropriate without feeling childish. Do not expose internal pedagogical or engineering terminology to the child.\n\nPrimary navigation is locked to:\n\n- **HOME** — today's learning, schedule, priorities, progress, and next useful action.\n- **FEED** — a real, full-screen, vertically swipeable stream of educational learning items.\n- **LIBRARY** — the student's real curriculum, digital books, lessons, saved content, notes, and folders.\n- **NOUR** — Miss Nour, the AI teacher and the front door to learning.\n\nOther capabilities belong inside these primary areas or in contextual flows. Do not add parallel top-level products or duplicate systems.\n\n## 2. One connected School Brain\n\nThe product must operate as one coherent loop:\n\n**School → Curriculum → Daily Plan → Teaching → Practice → Homework → Review → Mastery/Evidence → Next Action**\n\nAll entry points should connect to the same student context and the same learning state. Do not create separate teacher, curriculum, feed, mastery, homework, or review engines that disagree with one another.\n\n- Miss Nour is the common teaching interface regardless of where the student starts.\n- Amina must be able to select **any available curriculum lesson** and start the same genuine adaptive Miss Nour session for that lesson.\n- Home, Feed, Library/books, homework, review, games, saved content, and progress should hand context into Nour rather than opening disconnected experiences.\n- Learning evidence should influence the next action, practice, review timing, and explanations.\n- Preserve existing working architecture and features. Extend and connect them; do not restart the design or replace working systems without evidence and a specific reason.\n\n## 3. Miss Nour — required teaching loop\n\nNour is contextual, adaptive, and preferably voice-first. The target learning loop is:\n\n1. **Context** — identify the selected lesson, curriculum objective, prior evidence, recent mistakes, and relevant homework/review.\n2. **Diagnose** — determine what the student understands and where the misconception or gap is. Do not merely assign a fixed diagnosis based on the subject name.\n3. **Choose a teaching strategy** — adapt the explanation to the student's actual response and reasoning.\n4. **Teach** — give a clear, age-appropriate explanation grounded in the real lesson and curriculum.\n5. **Practice** — ask targeted questions and provide useful, varied practice.\n6. **Analyze reasoning** — inspect the student's answer and reasoning, not only whether the final answer is correct.\n7. **Recheck/adapt** — change the explanation or difficulty when evidence shows that the student has not understood; do not repeat an identical question as the only recovery strategy.\n8. **Verify outcome** — establish what the student can now do and record evidence. Do not report mastery merely because a session or quiz ended.\n9. **Next action** — recommend the next lesson, retry, homework step, or spaced review based on evidence.\n\nThe loop must have real terminal outcomes and handle partial understanding, repeated mistakes, interruptions, and resuming a session. Internal terms such as diagnosis, mastery, and evidence are implementation concepts; present child-facing language naturally.\n\nVoice should be a first-class interaction, not a decorative microphone. Preserve usable text interaction and accessibility when voice is unavailable.\n\n## 4. FEED — a hard acceptance requirement\n\nA real educational Feed is mandatory. Previous discussions explicitly called out that Feed/reels were still absent after a prior Phase 4 effort; do **not** assume the requirement is met because a route, tab, placeholder, or architecture exists.\n\nThe Feed must be a purposeful, full-screen, vertically swipeable experience containing curriculum-connected items such as:\n\n- Short lessons, visual explanations, and educational reels/micro-lessons.\n- Quick quizzes, practice questions, and misconception-focused challenges.\n- Textbook/lesson prompts and useful homework or review actions.\n- Follow-up content selected from the student's current school plan, learning gaps, and prior evidence.\n- Actions to open the item in Nour, continue learning, save it, or revisit it.\n\nFeed content must be educationally relevant and connected to the real curriculum and student state. Avoid a generic social-media feed, filler cards, fake content, or a scrollable list falsely presented as reels. Saving an item should connect to the Library/saved-content system, not a duplicate store.\n\n**Acceptance test:** From the actual running app, a student can open FEED, swipe vertically through multiple meaningful learning items, interact with them, and launch a contextual Nour session or save/revisit the item. Verify implementation and runtime behavior, not just component existence.\n\n## 5. Curriculum, books, and lesson selection\n\n- Support the actual target curriculum: Egyptian curriculum for the specified French-track context, with Mathematics and Science taught/assessed in French as agreed.\n- Use real curriculum structure and actual available digital books/lesson content. The student should be able to see and access all available subjects and full books, not an arbitrary truncated subset.\n- Do not fabricate curriculum lessons, book contents, timetable entries, or curriculum coverage to make the UI appear complete.\n- Do not introduce a second, parallel curriculum or teacher system.\n- Selecting a lesson from the curriculum/library must start the shared Nour flow with the selected lesson's context.\n- Keep curriculum language and subject labels consistent with the student's actual track and the source material.\n- If a real source/book is missing, unavailable, or not yet integrated, state the limitation and expose a truthful state; do not silently substitute demo material.\n\n## 6. HOME, planning, homework, review, and progress\n\nHOME should provide a clear, useful daily entry point, including the relevant schedule, planned learning, due work, progress, and next action, all sourced from the same student/curriculum state.\n\nRequirements discussed:\n\n- A real timetable/schedule, not hardcoded demo entries.\n- Complete subject coverage; do not arbitrarily cap the displayed subjects at four.\n- Integrated homework and planner context, including photo/handwriting submission and correction where supported by the current architecture.\n- Spaced review based on actual learning evidence and due review items, not hardcoded subject names.\n- Progress and mastery claims supported by recorded evidence.\n- Persistent continuation/resume so the student can return to an interrupted lesson or practice.\n- Games/challenges should serve learning objectives and feed their evidence back into the same learning loop.\n- Like/save/folders/notes and saved content should be connected to the Library rather than isolated implementations.\n\n## 7. Historical audit findings — leads to re-verify, not assumptions\n\nThese are historical findings from earlier audits and may already have changed. Forge must check the current default branch and report the exact current status with file/line/test evidence.\n\n### Audit around commit `695b713` (reported 2026-10-06)\n\nReported strengths:\n- Curriculum service integrated.\n- Adaptive quiz/retry and mastery evidence substantially working.\n\nReported gaps:\n- Demo timetable.\n- Subject list truncated to four.\n- Hardcoded subject names in spaced review.\n- `demo_student` fallback.\n\n### Audit around commit `fc7fdf0` (reported 2026-10-07)\n\nReported strengths:\n- Teacher context and Home → Nour handoff working.\n\nReported gaps:\n- Diagnosis hardcoded by subject.\n- Student reasoning captured but not actually analyzed.\n- Terminal outcomes and the full adaptive loop incomplete.\n- Fake student fallback.\n- Arabic lesson fallback despite the target French-track context.\n- Demo timetable and hardcoded review-subject fallbacks.\n\n### Phase 4 / later product review (reported 2026-10-08)\n\n- Architecture/navigation/intelligence had been upgraded.\n- The actual FEED/reels experience was still missing.\n- Acceptance was therefore **not passed**.\n- A locked requirement was confirmed: choose any curriculum lesson and begin the same genuine adaptive Miss Nour session.\n\nDo not repeat these findings as current facts until verified. Do not add parallel top-level products or duplicate systems.\n\n## 2. One connected School Brain\n\nThe product must operate as one coherent loop:\n\n**School → Curriculum → Daily Plan → Teaching → Practice → Homework → Review → Mastery/Evidence → Next Action**\n\nAll entry points should connect to the same student context and the same learning state. Do not create separate teacher, curriculum, feed, mastery, homework, or review engines that disagree with one another.\n\n- Miss Nour is the common teaching interface regardless of where the student starts.\n- Amina must be able to select **any available curriculum lesson** and start the same genuine adaptive Miss Nour session for that lesson.\n- Home, Feed, Library/books, homework, review, games, saved content, and progress should hand context into Nour rather than opening disconnected experiences.\n- Learning evidence should influence the next action, practice, review timing, and explanations.\n- Preserve existing working architecture and features. Extend and connect them; do not restart the design or replace working systems without evidence and a specific reason.\n\n## 3. Miss Nour — required teaching loop\n\nNour is contextual, adaptive, and preferably voice-first. The target learning loop is:\n\n1. **Context** — identify the selected lesson, curriculum objective, prior evidence, recent mistakes, and relevant homework/review.\n2. **Diagnose** — determine what the student understands and where the misconception or gap is. Do not merely assign a fixed diagnosis based on the subject name.\n3. **Choose a teaching strategy** — adapt the explanation to the student's actual response and reasoning.\n4. **Teach** — give a clear, age-appropriate explanation grounded in the real lesson and curriculum.\n5. **Practice** — ask targeted questions and provide useful, varied practice.\n6. **Analyze reasoning** — inspect the student's answer and reasoning, not only whether the final answer is correct.\n7. **Recheck/adapt** — change the explanation or difficulty when evidence shows that the student has not understood; do not repeat an identical question as the only recovery strategy.\n8. **Verify outcome** — establish what the student can now do and record evidence. Do not report mastery merely because a session or quiz ended.\n9. **Next action** — recommend the next lesson, retry, homework step, or spaced review based on evidence.\n\nThe loop must have real terminal outcomes and handle partial understanding, repeated mistakes, interruptions, and resuming a session. Internal terms such as diagnosis, mastery, and evidence are implementation concepts; present child-facing language naturally.\n\nVoice should be a first-class interaction, not a decorative microphone. Preserve usable text interaction and accessibility when voice is unavailable.\n\n## 4. FEED — a hard acceptance requirement\n\nA real educational Feed is mandatory. Saving an item should connect to the Library/saved-content system, not a duplicate store.\n\n**Acceptance test:** From the actual running app, a student can open FEED, swipe vertically through multiple meaningful learning items, interact with them, and launch a contextual Nour session or save/revisit the item. Do not merely assign a fixed diagnosis based on the subject name.\n3. **Choose a teaching strategy** — adapt the explanation to the student's actual response and reasoning.\n4. **Teach** — give a clear, age-appropriate explanation grounded in the real lesson and curriculum.\n5. **Practice** — ask targeted questions and provide useful, varied practice.\n6. **Analyze reasoning** — inspect the student's answer and reasoning, not only whether the final answer is correct.\n7. **Recheck/adapt** — change the explanation or difficulty when evidence shows that the student has not understood; do not repeat an identical question as the only recovery strategy.\n8. **Verify outcome** — establish what the student can now do and record evidence. Do not report mastery merely because a session or quiz ended.\n9. **Next action** — recommend the next lesson, retry, homework step, or spaced review based on evidence.\n\nThe loop must have real terminal outcomes and handle partial understanding, repeated mistakes, interruptions, and resuming a session. Internal terms such as diagnosis, mastery, and evidence are implementation concepts; present child-facing language naturally.\n\nVoice should be a first-class interaction, not a decorative microphone. Preserve usable text interaction and accessibility when voice is unavailable.\n\n## 4. FEED — a hard acceptance requirement\n\nA real educational Feed is mandatory. Previous discussions explicitly called out that Feed/reels were still absent after a prior Phase 4 effort; do **not** assume the requirement is met because a route, tab, placeholder, or architecture exists.\n\nThe Feed must be a purposeful, full-screen, vertically swipeable experience containing curriculum-connected items such as:\n\n- Short lessons, visual explanations, and educational reels/micro-lessons.\n- Quick quizzes, practice questions, and misconception-focused challenges.\n- Textbook/lesson prompts and useful homework or review actions.\n- Follow-up content selected from the student's current school plan, learning gaps, and prior evidence.\n- Actions to open the item in Nour, continue learning, save it, or revisit it.\n\nFeed content must be educationally relevant and connected to the real curriculum and student state. Avoid a generic social-media feed, filler cards, fake content, or a scrollable list falsely presented as reels. Saving an item should connect to the Library/saved-content system, not a duplicate store.\n\n**Acceptance test:** From the actual running app, a student can open FEED, swipe vertically through multiple meaningful learning items, interact with them, and launch a contextual Nour session or save/revisit the item. Verify implementation and runtime behavior, not just component existence.\n\n## 5. The owner's \"each book is a demo\" complaint was caused\nby false \"Demo Version\" UI labels (now removed) **and** by the tiny lesson\nregistry: ~40 lesson records total, ~24 with `isAvailable: true`, for a whole\nGrade 5 year. Every engine (pacing, missions, review, mastery, Nour loop) works;\nit is scheduling a demo-sized curriculum. See\n`docs/AMINA_REQUIREMENTS_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md` R5.1.\nThe fix is data extraction from the 24 source PDFs, not UI work.\n\n## Year pacing (added 2026-10-21)\n`src/services/pacing/academicPacing.ts` maps any date to the lesson each subject\nis on, over the Egyptian school week (Sun–Thu). Surfaced as the Library's third\ntab (`YearPlanView.tsx`).\n- **Pacing is opt-in.** `planDailyMissions` only paces when given\n  `academicCalendar`. No scheme of work exists in the supplied resources, so the\n  default dates are `isAssumed: true` and the UI says so. Do **not** make pacing\n  automatic with assumed dates — integrity Test 8 forbids planning without a\n  real school signal, and the work order forbids fabricated coverage.\n\n## Voice stop bug (fixed 2026-10-21)\n`cancelSpeech()` paused the `<audio>` element; pause never fires `ended`, so the\npending `speak()` promise never settled, `onEnd` never ran, and the UI's speaking\nflag stuck true forever. Fixed with a generation counter + `pendingSpeechAbort`\nin `voiceService.ts`. Regression tests in\n`src/services/__tests__/pacingAndVoiceStop.test.ts` fail without the fix.\n\n## Curriculum book pipeline\nRender with `tools/curriculum/pipeline.py`, then **link into the repo** with\n`tools/curriculum/link_books.py` — the renderer writes to `AMINA_BOOKS_DIR` but\nthe server reads `content/curriculum/books/<id>/`. Manifests are committed; page\nimages are gitignored (`content/curriculum/books/*/pages`).\n\n## Real lesson text (added 2026-10-21, later same day)\nR5.1 is closed. `tools/curriculum/refill_toc.py --force` re-reads every book's\ntable of contents from the PDFs into its manifest, and\n`tools/curriculum/extract_lessons.py` writes each lesson's real text to\n`content/curriculum/books/<id>/lessons.json`. Together: **426 chapters and 434\nlessons (~1.70M chars)** across 19 books. Both are committed.\n\nKey facts, so this is not re-derived:\n\n* **The PDFs have real text layers.** Lesson text and most contents pages need\n  **no API calls at all**. Always try text extraction before reaching for\n  vision; the owner's free Gemini tier is 20 calls/day and returns HTTP 429.\n* **Arabic here is visually ordered**, so flat `get_text()` scrambles it. Read\n  words by coordinate and sort right-to-left\n  (`extract_lessons.py:page_text`). Word spacing is a real space: do **not**\n  join on a gap threshold, it merges the whole line into one token.\n* A kashida-stretched title comes through as every letter doubled\n  (\"ع ع ر ر ف ف\"). Filter by *adjacent* repeated words, not short words —\n  legitimate letter-spaced words like `إ ج ا ز ا ت` are not decoration.\n* `toc.py` handles dot-leader, bare-number, two-column and (new) range-first\n  layouts. The range-first reader is gated by `_looks_range_first`, which\n  requires a column of page *ranges* (two numbers and a hyphen). Without that\n  gate it misreads dot-leader books and corrupts their chapter lists.\n* **Five books have no text layer on any page** (`calligraphy-g5`,\n  `islamic-g5-t2`, `morals-g5-t1`, `morals-g5-t2`, `profskills-g5-t1`). They\n  stay `structureStatus: \"not_found\"` and the catalog reports them honestly.\n  Reading them needs paid vision quota — an owner decision, not a bug.\n* A lesson whose pages are images only is marked `imageOnly: true` rather than\n  showing a handful of stray words.\n\nInteractive reading: `LessonReader.tsx` shows a lesson's text;\n`/api/tutor-explain` accepts `selectedText` and `userQuestion` so highlighting a\npassage or asking a question is answered from that lesson's real text.\n\nRun `npm test` — it now includes `test:lessons` (111 assertions) and\n`test:books` (82).\n",

### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `5226236e-732f-4b09-a02d-043728b026af` — 2026-10-21T21:55:08.100509

```
Locked down and committed. Here's what I captured.

## The spec is now the reference

`docs/MISS_NOUR_PRODUCT_SPEC.md` — linked from the top of the work order and from `AGENTS.md`, so any agent reads it before touching code.

**One correction I have to flag, because getting it wrong would be damaging.** You said the app is now officially **Miss Nour**. But "Amina" in the codebase currently means two different things, and there are 84 references:

- **Amina = the student** — she types her own name at onboarding, and Miss Nour addresses her as `يا أمينة` throughout.
- **Amina = the app brand** — the page title, the "AI School Companion" labels.

If I renamed all 84, Miss Nour would start calling the student "Miss Nour." So the spec separates them explicitly: **the app becomes Miss Nour; the student stays Amina.** The repo folder also stays `Amina/` — renaming a directory isn't worth the breakage. Tell me if you actually meant the student is renamed too, and I'll change it.

## What the spec locks down

- **Miss Nour is the app, not a feature in it** — one student state, one teaching interface, many activities. No second teacher or second progress system.
- **Library gets a second section, separate from Books**: subjects → the full real lesson list (Lesson 1, 2, 3… the whole subject) → tap a lesson → a menu of what to do with it.
- **The activity menu**: session with Miss Nour, reels, memorising, explain/vocab/exercises, practice, stage, read, open in book.
- **Reels must run on the real lesson text** — today they only work for ~10 hand-written demo concepts.
- **A real memorising session** (repeat → write → recall → spaced review). I verified this does not exist; it's the main new build.
- **The chat item**, where she says "I have a French test tomorrow" and Miss Nour prepares her.

## The most useful thing I found

**A complete ChatGPT-style chat screen already exists and is completely orphaned.** `CompanionChatScreen.tsx`, 732 lines — message list, persistence, wired to `/api/chat`, with intent handling for "don't understand", "test me", fatigue. **Nothing imports it.** So the chat item is mostly a wiring job, not a build.

I put that in a **reuse map (§8)** listing what already exists versus what's genuinely new. Seven things are new; everything else is re-pointing existing work. That matters because you said "rebuild the whole UX" — I've read that as re-pointing the architecture, not rewriting the codebase, and I said so plainly in the spec so you can correct me.

## Three questions I need answered before building

1. **"One after the other"** — auto-advance to the next lesson when one finishes, or an ordered list she taps through?
2. **The five image-only books** — show them as picture-only lessons, or leave them out?
3. **Teaching depth** — the teaching engine needs concepts/objectives/vocabulary, which exist only for the ~40 hand-written lessons. A session on a real book chapter runs from that chapter's real page text: genuine but lighter. Ship broad coverage now and enrich later, or enrich first and ship fewer? I recommend ship broad.

Answer those and I'll start on the new section.

Branch `wip/handoff-2026-10-21`, four commits, nothing pushed or merged.
```

The core idea, in one paragraph\n\nMiss Nour is not a feature inside a school app — **Miss Nour is the app.** She\nis the AI teacher and the single front door. She knows Amina's curriculum, her\nreal books, what she has studied, what she got wrong and what she is about to be\ntested on. Amina opens the app and Miss Nour is there, guiding her through the\nday. Everything else — books, lessons, reels, quizzes, memorising, review — is\nan *activity Miss Nour can run*, not a separate product with its own brain.\n\nThe rule that follows from this: **one student state, one teaching interface,\nmany activities.** Do not build a second teacher, a second curriculum, or a\nsecond progress system.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Navigation\n\nThe bottom bar is the spine. Four items, plus the chat:\n\n| Item | What it is |\n|------|------------|\n| **HOME** | Today. Miss Nour's daily plan, what is due, what to do next. |\n| **FEED** | The daily learning feed (vertical, swipeable) — built *with* Miss Nour, not a social feed. |\n| **LIBRARY** | Books and the real curriculum. Now holds two clearly separate sections (§3). |\n| **NOUR** | Miss Nour herself — the teaching interface. |\n| **CHAT** *(new)* | The free-form chat. See §6. |\n\n`learn` is the current tab id for LIBRARY and `companion` for NOUR — the ids\nstay, only what they contain changes.\n\n**Tension to be honest about:** the owner asked for the whole UX to be \"rebuilt\non this new concept.\" That is a change of **information architecture and entry\npoints**, not a codebase rewrite. The engines (teaching, pacing, mastery,\nreview, feed, reels, stage) already exist and work. We re-point them, we do not\nreplace them. Anything that genuinely must be rewritten gets called out\nexplicitly in §9.\n\n---\n\n## 3. LIBRARY now holds two separate sections\n\nThis is the owner's explicit requirement: the new section must be **other than**\nthe books section.\n\n### 3a. Books (exists — do not regress)\n\nThe real ministry books, page-for-page, downloadable on demand. A book shows\nits own فهرس and its real page images. This is the \"read the actual textbook\"\npath. 24 books are rendered. See §3c for the true text-coverage picture — an\nearlier version of this spec claimed \"five image-only books\" and that was wrong.\n\n### 3b. Subjects & Lessons (NEW — this is the main build)\n\nA second section, separate from Books, organised **by subject**:\n\n1. **Subject list.** Every subject Amina studies, each showing its real lesson\n   count. Plus an \"All subjects\" entry so she can see everything at once.\n   Subjects come from `curriculumService.getSubjectsSummary()`.\n2. **Tap a subject → the full lesson list, in order.**\n   `Lesson 1 — title`, `Lesson 2 — title`, `Lesson 3 — title`… one after\n   another, the whole subject, not a sample.\n   Source of truth is the **real book structure** (`lessons.json` per book,\n   read through `bookCatalog`), because that is where the real 426 chapters\n   live. The hand-written registry only has ~40 lessons and must not be the\n   list she sees.\n3. **Tap a lesson → the activity menu (§4).** This is the key moment: choosing\n   a lesson does not jump straight into one experience. She chooses what to do.\n\nEach lesson row shows its real position and title, and marks where she is\n(studied / not yet / needs review) from real evidence — never a decorative\ntick.\n\n---\n\n## 4. The lesson activity menu\n\nTapping a lesson opens a choice of what to do with **that** lesson. This is the\nowner's core requirement. Every option runs the same lesson context through a\ndifferent activity, and every option records evidence back into the one student\nstate.\n\n| Activity | What it does | Status |\n|----------|--------------|--------|\n| **Session with Miss Nour** | The full adaptive teaching loop on this lesson. | Exists (`TeachingSessionModal`, `teachingSession` engine). |\n| **Study through reels** | Short visual micro-lessons for this lesson. | Partly — `ReelViewer` + `contentGenerator`, but only for ~10 hand-written concepts. **Must be driven by the real lesson text.** See §4a. |\n| **Memorising session** | Repeat and write, to commit to memory. | **Does not exist.** Build it. See §4b. |\n| **Explain / vocabulary / exercises** | Lesson detail: explanation, vocab, exercises. | Exists (`LessonStudyModal`). |\n| **Practice / quiz** | Targeted questions with reasoning analysis. | Exists (`QuizRunner`, `Mission` type `practice`/`quiz`). |\n| **Interactive stage** | Drag-drop, match pairs, sequence, explain-back, voice answer. | Exists (`StageModal`, `stageEngine`, 10 interaction components). |\n| **Read the lesson** | The lesson's real text, with highlight-to-ask. | Exists (`LessonReader`). |\n| **Open in the book** | Jump to the lesson's real pages. | Exists (`BookReader`). |\n\nThe menu is the product. Keep it consistent, keep every option grounded in the\nselected lesson, and keep every option's result flowing into the same evidence.\n\n### 4a. Reels must address the particular lesson\n\nOwner's words: \"the reels can be adjusted to address this particular lesson.\"\n\nToday `getReelForConcept(conceptId)` only works for the ~10 hand-written demo\nconcepts, so reels cannot cover the real curriculum. The fix: generate the reel\nfrom the **selected lesson's real text** (the `lessons.json` text already\nextracted) — hook, explanation, example, quick check — instead of requiring a\nhand-authored concept. Reuse the existing scene structure\n(`ReelScene`: `hook` / `explanation` / `example` / `quick_check`) and the\nexisting viewer. Do not build a second reel system.\n\n### 4b. Memorising session — new, and it must be real\n\nOwner's words: \"memorizing session where [Miss Nour] will help Amina to\nmemorize by repeating and writing etc.\"\n\nA genuine memorising flow, not a label:\n\n1. **Listen / repeat** — Miss Nour reads a short unit of the lesson (a line, a\n   verse, a definition, a vocab set), Amina repeats it. Use the existing\n   `voiceService` and `VoiceInputControl`.\n2. **Write** — she writes it. Reuse the existing `TraceCanvas` (already a\n   touch/pointer tracing canvas built for calligraphy) rather than inventing a\n   new drawing surface.\n3. **Recall check** — the line is hidden and she reproduces it; compare.\n4. **Spaced repetition** — what she struggled with is scheduled for review,\n   through the existing review scheduler. Not a separate scheduler.\n\nMust work for Arabic, French and English text, and must be honest about the\nfive image-only books (no text → nothing to memorise → say so).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Miss Nour as the interface (proactive, not a screen)\n\nOwner's words: \"Miss Nour will be the AI interface that handles the app, this\nis the real teacher, so this is where how she measures and how she guides Amina\nthrough the daily interfaces and daily interactions, and she can pop up and\ngive advice and tell her 'see you missed this because of that'.\"\n\nWhat this requires:\n\n- **She is present across the app**, not only inside the NOUR tab. Other\n  screens hand her context instead of opening a disconnected experience\n  (`setCompanionContext`, `setSelectedCurriculumLessonId` already do this).\n- **She measures.** Mastery and evidence come from real activity and feed her\n  view of Amina. `masteryEngine`, `recordEvidence`, `teacherContextEngine`\n  already exist.\n- **She guides.** On HOME she says what to do next and why.\n- **She explains herself.** When Amina missed something, Miss Nour can say\n  *why* — \"you missed this because of that\" — grounded in real evidence\n  (a wrong answer, a skipped lesson, a due review), never a generic nudge.\n- **She pops up, gently.** Proactive help must be dismissible and must never\n  nag. The existing tone rules (no guilt, wellbeing first — see the companion\n  intent handlers for fatigue/frustration) apply to every popup.\n\n**Do not** build a second advisory system. This is the same Miss Nour, given\nmore places to speak.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The chat item\n\nOwner's words: \"one of the items at the bottom bar … opens a chat, a regular\nchat session similar to the ChatGPT interface exactly, where she can tell Miss\nNour what exactly she needs and then Miss Nour replies. If I have a test\ntomorrow in French … Miss Nour should prepare her for the test. This is where\nMiss Nour shines … the real benefit of the AI.\"\n\n- A plain, familiar **chat interface**: message list, text box, send. No\n  cleverness in the UI.\n- She states a need in her own words — \"I have a French test tomorrow.\"\n- Miss Nour **prepares her for it**: works out which lessons the test covers,\n  builds a plan, and runs the activities (teach, practise, reels, memorise,\n  review) — not just advice in a bubble.\n- It must know the student context (grade, school, curriculum track, today's\n  record, homework) and the real curriculum. `/api/chat` already accepts a\n  `schoolBrainContext` payload.\n- Voice should work here too, as everywhere (voice is first-class, text always\n  works when voice does not).\n\n**Important discovery — most of this already exists.** A full ChatGPT-style\nscreen is already written: `src/components/companion/CompanionChatScreen.tsx`\n(732 lines, message list, persistence, wired to `/api/chat`, intent handling\nfor \"don't understand\", \"explain differently\", \"test me\", fatigue, parent\noverride). **It is completely orphaned — nothing imports it.** The cheapest\ncorrect path is to review it, fix anything stale, and wire it to a bottom-bar\nitem. Do not write a second chat.\n\n---\n\n## 7. The opening experience\n\nOwner's words: \"after Miss Nour in first interaction at the beginning of the\nsession when [she] opens the app and they get up and get your daily feed\ntogether, this is how the app should work.\"\n\nOpening the app should feel like Miss Nour is there and they start the day\ntogether:\n\n1. **Miss Nour greets Amina by name** and states what today holds.\n2. **The daily feed is assembled with her** — today's learning items, drawn\n   from the real curriculum and Amina's actual state (due work, gaps, reviews).\n3. **A clear next action** — one obvious thing to start with, not a menu of\n   twelve.\n\nThis is the existing HOME + FEED pair, re-pointed so Miss Nour frames them\nrather than the screens standing alone.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Reuse map — what already exists\n\n**Read this before writing any new component.** Building a second version of\nanything here is a defect.\n\n| Need | Already exists |\n|------|----------------|\n| ChatGPT-style chat | `src/components/companion/CompanionChatScreen.tsx` — **orphaned, needs wiring** |\n| Daily feed | `src/components/feed/FeedScreen.tsx` (wired to `feed`) |\n| Miss Nour teaching UI | `src/components/teacher/VirtualTeacherClassroom.tsx` (2374 lines, wired to `companion`) |\n| Teaching session | `src/components/teaching/TeachingSessionModal.tsx` + `services/teaching/teachingSession.ts` |\n| Lesson detail (explain/vocab/exercises) | `src/components/curriculum/LessonStudyModal.tsx` |\n| Lesson real text + highlight-to-ask | `src/components/curriculum/LessonReader.tsx` |\n| Book reader / page images | `src/components/curriculum/BookReader.tsx` |\n| Book فهرس / real chapters | `src/components/curriculum/BookContentsView.tsx` + `services/content/bookCatalog.ts` |\n| Reels | `src/components/missions/ReelViewer.tsx` + `services/content/contentGenerator.ts` (demo concepts only) |\n| Tracing / writing canvas | `src/components/stage/interactions/TraceCanvas.tsx` |\n| Interactive stage activities | `src/components/stage/StageModal.tsx` + `services/stage/` + 10 interactions |\n| Quiz / practice | `src/components/missions/QuizRunner.tsx` |\n| Voice | `services/voice/voiceService.ts`, `VoiceInputControl`, `VoiceSpeakButton` |\n| Mastery / evidence | `services/mastery/masteryEngine.ts`, `recordEvidence` |\n| Spaced review | `services/review/` |\n| Real lesson text data | `content/curriculum/books/*/lessons.json` (434 lessons) |\n| Subject list | `curriculumService.getSubjectsSummary()` |\n\n## 9. What is genuinely new\n\n1. The **Subjects & Lessons section** (§3b) and its navigation.\n2. The **lesson activity menu** (§4) as a real choice screen.\n3. The **memorising session** (§4b) — repeat + write + recall + spaced review.\n4. **Reels driven by real lesson text** instead of hand-authored concepts (§4a).\n5. **Wiring the orphaned chat** into the bottom bar (§6).\n6. **Miss Nour's proactive presence** across screens (§5).\n7. The **rename** to Miss Nour (§0).\n\nEverything else is re-pointing existing work.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Open questions for the owner\n\n1. **\"One after the other\"** — should a lesson auto-advance to the next when\n   finished (continuous, like a series), or is it an ordered list she taps\n   through at her own pace?\n2. **The five image-only books** (`calligraphy-g5`, `islamic-g5-t2`,\n   `morals-g5-t1`, `morals-g5-t2`, `profskills-g5-t1`) have no text layer at\n   all. Show them in the new section as picture-only lessons, or leave them\n   out until vision quota is available? (Vision costs ~1 API call per page\n   against a 20/day free tier.)\n3. **Teaching depth for real chapters.** The teaching engine expects concepts,\n   objectives, key points and vocabulary — which exist only for the ~40\n   hand-written lessons. A teaching session on a real book chapter would run\n   from that chapter's real page text (genuine, but lighter). Do we ship broad\n   coverage now and enrich the most-used chapters later, or enrich first and\n   ship fewer lessons? *Recommended: ship broad, enrich in use.*\n\n---\n\n## 11. Non-negotiables carried forward\n\n- No rebuild from scratch. Re-point and extend.\n- No merging or deploying without explicit owner approval.\n- No fake curriculum, fake student identity, demo timetable, or unsupported\n  mastery claims.\n- No duplicate/parallel teacher, curriculum, feed, chat, saved-content, review,\n  or mastery systems.\n- Evidence before claims. Every \"done\" points to code and/or a test or runtime\n  result.\n- FEED remains a real requirement, not optional polish.\n- Keep token/cost use low: inspect first, targeted reads, consolidate edits per\n  file.\n- Where content is genuinely missing (image-only books, no school calendar),\n  expose a truthful state rather than substituting demo material.\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}

   "text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * Book catalog: maps a curriculum subject to the real ministry books that\n * belong to it, and exposes each book's own table of contents.\n *\n * Why this exists: the Library used to show a book's lesson list from the\n * *curriculum lesson registry*, which holds only a handful of hand-written\n * lessons per subject. Opening \"Arabic\" showed three lessons even though the\n * real Arabic textbook has thirty chapters. The rendered books were complete\n * the whole time — the UI was reading the wrong source.\n *\n * The manifest the renderer produces is the book's own فهرس: every unit and\n * every chapter with its printed page and image page. That is the source of\n * truth for \"what is in this book\", so that is what this module serves.\n *\n * Nothing here invents structure. If a manifest has no usable contents, the\n * caller is told so rather than shown a substitute.\n */\n\nimport {\n  listBooks,\n  getBookManifest,\n  type BookSummary,\n  type BookManifest,\n  type CurriculumUnit,\n} from './bookLibrary';\n\n/**\n * Canonical subject id -> the subject value the renderer wrote into each\n * manifest. Kept explicit rather than derived, so a mismatch is visible here\n * instead of silently producing an empty book list.\n */\nconst SUBJECT_TO_BOOK_SUBJECT: Record<string, string> = {\n  subj_arabic: 'arabic',\n  subj_french: 'french',\n  subj_math: 'math',\n  subj_science: 'science',\n  subj_social_studies: 'social',\n  subj_social: 'social',\n  subj_english: 'english',\n  subj_ict: 'ict',\n  subj_islamic: 'islamic',\n  subj_calligraphy: 'calligraphy',\n};\n\n/** A chapter as the book itself presents it. */\nexport interface BookChapter {\n  /** Stable id: book id + image page. */\n  id: string;\n  title: string;\n  /** Page number printed on the page, when the فهرس recorded one. */\n  printedPage: number | null;\n  /** Index into the book's page list, used to jump the reader. */\n  page: number;\n  unitName: string;\n  unitNumber: number;\n}\n\nexport interface BookContents {\n  bookId: string;\n  subject: string;\n  language: string;\n  term: number;\n  pages: number;\n  units: Array<{ name: string; chapters: BookChapter[] }>;\n  chapters: BookChapter[];\n  /**\n   * How the contents were obtained. 'toc' means the book's own فهرس was\n   * parsed; 'pages' means no contents were found and the book is still\n   * readable page by page.\n   */\n  contentsSource: 'toc' | 'pages';\n}\n\n/**\n * The renderer's text layer sometimes emits Arabic in visual order, which\n * leaves stray bracket fragments and doubled spaces. This is display cleanup\n * only — it never adds or changes words, so the title stays the book's own.\n */\nexport function cleanChapterTitle(raw: string): string {\n  return raw\n    .replace(/\\s+/g, ' ')\n    .replace(/^[\\s)\\](:.\\-–—]+/, '')\n    .replace(/[\\s([:.\\-–—]+$/, '')\n    .trim();\n}\n\nfunction toChapter(\n  bookId: string,\n  unitName: string,\n  unitNumber: number,\n  lesson: { title: string; printedPage?: number | null; page?: number | null },\n): BookChapter | null {\n  // A chapter with no resolvable page cannot be opened, so it is not offered.\n  if (typeof lesson.page !== 'number') return null;\n  const title = cleanChapterTitle(lesson.title || '');\n  if (!title) return null;\n  return {\n    id: `${bookId}:${lesson.page}`,\n    title,\n    printedPage: typeof lesson.printedPage === 'number' ? lesson.printedPage : null,\n    page: lesson.page,\n    unitName,\n    unitNumber,\n  };\n}\n\n/** Build the readable contents of a book from its manifest. */\nexport function buildBookContents(manifest: BookManifest): BookContents {\n  const units: BookContents['units'] = [];\n  const all: BookChapter[] = [];\n\n  (manifest.units ?? []).forEach((u: CurriculumUnit, idx: number) => {\n    const unitName = cleanChapterTitle(u.unit || '') || `الوحدة ${idx + 1}`;\n    const chapters = (u.lessons ?? [])\n      .map((l) => toChapter(manifest.id, unitName, idx + 1, l))\n      .filter((c): c is BookChapter => c !== null);\n\n    if (chapters.length > 0) {\n      units.push({ name: unitName, chapters });\n      all.push(...chapters);\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Chapters must be in the order the book is bound in, regardless of how the\n  // فهرس was laid out on the page.\n  all.sort((a, b) => a.page - b.page);\n\n=== bookLibrary exports ===\n16:export interface BookSummary {\n27:export interface BookPage {\n35:export interface CurriculumUnit {\n40:export interface BookManifest extends Omit<BookSummary, 'unitCount'> {\n60:export function listBooks(): Promise<BookSummary[]> {\n65:export function getBookManifest(bookId: string): Promise<BookManifest> {\n70:export function pageUrl(bookId: string, file: string): string {\n75:export interface LessonText {\n89:export type BookLessons = Record<string, LessonText>;\n99:export async function getBookLessons(bookId: string): Promise<BookLessons> {\n119:export async function requestPersistentStorage(): Promise<boolean> {\n129:export interface StorageStatus {\n135:export async function storageStatus(): Promise<StorageStatus | null> {\n149:export interface DownloadProgress {\n161:export async function downloadBook(\n187:export function downloadedBookIds(): string[] {\n195:export function markDownloaded(bookId: string): void {"

'toc' : 'pages',\n  };\n}\n\n/** Every book that belongs to a subject, term-ordered. */\nexport async function booksForSubject(\n  subjectId: string,\n  language?: string,\n): Promise<BookSummary[]> {\n  const bookSubject = SUBJECT_TO_BOOK_SUBJECT[subjectId];\n  if (!bookSubject) return [];\n\n  const books = (await listBooks()).filter((b) => b.subject === bookSubject);\n  // Prefer the student's language when a subject has both, but never hide the\n  // other edition: a French-track student still needs the Arabic textbook.\n  const preferred = language\n    ? books.filter((b) => b.language === language)\n    : [];\n  const ordered = (preferred.length > 0 ? preferred : books)\n    .slice()\n    .sort((a, b) => a.term - b.term);\n  return ordered.length > 0 ? ordered : books.slice().sort((a, b) => a.term - b.term);\n}\n\n/** All editions of a subject (both terms, both languages) for a term picker. */\nexport async function allBooksForSubject(subjectId: string): Promise<BookSummary[]> {\n  const bookSubject = SUBJECT_TO_BOOK_SUBJECT[subjectId];\n  if (!bookSubject) return [];\n  return (await listBooks())\n    .filter((b) => b.subject === bookSubject)\n    .sort((a, b) => a.term - b.term || a.language.localeCompare(b.language));\n}\n\n/** Fetch and build one book's contents. */\nexport async function getBookContents(bookId: string): Promise<BookContents> {\n  return buildBookContents(await getBookManifest(bookId));\n}"

 "file_text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * Subject curriculum sequence — every lesson of a subject, in one list.\n *\n * The girl picks a subject (Arabic, French, Maths…) and needs to see the whole\n * year for it: lesson one, lesson two, lesson three…, the real ones, in the\n * order the book binds them. From a lesson she then chooses what to do.\n *\n * Why this is not just the book contents: a subject has two terms, and often\n * two editions (Arabic and English Maths). She thinks in subjects, not in\n * volumes. This module stitches a subject's books into one continuous\n * sequence, and records which book each lesson came from so the activity menu\n * can still open the right pages.\n *\n * Source of truth is the book's own فهرس, read through bookCatalog. Nothing is\n * invented: a book whose فهرس could not be read contributes no lessons and\n * says so, rather than showing a substitute list.\n */\n\nimport {\n  allBooksForSubject,\n  getBookContents,\n  type BookChapter,\n} from './bookCatalog';\nimport type { BookSummary } from './bookLibrary';\n\n/** One lesson in a subject's sequence, with the book it belongs to. */\nexport interface SubjectLesson {\n  /** Stable across the whole sequence: bookId + image page. */\n  id: string;\n  bookId: string;\n  bookTitle: string;\n  term: number;\n  language: string;\n  /** 1-based position in the subject's whole sequence. */\n  sequenceNumber: number;\n  /** The lesson number within its own book, as printed. */\n  lessonNumber: number;\n  title: string;\n  unitName: string;\n  unitNumber: number;\n  page: number;\n  printedPage: number | null;\n}\n\n/** A book that could not supply lessons, and why. */\nexport interface SubjectBookGap {\n  bookId: string;\n  bookTitle: string;\n  term: number;\n  language: string;\n  reason: 'no_toc' | 'no_pages';\n}\n\nexport interface SubjectCurriculum {\n  subjectId: string;\n  lessons: SubjectLesson[];\n  /** Term-grouped view, for showing the sequence split by term. */\n  terms: Array<{ term: number; lessons: SubjectLesson[] }>;\n  /** Books that contributed lessons, in the order they appear. */\n  books: BookSummary[];\n  /** Books that contributed nothing, so the UI can be honest about them. */\n  gaps: SubjectBookGap[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Build one subject's continuous lesson sequence across all its books.\n *\n * Order: term first, then language (the student's own edition before the other\n * edition of the same subject), then the book's own binding order. Numbering\n * runs continuously across books so the girl sees one sequence, not two.\n */\nexport async function getSubjectCurriculum(\n  subjectId: string,\n  options: { language?: string } = {},\n): Promise<SubjectCurriculum> {\n  const books = await allBooksForSubject(subjectId);\n  if (books.length === 0) {\n    return { subjectId, lessons: [], terms: [], books: [], gaps: [] };\n  }\n\n  const preferred = options.language;\n  const ordered = books.slice().sort((a, b) => {\n    if (a.term !== b.term) return a.term - b.term;\n    if (preferred) {\n      const aPref = a.language === preferred ? 0 : 1;\n      const bPref = b.language === preferred ? 0 : 1;\n      if (aPref !== bPref) return aPref - bPref;\n    }\n    return a.language.localeCompare(b.language);\n  });\n\n  const lessons: SubjectLesson[] = [];\n  const gaps: SubjectBookGap[] = [];\n  const contributing: BookSummary[] = [];\n\n  for (const book of ordered) {\n    const contents = await getBookContents(book.id);\n    if (contents.chapters.length === 0) {\n      gaps.push({\n        bookId: book.id,\n        bookTitle: book.title,\n        term: book.term,\n        language: book.language,\n        reason: contents.pages > 0 ? 'no_toc' : 'no_pages',\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n    contributing.push(book);\n    contents.chapters.forEach((chapter: BookChapter, index: number) => {\n      lessons.push({\n        id: `${chapter.id}`,\n        bookId: book.id,\n        bookTitle: book.title,\n        term: book.term,\n        language: book.language,\n        sequenceNumber: lessons.length + 1,\n        lessonNumber: index + 1,\n        title: chapter.title,\n        unitName: chapter.unitName,\n        unitNumber: chapter.unitNumber,\n        page: chapter.page,\n        printedPage: chapter.printedPage,\n      });\n    });\n  }\n\n  // Re-number after stitching so the sequence is continuous even when a book\n  // in the middle contributed nothing.\n  lessons.forEach((l, i) => {\n    l.sequenceNumber = i + 1;\n  });\n\n  const termNumbers = Array.from(new Set(lessons.map((l) => l.term))).sort(\n    (a, b) => a - b,\n  );\n  const terms = termNumbers.map((term) => ({\n    term,\n    lessons: lessons.filter((l) => l.term === term),\n  }));\n\n  return { subjectId, lessons, terms, books: contributing, gaps };\n}\n\n/**\n * Total lesson count per subject, for the subject list. Reads only manifests,\n * so it stays cheap enough to call for every subject on one screen.\n */\nexport async function getSubjectLessonCounts(\n  subjectIds: string[],\n  options: { language?: string } = {},\n): Promise<Record<string, number>> {\n  const entries = await Promise.all(\n    subjectIds.map(async (id) => {\n      const { lessons } = await getSubjectCurriculum(id, options);\n      return [id, lessons.length] as const;\n    }),\n  );\n  return Object.fromEntries(entries);\n}\n",

### ActionEvent — tool: `file_editor` — source: `agent` — id: `8f3067cc-c655-41f2-aa0c-76ae52e0f8aa` — 2026-10-21T22:15:21.890855

```
{
 "command": "create",
 "path": "/workspace/project/Amina/src/services/__tests__/subjectCurriculum.test.ts",
 "file_text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * The subject lesson sequence must show the girl her real curriculum.\n *\n * The bug this guards against: the Library used to list lessons from the\n * hand-written curriculum registry, which holds a few dozen lessons for a\n * whole Grade 5 year. The real books have hundreds. These tests read the real\n * rendered manifests from disk, so they fail if the sequence ever silently\n * falls back to a demo-sized list.\n */\n\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';\nimport fs from 'fs';\nimport path from 'path';\n\nconst BOOKS_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../../content/curriculum/books');\n\ninterface Unit {\n  unit: string;\n  lessons: Array<{ title: string; page: number | null; printedPage?: number | null }>;\n}\ninterface Manifest {\n  id: string;\n  subject: string;\n  term: number;\n  language: string;\n  pages: number;\n  units?: Unit[];\n  structureStatus?: string;\n}\n\nfunction loadManifest(bookId: string): Manifest | null {\n  const f = path.join(BOOKS_DIR, bookId, 'manifest.json');\n  if (!fs.existsSync(f)) return null;\n  return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8')) as Manifest;\n}\n\nfunction chapterCount(m: Manifest): number {\n  return (m.units ?? []).reduce(\n    (n, u) => n + (u.lessons ?? []).filter((l) => typeof l.page === 'number').length,\n    0,\n  );\n}\n\ndescribe('subject lesson sequence reads the real books', () => {\n  it('arabic has a full year of lessons across its two books, not a demo handful', () => {\n    const t1 = loadManifest('arabic-g5-t1');\n    const t2 = loadManifest('arabic-g5-t2');\n    expect(t1, 'arabic-g5-t1 manifest must exist').not.toBeNull();\n    expect(t2, 'arabic-g5-t2 manifest must exist').not.toBeNull();\n\n    const total = chapterCount(t1!) + chapterCount(t2!);\n    // The old registry exposed ~3 Arabic lessons. The real books have many more.\n    expect(total, `Arabic sequence must be the real book contents (${total})`).toBeGreaterThan(25);\n  });\n\n  it('a stitched subject sequence is continuous and ordered by book page', () => {\n    const t1 = loadManifest('arabic-g5-t1')!;\n    const t2 = loadManifest('arabic-g5-t2')!;\n\n    const seq: Array<{ book: string; page: number }> = [];\n    for (const m of [t1, t2]) {\n      for (const u of m.units ?? []) {\n        for (const l of u.lessons ?? []) {\n          if (typeof l.page === 'number') seq.push({ book: m.id, page: l.page });\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    expect(seq.length).toBeGreaterThan(25);\n\n    // Within a book, pages must ascend: that is the binding order.\n    const t1Pages = seq.filter((s) => s.book === 'arabic-g5-t1').map((s) => s.page);\n    for (let i = 1; i < t1Pages.length; i++) {\n      expect(t1Pages[i]).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(t1Pages[i - 1]);\n    }\n  });\n\n  it('every subject the girl studies maps to at least one real book', () => {\n    const map: Record<string, string> = {\n      subj_arabic: 'arabic',\n      subj_math: 'math',\n      subj_science: 'science',\n      subj_english: 'english',\n      subj_ict: 'ict',\n      subj_social_studies: 'social',\n      subj_islamic: 'islamic',\n    };\n    const manifests = fs\n      .readdirSync(BOOKS_DIR)\n      .filter((d) => fs.existsSync(path.join(BOOKS_DIR, d, 'manifest.json')))\n      .map((d) => loadManifest(d)!);\n\n    for (const [subjectId, bookSubject] of Object.entries(map)) {\n      const found = manifests.filter((m) => m.subject === bookSubject);\n      expect(found.length, `${subjectId} must have real books`).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n    }\n  });\n\n  it('books whose فهرس could not be read are reported as gaps, not faked', () => {\n    const manifests = fs\n      .readdirSync(BOOKS_DIR)\n      .filter((d) => fs.existsSync(path.join(BOOKS_DIR, d, 'manifest.json')))\n      .map((d) => loadManifest(d)!);\n\n    const noToc = manifests.filter((m) => chapterCount(m) === 0);\n    for (const m of noToc) {\n      // A book with no readable contents must be flagged, so the UI can say so.\n      expect(\n        m.structureStatus,\n        `${m.id} has no chapters and must report a structure status`,\n      ).toBeTruthy();\n      expect(m.structureStatus).not.toBe('ok');\n    }\n  });\n});\n",
 "old_str": null,
 "new_str": null,
 "insert_line": null,
 "view_range": null,
 "kind": "FileEditorAction"
}

{
 "command": "create",
 "path": "/workspace/project/Amina/src/services/__tests__/subjectCurriculum.test.ts",
 "file_text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * Tests for the subject lesson sequence.\n *\n * The bug this guards against: the Library used to list lessons from the\n * hand-written curriculum registry, which holds a few dozen lessons for a whole\n * Grade 5 year, so opening \"Arabic\" showed three lessons. The real books have\n * hundreds. These tests read the real rendered manifests from disk, so they\n * fail if the sequence ever silently falls back to a demo-sized list.\n */\n\nimport * as fs from 'fs';\nimport * as path from 'path';\nimport { bookLabel } from '../content/subjectCurriculum';\nimport type { BookManifest } from '../content/bookLibrary';\n\nlet passed = 0;\nlet failed = 0;\n\nfunction assert(condition: boolean, message: string) {\n  if (condition) {\n    console.log(`✅ [PASS] ${message}`);\n    passed++;\n  } else {\n    console.error(`❌ [FAIL] ${message}`);\n    failed++;\n  }\n}\n\nconst BOOKS_ROOT = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'content/curriculum/books');\n\nfunction loadManifest(bookId: string): BookManifest | null {\n  const p = path.join(BOOKS_ROOT, bookId, 'manifest.json');\n  if (!fs.existsSync(p)) return null;\n  return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8')) as BookManifest;\n}\n\nfunction chapterCount(m: BookManifest): number {\n  return (m.units ?? []).reduce(\n    (n, u) => n + (u.lessons ?? []).filter((l) => typeof l.page === 'number').length,\n    0,\n  );\n}\n\n/** The subject -> book-subject mapping the sequence relies on. */\nconst SUBJECT_MAP: Record<string, string> = {\n  subj_arabic: 'arabic',\n  subj_math: 'math',\n  subj_science: 'science',\n  subj_english: 'english',\n  subj_ict: 'ict',\n  subj_social_studies: 'social',\n  subj_islamic: 'islamic',\n  subj_christian: 'christian',\n  subj_calligraphy: 'calligraphy',\n  subj_morals: 'morals',\n  subj_profskills: 'profskills',\n};\n\nfunction runSequenceTests() {\n  console.log('--- SUBJECT LESSON SEQUENCE ---\\n');\n\n  const ids = fs.existsSync(BOOKS_ROOT)\n    ? fs.readdirSync(BOOKS_ROOT).filter((d) =>\n        fs.existsSync(path.join(BOOKS_ROOT, d, 'manifest.json')),\n      )\n    : [];\n  const manifests = ids.map((id) => loadManifest(id)!).filter(Boolean);\n\n  assert(manifests.length > 0, `rendered books are present on disk (${manifests.length})`);\n\n  // 1. Arabic must be a full year, not the demo handful the old registry had.\n  const arabic = ['arabic-g5-t1', 'arabic-g5-t2']\n    .map(loadManifest)\n    .filter((m): m is BookManifest => m !== null);\n  assert(arabic.length === 2, 'Arabic has both term books rendered');\n  const arabicChapters = arabic.reduce((n, m) => n + chapterCount(m), 0);\n  assert(\n    arabicChapters > 25,\n    `Arabic exposes the real book contents, not a demo list (${arabicChapters} lessons)`,\n  );\n\n  // 2. A stitched sequence stays in the book's binding order.\n  const t1 = loadManifest('arabic-g5-t1');\n  if (t1) {\n    const pages = (t1.units ?? [])\n      .flatMap((u) => u.lessons ?? [])\n      .filter((l) => typeof l.page === 'number')\n      .map((l) => l.page as number);\n    let ascending = true;\n    for (let i = 1; i < pages.length; i++) {\n      if (pages[i] < pages[i - 1]) ascending = false;\n    }\n    assert(ascending, `Arabic term 1 lessons ascend in page order (${pages.length} lessons)`);\n  }\n\n  // 3. Every subject the girl studies resolves to at least one real book.\n  for (const [subjectId, bookSubject] of Object.entries(SUBJECT_MAP)) {\n    const found = manifests.filter((m) => m.subject === bookSubject);\n    if (found.length === 0) {\n      console.log(`ℹ️  [SKIP] ${subjectId}: no rendered book for subject \"${bookSubject}\"`);\n      continue;\n    }\n    const chapters = found.reduce((n, m) => n + chapterCount(m), 0);\n    assert(\n      chapters > 0 || found.every((m) => m.structureStatus === 'not_found'),\n      `${subjectId} has real lessons or is honestly flagged as unreadable (${chapters})`,\n    );\n  }\n\n  // 4. A book with no readable contents must be flagged, so the UI can say so\n  //    rather than showing an empty or invented list.\n  for (const m of manifests) {\n    if (chapterCount(m) === 0) {\n      assert(\n        m.structureStatus !== 'ok' && !!m.structureStatus,\n        `${m.id} has no chapters and reports a truthful structureStatus (${m.structureStatus})`,\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 5. Book labels must be distinguishable, since a manifest carries no title.\n  const labelA = bookLabel({ subject: 'arabic', term: 1, language: 'ar' }, 'ar');\n  const labelB = bookLabel({ subject: 'arabic', term: 2, language: 'ar' }, 'ar');\n  assert(labelA !== labelB, `term 1 and term 2 books are distinguishable (\"${labelA}\" vs \"${labelB}\")`);\n  assert(\n    labelA.includes('1') && labelB.includes('2'),\n    'the term number appears in the book label',\n  );\n}\n\nfunction main() {\n  runSequenceTests();\n  console.log(`\\n=== SUBJECT SEQUENCE: ${passed} passed, ${failed} failed ===`);\n  if (failed > 0) process.exit(1);\n}\n\nmain();\n",
 "old_str": null,
 "new_str": null,
 "insert_line": null,
 "view_range": null,
 "kind": "FileEditorAction"
}

## Your phone link — it's fixed

**The app wasn't broken. Both servers were down.** That's the whole reason the link wouldn't open — nothing to do with the code. I rebuilt and restarted them.

**Your link:**
```
https://work-1-xplvxvupzdnrwwrz.prod-runtime.all-hands.dev/
```

Verified working right now:
- Homepage: 200
- API key loaded (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `hasApiKey: true`)
- **Real AI confirmed live** — I sent a Maths question about fractions and Miss Nour answered in Arabic with a pizza analogy
- Curriculum index: 24 books
- Book page images: 200, real WEBP

**One thing to know:** the sandbox restarts the servers when the session ends. If the link stops opening again, tell me and I'll restart it — it's a 10-second fix, not a code problem.

**Note:** what's on the link now is everything built so far. The new Subjects & Lessons section is *not* on it yet — the service is built and tested, but I haven't built the screens. I'll be honest about that rather than let you go looking for something that isn't there.

## What I built this session

**The subject lesson sequence** (`subjectCurriculum.ts`) — the engine for your new section. It stitches a subject's books into one continuous lesson list. Real counts, from the actual books:

| Subject | Lessons |
|---|---|
| Science | 155 |
| Maths | 101 |
| English | 87 |
| Arabic | 54 |
| Social Studies | 38 |
| ICT | 31 |
| Islamic | 28 |
| Christian | 20 |

That's against the **~40 hand-written lessons** the old library showed for the entire year. That was your "book library is broken" bug, and this is the fix underneath it.

Where a book's فهرس can't be read, the service returns it as a **gap with a reason** rather than a short or invented list — so calligraphy and the three scanned books surface honestly.

**22 tests pass**, following the repo's own convention. Worth noting: **vitest hangs in this project** — it uses plain `tsx` scripts instead. I matched the existing pattern rather than fight it.

## Sport is now locked in properly

You said something important: Amina is a **Republic champion gymnast** with a real sporting career. I'd originally filed sport as a checkbox in the parent report. That was too small, and I've rewritten it as **§9b — a first-class bottom-bar section**.

The principle you set: *Miss Nour handles the sporting career the way she handles the school career.* So it reuses the same machinery rather than inventing a parallel system:

| School | Sport |
|---|---|
| Concepts | Skills and routines |
| Homework | Training |
| Exams | Competitions |
| Study plan | Training plan |

**And the part I think matters most:** both calendars are visible to her together. A competition week and an exam week is a real collision for a child doing both at national level. Miss Nour should see it and say so.

I also flagged honestly: there's **no sport data in the app**, so it needs a real source — you or Amina logging it. I won't seed a fake career or a fake score.

## Two things still open

1. **How much sport detail do you want to log by hand?** A competition result is one entry; a full training diary is a habit. I'd start with profile + competition record + current skills.
2. **Calligraphy** — you said forget it, so I have. Flagging only that it has 39,198 characters of readable text sitting unused, so it's a cheap fix whenever you want it.

Next I'll build the actual screens for the new section — subject list → lesson sequence → activity chooser.

 "file_text": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n *\n * Memorising session — repeat it, write it, recall it.\n *\n * The girl picks a lesson and chooses \"memorise\". Miss Nour breaks the lesson's\n * real text into short pieces and works through them one at a time:\n *\n *   1. Listen  — the piece is read aloud.\n *   2. Repeat  — she says it back, or reads it again with the voice.\n *   3. Write   — the piece is hidden and she writes it from memory.\n *   4. Recall  — what she wrote is compared with the book's own words.\n *\n * The text is the book's own, never a paraphrase, so what she memorises is what\n * the book prints. Anything she struggles with is what the review scheduler\n * should see later, so the result is reported back as a real score.\n */\n\nimport React, { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';\nimport { voiceService } from '../../services/voice/voiceService';\nimport {\n  Check,\n  RotateCcw,\n  Volume2,\n  Eye,\n  EyeOff,\n  ArrowRight,\n  ArrowLeft,\n  Sparkles,\n  Trophy,\n} from 'lucide-react';\n\ninterface Props {\n  lessonTitle: string;\n  lessonText: string;\n  language: string;\n  isAr: boolean;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Reported once, at the end, with how much she recalled (0..1). */\n  onComplete: (recallScore: number) => void;\n}\n\ntype Stage = 'listen' | 'write' | 'compare' | 'done';\n\nconst COPY = {\n  ar: {\n    title: 'جلسة تحفيظ',\n    piece: 'المقطع',\n    of: 'من',\n    listen: 'اسمعي المقطع كويس',\n    hearIt: 'اسمعيه',\n    repeat: 'كرري معايا بصوت عالي',\n    ready: 'جاهزة أكتبه؟',\n    write: 'اكتبيه من ذاكرتك',\n    placeholder: 'اكتبي المقطع هنا…',\n    check: 'صحّحي إجابتي',\n    yourAnswer: 'اللي كتبتيه',\n    theBook: 'كلام الكتاب',\n    correct: 'ما شاء الله! كتبتيه صح',\n    close: 'قريبة جداً، شوفي الفرق',\n    missed: 'تعالي نقراه سوا تاني',\n    again: 'جرّبي تاني',\n    next: 'المقطع اللي بعده',\n    finish: 'خلصنا',\n    doneTitle: 'خلصتي جلسة التحفيظ',\n    doneBody: 'حفظنا',\n    pieces: 'مقاطع',\n    accuracy: 'دقة الحفظ',\n    retryAll: 'أعيدي الجلسة',\n    closeBtn: 'إغلاق',\n    noText: 'الدرس ده مش فيه نص محفوظ.',\n    reveal: 'وريني',\n    hide: 'خبّي',\n  },\n  en: {\n    title: 'Memorising session',\n    piece: 'Piece',\n    of: 'of',\n    listen: 'Listen to the piece carefully',\n    hearIt: 'Hear it',\n    repeat: 'Repeat it out loud',\n    ready: 'Ready to write it?',\n    write: 'Write it from memory',\n    placeholder: 'Write the piece here…',\n    check: 'Check my answer',\n    yourAnswer: 'You wrote',\n    theBook: 'The book says',\n    correct: 'Well done! That matches',\n    close: 'Very close — see the difference',\n    missed: \"Let's read it together again\",\n    again: 'Try again',\n    next: 'Next piece',\n    finish: 'Finish',\n    doneTitle: 'Memorising session complete',\n    doneBody: 'We memorised',\n    pieces: 'pieces',\n    accuracy: 'Recall accuracy',\n    retryAll: 'Restart the session',\n    closeBtn: 'Close',\n    noText: 'This lesson has no memorisable text.',\n    reveal: 'Show',\n    hide: 'Hide',\n  },\n} as const;\n\n/** Arabic diacritics and tatweel carry no meaning for a recall comparison. */\nfunction normalise(s: string): string {\n  return s\n    .replace(/[\\u064B-\\u065F\\u0670\\u06D6-\\u06ED]/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\u0640/g, '')\n    .replace(/[أإآٱ]/g, 'ا')\n    .replace(/ى/g, 'ي')\n    .replace(/ؤ/g, 'و')\n    .replace(/ئ/g, 'ي')\n    .replace(/ة/g, 'ه')\n    .replace(/[^\\p{L}\\p{N}\\s]/gu, '')\n    .replace(/\\s+/g, ' ')\n    .trim()\n    .toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/** How much of the piece she recalled, by word overlap. */\nfunction recallRatio(attempt: string, target: string): number {\n  const want = normalise(target).split(' ').filter(Boolean);\n  const got = new Set(normalise(attempt).split(' ').filter(Boolean));\n  if (want.length === 0) return 0;\n  const hit = want.filter((w) => got.has(w)).length;\n  return hit / want.length;\n}\n\n/**\n * Break the lesson into memorisable pieces. Lines are the natural unit: a verse\n * line, a definition, a vocabulary row. Very short fragments are joined to the\n * next line so she is never asked to memorise two words on their own.\n */\nexport function buildPieces(text: string, maxPieces = 12): string[] {\n  const lines = text\n    .split(/\\n+/)\n    .map((l) => l.trim())\n    .filter((l) => l.length > 0);\n\n  const pieces: string[] = [];\n  let buffer = '';\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    // A long paragraph is a piece on its own; short lines accumulate.\n    if (line.length >= 60) {\n      if (buffer) {\n        pieces.push(buffer);\n        buffer = '';\n      }\n      pieces.push(line);\n    } else {\n      buffer = buffer ? `${buffer} ${line}` : line;\n      if (buffer.length >= 60) {\n        pieces.push(buffer);\n        buffer = '';\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (buffer) pieces.push(buffer);\n\n  // Keep a session to a sensible length, and keep each piece readable.\n  return pieces.slice(0, maxPieces).map((p) => (p.length > 300 ? p.slice(0, 300).trim() : p));\n}\n\nexport const MemorizeSession: React.FC<Props> = ({\n  lessonTitle,\n  lessonText,\n  language,\n  isAr,\n  onClose,\n  onComplete,\n}) => {\n  const t = isAr ? COPY.ar : COPY.en;\n  const pieces = useMemo(() => buildPieces(lessonText), [lessonText]);\n\n  const [index, setIndex] = useState(0);\n  const [stage, setStage] = useState<Stage>('listen');\n  const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState('');\n  const [showTarget, setShowTarget] = useState(false);\n  const [results, setResults] = useState<number[]>([]);\n  const [lastRatio, setLastRatio] = useState(0);\n\n  const piece = pieces[index] || '';\n\n  useEffect(() => () => voiceService.cancelSpeech(), []);\n\n  const hearIt = useCallback(() => {\n    if (!piece) return;\n    voiceService.cancelSpeech();\n    voiceService.speak(piece, language as 'ar' | 'en' | 'fr');\n  }, [piece, language]);\n\n  const goNext = useCallback(\n    (ratio: number) => {\n      const next = [...results, ratio];\n      setResults(next);\n      if (index + 1 >= pieces.length) {\n        const avg = next.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / Math.max(next.length, 1);\n        setStage('done');\n        onComplete(avg);\n      } else {\n        setIndex(index + 1);\n        setStage('listen');\n        setAttempt('');\n        setShowTarget(false);\n      }\n    },\n    [index, pieces.length, results, onComplete],\n  );\n\n  const check = useCallback(() => {\n    const ratio = recallRatio(attempt, piece);\n    setLastRatio(ratio);\n    setStage('compare');\n  }, [attempt, piece]);\n\n  if (pieces.length === 0) {\n    return (\n      <div className=\"fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-slate-50 flex flex-col items-center justify-center p-6\" dir={isAr ? (\n          <>\n            <div className=\"rounded-2xl bg-white border border-slate-200 p-5 space-y-2\">\n              <p className=\"text-xs font-bold text-indigo-600\">{t.write}</p>\n              <textarea\n                value={attempt}\n                onChange={(e) => setAttempt(e.target.value)}\n                placeholder={t.placeholder}\n                rows={5}\n                autoFocus\n                dir=\"auto\"\n                className=\"w-full px-3 py-2 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 text-[17px] leading-loose text-slate-800 resize-y\"\n              />\n            </div>\n            <div className=\"flex gap-2\">\n              <button\n                onClick={() => setShowTarget((v) => !v)}\n                className=\"px-3 py-3 rounded-xl bg-slate-100 text-slate-700 text-sm font-semibold inline-flex items-center gap-1.5\"\n              >\n                {showTarget ? <EyeOff className=\"w-4 h-4\" /> : <Eye className=\"w-4 h-4\" />}\n                {showTarget ? t.hide : t.reveal}\n              </button>\n              <button\n                onClick={check}\n                disabled={!attempt.trim()}\n                className=\"flex-1 py-3 rounded-xl bg-emerald-600 text-white text-sm font-bold disabled:opacity-40 inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-2\"\n              >\n                <Check className=\"w-4 h-4\" />\n                {t.check}\n              </button>\n            </div>\n            {showTarget && (\n              <div className=\"rounded-2xl bg-slate-100 border border-slate-200 p-4\">\n                <p className=\"text-xs font-bold text-slate-500 mb-1\">{t.theBook}</p>\n                <p className=\"text-[17px] leading-loose text-slate-800\">{piece}</p>\n              </div>\n            )}\n          </>\n        ) : (\n          <>\n            <div\n              className={`rounded-2xl p-4 border ${\n                lastRatio >= 0.9\n                  ? <AlertTriangle className=\"w-3 h-3\" />\n            {t.gapTitle}\n          </p>\n          {curriculum.gaps.map((g) => (\n            <p key={g.bookId} className=\"text-[10px] text-slate-500
